A neutron polarization exceeding 80% was achieved for epithermal neutrons with energies below 1 eV, including a polarization of 86.4 $\pm$ 0.5% for 0.75 eV neutrons, which corresponds to the resonance energy of the p-wave compound state in the 139La+n system. The spin filter consisted of a 20-cm-long, 3.2-atm 3He gas cell polarized on the beamline using a compact laser-optics system for spin-exchange optical pumping (SEOP). A 3He polarization of approximately 78% was stably maintained on the beamline for more than 100 hours. The polarized epithermal neutron beam developed in this work provides a powerful tool for studies of discrete symmetry violations, including measurements of enhanced parity violation in neutron absorption by medium-heavy nuclei such as 139La and searches for time-reversal symmetry violation in neutron-nucleus systems.

title: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning
abstract: Multi-modal fusion algorithms combining conventional frame-based cameras and event cameras have recently attracted substantial research attention. Typically, existing approaches convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, and then learn the required spatiotemporal information from these transformed event representations for fusion with conventional frame-camera data. Obviously, such paradigms only exploit the limited representational capacity of event data. Moreover, standard training pipelines fail to fully leverage diverse model parameters obtained throughout the learning process. In this paper, we propose a novel mutual distillation method leveraging multi-view teacher network weights to better integrate multiple event representations and achieve model-parameter level fusion. Specifically, we employ multiple encoders to extract different types of event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at both the feature-level and logit-level in this process. Afterwards, we perform a dynamic hierarchical model merge strategy on the model parameters from the first stage to yield a unified multi-modal RGB-Event representation model. Experimental results across multiple event-based datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements.

title: Inverse modelling of a laser-plasma accelerator
abstract: The electron beams of a laser-plasma accelerator depend non-linearly on the laser and gas settings. This dependence is explored using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, and machine-learning models trained on these simulations predict the beam from the settings. Here we address the reverse problem: given a measured beam, which settings produced it? We infer three of them: the gas pressure $p\_1$, the normalised vector potential $a\_0$ and the nitrogen concentration $c\_{N\_2}$. The solution is not guaranteed to be unique. We train an ensemble of mixture density networks that, for each beam, output several possible sets of settings with their probabilities and uncertainties, and test them on simulated beams with realistic measurement noise. On average, the predictions are accurate ($R^2 = 0.91$), yet for about two-thirds of the beams the inferred distribution has two competing solutions. These share nearly the same value of $a\_0^2 p\_1$, which controls how strongly the laser focuses itself in the plasma and, in earlier PALLAS studies, when electrons start to be injected. Keeping this quantity fixed gives beams that are practically indistinguishable with realistic diagnostics. A forward model used as a check removes unphysical solutions but cannot choose between the two plausible ones. We then test two ways to resolve the ambiguity. Adding the full electron energy spectrum improves the mean prediction ($R^2 = 0.94$), mostly through $a\_0$. It changes the weights of the two solutions but does not move them. A second measurement at a deliberately different plasma density is more effective. In paired PIC simulations, it reduces the error on $a\_0$ by a factor of 2.6, whereas repeating the measurement at the same density brings almost no gain.

title: Classification of three-dimensional Leibniz dialgebras with two-dimensional annihilator
abstract: A Leibniz dialgebra is a vector space with two bilinear products $\dashv$ and $\vdash$ satisfying the dialgebra analogue of the right Leibniz identity. This notion is obtained by the same standard procedure that turns the associative identity into the axioms of Loday's associative dialgebras. In particular, $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is a right Leibniz algebra, so a Leibniz dialgebra is a Leibniz algebra together with a second, compatible product. This paper recalls the definition of Leibniz dialgebras and continue the algebraic classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz dialgebras. This paper describes up to isomorphism all Leibniz dialgebras $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv,\vdash)$ for which the Leibniz algebra $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is isomorphic to one of the algebras $\mathcal{L}_{8}(α)$, $\mathcal{L}_9$, $\mathcal{L}_{10}$, $\mathcal{L}_{11}$ of the classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz algebras. The result consists 18 families of pairwise non-isomorphic Leibniz dialgebras, nine of which depend on a complex parameter.

title: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting
abstract: Curves and interfaces play a central role in computer vision and image processing, and Euler's elastica energy is one of the most successful tools to model and manipulate them. The elastica energy is usually computed through a level-set or a phase field representation of the curve, in which the curvature term makes the energy nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, so that its minimization is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we propose a new formulation of the elastica model based on a binary representation of curves. The key ingredient is a very simple formula for the curvature: if $ϕ$ is the $\pm1$ binary function associated with a curve $Γ$, then along $Γ$ the curvature is given by $-\frac{1}{C_0ε}\left(R_ε*ϕ\right)+O(ε)$, where $R_ε$ is a radial kernel supported in a ball of radius $ε$ and $C_0$ is an explicit constant. No derivative of $ϕ$ is involved and the convolution is evaluated by FFT. The resulting energy is a weighted total variation, so that formally the new formulation is a generalization of the well-known ROF model; a phase field type model is obtained from the same curvature formula. Combining FFT with the split Bregman iteration, which for the present problem coincides with an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), we obtain efficient algorithms whose subproblems are either linear systems solved by conjugate gradient or explicit pointwise formulas. Numerical experiments on the inpainting of binary images are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

title: SpatialVec: A Unified Representation Learning Framework for Geospatial Objects with Boundary-Aware Sampling
abstract: Spatial representation learning is essential for Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) applications, enabling machine learning models to capture the geometry, location, and spatial relationships of geographic entities such as points, polylines, and polygons. Existing spatial encoding methods often struggle to preserve fine-grained topological information, particularly for interactions involving complex geometries such as polylines and polygons. These approaches inadequately capture boundary structure and local spatial context, causing topology-sensitive relationships near geometry boundaries to be underrepresented in the learned embedding space. Consequently, accurately modeling complex spatial interactions remains a significant challenge for downstream spatial reasoning tasks. To fill the gap, we introduce SpatialVec, a boundary-aware spatial representation learning framework that adaptively samples geometry boundaries and their surrounding regions, capturing fine-grained geometric structures critical for topology-aware spatial reasoning. A transformer-based encoder-decoder trained through geometry reconstruction produces compact, geometry-aware, and unified representations for points, polylines, and polygons. Empirical evaluation on two real-world datasets shows that SpatialVec substantially improves the preservation of challenging topological relationships involving polygonal interactions and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines significantly on downstream prediction and classification tasks.

title: SpikeAD: Toward Multiplication-Free Spike-Controlled Neuromorphic Architecture for Energy-Efficient Small Object Detection
abstract: Energy-constrained aerial platforms require accurate object detection under strict power and latency budgets, yet conventional inference remains bottlenecked by multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. While spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer bio-inspired efficiency, many SNN detectors retain hybrid MACs in intermediate layers, or use spike-driven inference where multi-level spikes are interpreted as repeated binary events. We propose SpikeAD, a direct-trained spike-controlled neuromorphic aerial detector. In SpikeAD, sparse bounded integer spikes act strictly as multiplexer control signals for multiplier-free shift-add inference, preserving spike boundaries throughout a four-scale bidirectional feature pyramid. We introduce the Spike-Gated Multi-Scale (SGMS) block, performing receptive field expansion with activity-driven channel selection, implementable with adders and comparators. Evaluated on VisDrone and DOTA and across Nano, Small, and Medium variants, SpikeAD achieves up to 46.2% mAP@50 on VisDrone (+4.8% over SNN prior art), and generalizes to oriented bounding box (77.6% mAP@50 on DOTA) using the proposed SpikeOBB head. Under the Horowitz 45nm arithmetic energy model following standard methodology in SNN literature, SpikeAD achieves up to 18.9x estimated reduction relative to an equivalent MAC-based implementation. We propose the Spike Processing Core (SPC), an RTL compute primitive to validate hardware realizability for reconfigurable and scalable custom accelerator chip design on FPGA/ASIC, highlighting a promising path toward next-generation ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors for aerial object detection. Link to the open-source and open-weight GitHub repository will be added upon publication.

title: Predicting Cognitive Profiles from Structural MRI using Spatial Graph Representation Learning
abstract: Predicting cognitive abilities from structural neuroimaging remains challenging due to the high dimensionality and geometric complexity of brain morphology. Conventional models typically flatten regional morphometry into tabular features, failing to explicitly represent spatial relationships. We propose a Spatial-Topological Graph Neural Network (ST-GNN) to predict four distinct cognitive phenotypes across large pediatric cohorts (N = 2,378 to 2,424). By projecting regional morphometry onto a population-level standardized spatial graph, ST-GNN restricts message passing to defined neighboring regions. Evaluations demonstrate that ST-GNN effectively fuses spatial morphology with systemic covariates, outperforming linear baselines and topology-free deep models. Ablations reveal that imposing a sparse geometric topology (K-nearest neighbors) and utilizing global feature scaling - which preserves absolute morphometric scale - outperform fully connected networks and region-normalized approaches. These choices provide transferable architectural inductive biases, revealing differences between computational routing and morphometric feature attribution. Integrated Gradients analysis identified distinct morphological features consistent with neuroanatomical evidence, such as cerebellar volume for working memory and superior frontal surface area for executive function. These findings suggest standardized structural MRI provides useful information for task-specific cognitive prediction, establishing a foundation for MRI-based neurodevelopmental assessment.

title: Brain-Behavior Modeling from Multimodal MRI using Opportunistic Pretraining and Common-Cohort Adaptation
abstract: Incomplete imaging coverage limits sample sizes for multimodal cognitive prediction. We evaluated a two-stage opportunistic deep ensemble using baseline Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study data to predict fluid, crystallized, and total cognition. Separate neural models processed structural/diffusion, resting-state, and task-based MRI data with covariates. Models were pretrained on eligible modality cohorts (up to 9,686 participants), adapted to common training cohorts, and fused via Ridge regression (trimodal cohort: 4,216 participants). Five-fold family-aware cross-validation compared this approach against constituent and covariate-only models. Two-stage training increased mean test coefficient of determination (R^2) in 24 of 27 comparisons (median gain: 0.0081). Fusion increased mean R^2 by 0.0051-0.0333 over the strongest constituent and reduced mean absolute error by 0.0067-0.0976. Task-plus-resting-state and trimodal ensembles reduced absolute error across all targets (nominal p <= 0.0108). Task-plus-resting-state fusion achieved the highest mean R^2 for fluid (0.2222) and total cognition (0.3665), while structural-plus-resting-state led for crystallized cognition (0.3706), yielding R^2 gains of 0.0805, 0.1180, and 0.0890 over covariate-only references. Ablations showed expanded pretraining drove most improvements. Gradient-based attribution identified target-dependent input patterns. These findings support using partially observed cohorts for model development to achieve modest fusion gains. Pending external validation, this approach may support MRI-informed cognitive phenotyping.

title: Characterization of Next Generation Power Over Fiber Systems under Cryogenic Conditions for Advanced Physics Instrumentation
abstract: The successful application of Power-over-Fiber (PoF) technology to power photon detection systems in DUNE prototypes operating under high-voltage and cryogenic conditions has laid the groundwork for the next generation of PoF systems operating in harsh environments. This paper presents the characterization of the main components of a new PoF system operating at 1470 and 1550 nm, including the measurement of the electrical-to-optical conversion efficiency of laser transmitters, the optical-to-electrical conversion efficiency of commercial optical power converters (OPCs), and the estimation of optical fiber attenuation under cryogenic conditions. In addition, a detailed characterization of the response of silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) to light leakage from optical fibers and OPCs is presented, using 808 nm as a reference to evaluate the reduction in the SiPM response at longer wavelengths. The results of this work provide a foundation for the development of next-generation PoF systems capable of powering electronics and electrical systems for future high-energy physics experiments. In addition, the electrical isolation, low-noise operation, and long-term reliability of PoF technology could motivate its application in other research fields requiring remote power delivery under cryogenic conditions, as well as in systems where infrared photons could affect their performance.

title: A Scalable Two-Stage Back-End Architecture for 400GbE Data Acquisition Systems
abstract: A primary challenge in High Energy Physics (HEP) data acquisition is the aggregation of numerous low-speed (10 Gb/s) radiation-hard data links into high-speed back-end interfaces. While high-end FPGAs traditionally perform this task, transceiver density and speed in modern devices can limit cost-effective scaling. This study proposes a two-stage architecture that utilizes mid-range FPGAs for decoding and Ethernet conversion, followed by a Microchip META-DX2+ Ethernet PHY that aggregates these streams into a 400 GbE interface. This study evaluates the design's performance, validating it as a scalable and cost-effective architecture for next-generation HEP data acquisition systems.

title: AnchorKV: Lossless Key-Value Cache Reconstruction from Layer-Sparse Residual Anchors
abstract: Residual-stream caching can reconstruct transformer key-value (KV) caches losslessly, but its memory advantage depends on architecture. We present AnchorKV, a storage-replay spectrum connecting per-layer residual caching and full recomputation through configurable residual anchors. An architecture-dependent break-even rule identifies the first storage-saving spacing, while deployment selects an operating point from the spectrum and cascade replay reduces reconstruction from O(Ls) to O(L), with L the model depth and s the anchor spacing. For interleaved sliding-window architectures, exact dynamic programming places anchors under non-uniform reconstruction demand. Across CPU, CUDA, and Ascend NPU backends, six architecture families, and fp32/bf16 arithmetic, evaluations verify bit-exact KV reconstruction and unchanged continuation logits and tokens. At 4k context, cascade reconstruction is up to 16.3 times faster than naive replay; across eight applicable global-attention checkpoints at 32k context, deepest spacing yields 5.78-54.0 times full-KV reactivatable session capacity. Compared with seven external cache methods on a common model, AnchorKV preserves full-cache retrieval and question-answering scores, whereas lossy methods change output fidelity and task scores. The break-even spacing is computable from a model's configuration file alone.

title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
abstract: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 π^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 π^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

title: State-Dependent Memristor Dynamics for Device-Informed Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity in Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: This work investigates device-informed spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) in spiking neural networks using a literature-derived threshold-memristor model. Local STDP commands determine programming polarity and a programming coordinate for state-dependent conductance updates in the first fully connected layer, while a backpropagation-trained readout performs classification. HSPICE simulations characterize thresholded, polarity- and state-dependent device dynamics and differential crossbar multiply-accumulate behavior. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST compare the hybrid learning rule with direct clipped STDP and evaluate programming asymmetry, device-parameter variation, write noise, stuck-at faults, and input corruption. The hybrid model achieved 95.15% accuracy on MNIST and 85.92% on Fashion-MNIST. In a separate seed-matched comparison, it reached 95.02% and 84.79%, versus 92.33% and 83.25% for direct clipped STDP. Potentiation-dominant asymmetry reduced input-dependent feature selectivity, and endpoint faults introduced during training were less damaging than faults introduced after training. The network-level mapping is a reduced-order, validation-selected abstraction rather than a pulse-accurate physical programming implementation. These results quantify how state-dependent memristor dynamics shape local-STDP learning and its sensitivity to hardware nonidealities.

title: DTP-OPSD: Reinforcement Learning with Distractor-Aware Temporal-Privilege On-Policy Self-Distillation for Temporal Video Grounding
abstract: Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) aims to localize the start and end times of an event described by a language query in a video. The task becomes particularly challenging when the same video contains multiple repeated, similar, or opposite events. On these hard examples, all responses sampled by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) may miss the target and receive zero temporal Intersection-over-Union (tIoU). Their group-relative advantages are then all zero, leaving no useful policy gradient signal. To address this, we propose DTP-OPSD, a reinforcement learning framework with distractor-aware temporal-privilege on-policy self-distillation. The student observes the clean video and generates responses on-policy, while a shared-weight teacher observes a privileged video in which the target window is marked by red full-frame borders and same-video distractor windows by blue full-frame borders. For the distillation loss, the teacher evaluates student-generated prefixes and provides dense token-level Jensen-Shannon divergence supervision. This supervision remains informative even when GRPO provides no policy gradient signal. We suppress distillation when the teacher does not outperform the student and strengthen it for groups where the teacher performs better but all student rollouts receive zero tIoU. We also construct a compact hard-interference training set through VLM screening and human verification. With only 300 additional post-training examples, DTP-OPSD achieves the highest mIoU among the compared open-source 8B models on Charades-TimeLens, ActivityNet-TimeLens, and QVHighlights-TimeLens, reaching 55.93, 54.77, and 66.71, respectively. Compared with Pure GRPO trained on the same data, DTP-OPSD improves all 12 reported metrics, with R1@0.7 gains of 1.28, 1.62, and 1.78 points on the three benchmarks. Code will be released at https://github.com/nian1125/DTP-OPSD

title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
abstract: Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data. We investigate conditional normalizing flows (NFs) and compare their performance with random forest (RF) and quantile random forest (QRF) models. We consider DESI galaxy and quasar targets from DESI DR1 spectroscopic data and with the photometry from Legacy Surveys DR10. We train on 1.1 million sources and test on 2.0 million sources in a non-overlapping sky region ($0<z_{\rm spec}<4.5$). For point estimation, the NF achieves the lowest scatter and outlier fraction at $0<z_{\rm spec}<1.6$ and outperforms both baselines across all three metrics at $z_{\rm spec}>1.6$. By introducing distribution-level metrics like Wasserstein distance and JS divergence, we find that stacking NF posterior PDFs provides more accurate tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction than QRF, particularly at high redshifts. For $z_{\rm median}>2.5$, the NF achieves a smaller absolute mean-redshift bias ($0.060\pm0.031$ versus $0.318$) and higher probability overlap ($0.905\pm0.008$ versus $0.787$) than QRF. We apply redshift-dependent post-hoc PDF calibration derived from a held-out validation sample. After calibration, the absolute mean-redshift biases in four bins spanning $0.2<z_{\rm median}<1.0$ range from $0.0016$ to $0.0019$, with central values below referring benchmark $0.002(1+z)$. In the highest-redshift bin, calibration further reduces the bias to $0.016\pm0.011$. Our results demonstrate the potential of NF PDFs for tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction while highlighting challenges in transferring models across galaxy populations.

title: CDBM: Complexity-Diversity Framework for Building Morphology Analysis
abstract: We introduce Complexity-Diversity Building Metrics (CDBM), twelve interpretable descriptors for building massings represented as vertical extrusions. They measure how strongly geometric detail is expressed (complexity) and how unevenly it varies across one- and two-dimensional elements (diversity). Computed for 482,241,306 OpenStreetMap buildings and compared with 3D Building Metrics (3DBM) and the LION shape latent on task-specific samples, CDBM is tested on function, region, contextual relevance, real-generated discrimination, human preference and geometry-conditioned generation. With gradient boosting, CDBM best separates generated from mapped massings and best matches human preference; with logistic regression it matches 3DBM on realism. 3DBM leads on the other three tasks. As generation targets, the descriptors show that models struggle to produce strongly expressed and heterogeneous forms. CDBM complements existing indicators.

title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $π$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $π((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-κ}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $κ>0$ solves $p^κ+pκ=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

title: OPALX: A performance-portable framework for particle accelerator simulations
abstract: Accurate charged-particle beam simulations require self-consistent collective fields and realistic accelerator models, while their computational cost motivates efficient use of heterogeneous computing systems. We present OPALX, a performance-portable accelerator simulation framework that builds on the beam-dynamics capabilities of OPAL. Its modular architecture uses the Independent Parallel Particle Layer (IPPL) and Kokkos to support distributed-memory execution on multicore CPUs and GPUs from a common codebase. The framework combines relativistic particle tracking with prescribed accelerator fields, particle-in-cell space charge calculations, and spin tracking. We describe the physical and numerical models and their integration into the simulation workflow. The implementation is assessed using disorder-induced heating and frozen-spin test cases, together with comparisons of spin evolution with G4Beamline and beam transport with TraceWin. A three-dimensional space charge benchmark evaluates throughput on CPU and GPU systems, reaching approximately $10^9$ macroparticles per second on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU for this benchmark. These results provide initial verification of the implemented models and demonstrate CPU and GPU execution of self-consistent space charge calculations. OPALX provides a common foundation for extending accelerator models and numerical methods across heterogeneous computing platforms.

title: Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics
abstract: What does it mean to tell the story of a mathematician? Written as a letter to a young Black mathematician, this article reflects on how stories shape our understanding of mathematics and our sense of belonging within the mathematical community. Through the lens of Hidden Figures Revealed, a project documenting Black mathematicians at The Ohio State University, I discuss humanity, mathematics, and context as three guiding principles for mathematical storytelling. In particular, I reflect on how this framework emerged through archival research, shaped historical narratives, and informed mathematical learning experiences.

title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
abstract: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{ρ,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\midρ$. For $c=2$ the graphs are exactly the cocktail party graphs, and for $c=3$ they are exactly the Cartesian product $K_3\,\square\,K_3$ of two triangles, the Petersen graph and its complement. We also show that such a graph need not be transmission-regular: Seidel switching the lattice graph $K_6\,\square\,K_6$ with respect to a line and the triangular graph $T(11)$ with respect to a maximal clique of size $10$ gives graphs on $36$ and $55$ vertices with distance spectra $\{54,0^{(26)},(-6)^{(9)}\}$ and $\{81,0^{(45)},(-9)^{(9)}\}$. Among the graphs of diameter $2$ obtained by switching a strongly regular graph with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ with respect to one part of an equitable partition, these two are the only ones that have exactly three distance eigenvalues and are not transmission-regular. We also observe that the transmission-regular graphs with exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues, the smallest one being $-3$, are exactly the complements of the strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ other than the cocktail party graphs.

title: A $θ$-implicit hybrid particle-in-cell algorithm for kinetic simulations of magnetized plasmas
abstract: Hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) models with kinetic ions and an inertialess electron fluid are widely used to simulate magnetized plasmas at ion scales, but explicit time advances are constrained by the whistler-wave CFL condition $\dt \propto Δx^2$, and the sub-cycling and artificial dissipation used to mitigate it carry accumulating costs. We present a $θ$-implicit hybrid PIC algorithm, implemented in the open-source GPU-capable code WarpX, in which fields and particles are advanced as a single nonlinear system solved by a particle-suppressed Jacobian-free Newton--Krylov method: the particles are nonlinearly eliminated, the electric field of the generalized Ohm's law is the sole unknown, and mass matrices remove all particle operations from the linear iterations. The electron pressure is advanced inside the nonlinear solve, and the scheme satisfies a discrete energy law whose single dissipation term vanishes at $θ= 1/2$ and damps only temporally under-resolved modes for $θ> 1/2$. The advance reproduces parallel and perpendicular wave dispersion including the ion Bernstein modes, conserves total energy to machine roundoff where the explicit advance heats secularly, does not develop the cold-beam finite-grid instability, and reproduces the $m=0$ instability of a Bennett pinch in RZ geometry. We conclude with 3D simulations of a field-reversed configuration initialized from a Grad--Shafranov equilibrium, comparing the explicit and implicit advances on the growth of the tilt instability and the preservation of trapped magnetic flux.

title: SPARQLcirc: Probabilistic Query Evaluation with Provenance Circuits
abstract: Probabilistic query evaluation (PQE) computes the probability of every answer of a query over a tuple-independent probabilistic knowledge graph. We study exact PQE for SPARQL over graphs accessed through SPARQL 1.1 endpoints. Shared triples among the derivations of an answer make exact PQE #P-hard in general. Knowledge compilation of the Boolean provenance of every answer yields exact probabilities, and the provenance formulas of different answers can share subformulas. We propose SPARQLcirc, which rewrites a SPARQL query into CONSTRUCT queries that name every gate by its content, so that the results of independent queries form one Boolean provenance circuit for all answers. The rewriting covers joins, unions, projection, filters, OPTIONAL, difference, and transitive closures. SPARQLcirc compiles the circuit and computes the exact probability of every answer by weighted model counting. For the evaluation, we draw random probabilities for the triples of WatDiv and gMark and the statements of Wikidata and evaluate the CONSTRUCT queries on GraphDB, Fuseki, and Oxigraph. The ratio of the end-to-end time of PQE with SPARQLcirc to that of PQE by compiling the provenance expressions of the SPARQL provenance rewriting NPCS decreases with the number of derivations.

title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
abstract: For Hermitian matrices $α,β$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^α$ and $m$ letters $e^β$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)\ge\Tr e^{nα+mβ}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.

title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs). These algorithms primarily target forward MDPs whose dynamics evolve over time from an initial state. However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics. As a consequence, they cannot be expressed as a standard MDP, thereby calling for a novel theory for RL in this context. Accordingly, this work introduces the concept of Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems, develops a novel theoretical framework to characterize their optimal solutions, and proposes a general forward-backward step-wise template that allows to adapt RL algorithms for FB-MDP problems. A Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) algorithm is introduced accordingly to obtain optimal policies with guaranteed convergence and a competitive rate with respect to standard approaches in RL. FB-MOAC is evaluated on diverse use cases in the context of mathematical finance and mobile resource management. The obtained results show that FB-MOAC outperforms the state of the art across different metrics, highlighting its ability to learn and maximize rewards.

title: $α$-decay widths from two-potential approaches and WKB prefactors
abstract: The accurate calculation of $α$-decay widths can be obtained with several equivalent descriptions of the Gurvitz-Kalbermann two-potential approach (TPA) or a semiclassical WKB description having both correct barrier penetrability and consistent inner-state normalization prefactor. This prefactor, which is related to the assault frequency, is implemented in several ways in the literature, producing systematically different results that can be mistaken for $α$ preformation effects. We benchmark single-particle $α$-decay widths across 161 even-even nuclei ($A_p=144$--$252$) using several TPA descriptions and WKB calculations with four common prefactors, employing a Woods-Saxon potential fixed by the quantization-constrained parameter method. The TPA formulas agree to within a few parts in $10^{-8}$, highlighting their robustness. Among semiclassical prefactors, only the widely used round-trip (RT) approximation closely reproduces the TPA widths to within a few percent. An Airy-function analysis reveals this $\cos^2\to 1/2$ averaged WKB prefactor is the correct leading-order semiclassical normalization of the exact quasibound state, clarifying the counterintuitive empirical observations associated with the WKB prefactors. Our benchmark identifies the WKB prefactor appropriate for $α$-decay tunneling analysis and provides a clean reference for isolating preformation and structure effects in future studies.

title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
abstract: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

title: Unitarity and Positivity Constraints on C- or P-odd Anomalous Quartic Couplings
abstract: In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints in the dimension-eight genuine anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We extend previous partial-wave unitarity analyses to include all C- or P-odd operators, thereby completing the coverage of the full basis of 34 operators. We also derive an analytical set of necessary forward-limit positivity bounds that include all CP-odd Wilson coefficients. We demonstrate that non-vanishing CP-odd Wilson coefficients require non-vanishing contributions from the CP-even sector to satisfy the derived positivity conditions. Combining the positivity conditions with partial-wave unitarity, we obtain stronger bounds on twenty-three of the thirty-four Wilson coefficients in this sector of the SMEFT.

title: Hydrodynamic flow in the gut hinders the fixation of beneficial mutants but accelerates their invasion
abstract: Gut bacteria experience a spatially structured environment with hydrodynamic flow. Using a branching-process approach, we show that beneficial mutants arising randomly upon division have a reduced fixation probability compared to the well-mixed case. The suppression factor is set by the spatial heterogeneity of mutant fate across the gut. In contrast, the invasion of mutant lineages that avoid early stochastic extinction is accelerated in the gut compared to a matched well-mixed case. Stronger advective flow decreases fixation probabilities while accelerating mutant invasion.

title: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
abstract: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($γγ\to a\toγγ$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.

title: Remark About Action for Rastall Gravity
abstract: In this short note we study Rastall gravity action as was proposed by Golovnev in [7]. We construct its reparametrization invariant form and determine corresponding equations of motion.

title: Partial $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
abstract: We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings: (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$. In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,α}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property. In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$. We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations. Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.

title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents
abstract: Existing large language model (LLM) backdoor attacks operate primarily in chat settings, where the risk is bounded by free-form text outputs. AI agents remove that bound by performing actions and executing commands on the user's machine. We introduce structured-output backdoor attacks against reasoning models in agentic coding settings. A trigger placed anywhere in the agent's context causes the model to emit an attacker-chosen tool call, which the harness executes, directly compromising the system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability. We present Kerkoporta, a methodology that constructs high-quality poison samples, injects the backdoor via supervised fine-tuning, and recovers utility loss with lightweight reinforcement learning. We evaluate on modern, heavily post-trained open-weight models across proprietary and open-source harnesses, focusing on coding for its wide adoption and long-horizon task structure. The attack reaches success rates of up to 96.2% and can be configured to generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target. The resulting models can outperform the clean baseline on standard utility benchmarks, giving victims a direct incentive to adopt them. Overall, we demonstrate that LLM backdoors can have critical security impacts in the context of modern coding agents, and we characterize the poisoning methodology required to insert backdoors that are both effective and stealthy in this setting.

title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Ważewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

title: Toward Contrast-Free Breast MRI: Improving Cancer Detection With Virtual Contrast Enhanced Imaging
abstract: Although contrast-enhanced (CE) breast MRI is an important tool for cancer detection, intravenous gadolinium administration introduces additional considerations for patients and clinical workflows. AI based virtual contrast enhanced (VCE) MRI could help identify patients for whom acquired CE imaging may be avoidable without compromising diagnostic performance. We developed a framework that combines non contrast (NC) and VCE MRI predictions for cancer detection. On the held-out test set, cancer detection using NC MRI alone achieved an AUROC of 0.865. Combining the predictions from NC and VCE MRI improved AUROC to 0.901. Building on this complementary predictive value, we evaluated patient-level routing to progressively replace acquired CE examinations with the NC plus VCE pathway, prioritizing patients with the most confident NC predictions. This simulation suggests that diagnostic performance can be largely preserved while limiting acquired CE imaging to approximately 40% of patients. Together, these findings demonstrate the complementary value of VCE MRI and suggest its potential to support selective contrast use in breast cancer screening.

title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
abstract: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_ξ$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $γ_5$.

title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

title: Global and crustal properties of neutron stars
abstract: We investigate how the treatment of the neutron star crust affects both the global properties of the star and the properties of the crust itself. Three approaches are compared: a direct connection between a fixed crust and the core equation of state (EOS), a smooth crossover between them, and a unified EOS in which the crust is computed within a compressible liquid-drop model with the same nuclear empirical parameters of the relativistic mean-field model used for the core. For each approach, we consider four values of the symmetry energy slope, $44 \le L \le 92$ MeV. For a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star, some global properties are weakly to moderately affected: the radius and the moment of inertia agree within 1\% among the three approaches. On the other hand, the tidal deformability obtained with the direct connection is up to 21\% lower than the unified one for $L = 92$ MeV. A much larger contrast comes from the crustal properties. Relative to the unified EOS, the direct connection yields a crust that is 15--36\% thinner, 6--12 times less massive, and that carries a fraction of the total moment of inertia 5--8 times smaller (0.3--1.1\% instead of 2.8--6.2\%). The differences between crust treatments are thus comparable to or larger than those arising from variations in $L$ for crustal properties, while they remain subleading for global ones.

title: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state
abstract: This paper determines exactly the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the normalized symmetric Werner state in every local dimension $d\ge2$ \begin{equation*} \mathrm{EoP}_2(W_{+,d})=\log_2\frac{4d(d+1)}{d^2+3d+4}. \end{equation*} We establish additivity for tensor power and, more generally, additivity for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. A canonical purification and its products achieve these values globally, even when arbitrary joint purifications with unrestricted finite dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. We further examine perturbations away from the symmetric endpoint, and prove the continuity of the optimal value at this endpoint; moreover, we show a sharp square root order of variation in the optimal purity, while the canonical purification remains asymptotically optimal in the achieved entropy as this weight goes to zero.

title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

title: FastHeapDict: Permanent Slot Indexing for Efficient Decrease-Key Operations in Indexed Priority Queues
abstract: Efficient decrease-key support remains an important practical concern in priority queues used by shortest-path and graph-processing algorithms. Although duplicate-entry heaps avoid explicit decrease-key operations and are simple to implement, they may accumulate many stale entries when tentative priorities are repeatedly improved. This paper presents FastHeapDict, an indexed binary min-heap based on permanent slot indexing. Instead of repeatedly locating keys through hash-table lookups during heap repair, FastHeapDict assigns each key a stable integer slot and stores that slot directly in heap entries. As a result, position updates during sift-up and sift-down operations are performed through integer indexing while preserving the usual indexed-heap interface. We evaluate FastHeapDict in both Python and C++20 using Dijkstra's algorithm as the primary experimental workload. The benchmarks include constructed dense stress graphs, randomized dense graph variants, and comparisons against duplicate-entry heaps and existing priority-queue alternatives. Across the tested Python workloads, FastHeapDict consistently outperforms the duplicate-entry heapq baseline and the tested heapdict and pqdict implementations. In the C++20 implementation, FastHeapDict also achieves strong constant-factor improvements over std::priority_queue duplicates, std::set-based decrease-key, and std::multiset duplicates. These results indicate that permanent slot indexing can provide a compact and effective implementation strategy for indexed priority queues in workloads where priority updates are frequent.

title: Optical Signature of Bias-Induced Carrier Injection in a WSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure Diode
abstract: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe$_2$ is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: The sum of sizes of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
abstract: Families $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_m\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ are cross-intersecting if every member of one family meets every member of each other family. A family is nontrivial if its members have no common element. For $n>2k$ and $m\ge3$, we determine the maximum sum of the sizes of $m$ nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families. We prove the sharp bound \[ \sum_{i=1}^{m}|\mathcal A_i| \le \max\bigl\{m\,h(n,k,1),\ g(n,k)+3(m-1)\bigr\}, \] where \[ h(n,k,1)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+1 \] and \[ g(n,k)=\binom nk-2\binom{n-k}k -\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}k. \] We also characterize all equality cases. Two types of extremal configurations arise: copies of a maximum nontrivial intersecting family, and copies of a specific three-member nontrivial intersecting family together with its full cross-intersecting companion. The proof applies a known restricted lexicographic comparison to obtain the weighted bound for shifted families, and uses local generator reductions for critically shifted families. These reductions exploit shiftedness after removing the common core of a section, while preserving nontriviality and the required shadow relations between sections.

title: Large Maximal Intersecting Families with Covering Number Three
abstract: Let $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$. The largest size of an intersecting family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ with covering number at least three is \[ g_1(n,k)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k}{k-1}+3, \] attained by a unique family up to isomorphism. We prove that every other maximal intersecting family $\mathcal F$ with covering number three satisfies \[ |\mathcal F|\le M(n,k)=\max\{q(n,k),g_2(n,k)\}, \] where \begin{align*} q(n,k)&=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-3}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}{k-1}+3,\\ g_2(n,k)&=g_1(n,k)-\binom{n-k-3}{k-3}+1. \end{align*} This bound is attained for every $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$, so $M(n,k)$ is the second largest distinct size. For $k=4$, $g_1(n,4)=13n-69$ and $M(n,4)=12n-61$. For $k\ge5$, we have $M(n,k)=q(n,k)$ when $2k<n\le3k-2$ and $M(n,k)=g_2(n,k)$ when $n\ge3k-2$; the two terms coincide only at $n=3k-2$. We also classify all families attaining $M(n,k)$ that admit a critically shifted labeling, including additional nonisomorphic families at $n=2k+1$. The proof combines local replacements with an inverse-shift estimate and gives a new proof of the known maximum and its uniqueness.

title: Contrastive Astromer: Two-Stage Contrastive Representation Learning for Astronomical Light Curve Classification
abstract: Large astronomical surveys collect abundant light curves, but reliable class labels remain scarce. ASTROMER 2 learns from unlabeled light curves by reconstructing masked observations, yet this objective does not explicitly encourage class separation in a compact representation of each light curve. We introduce Contrastive Astromer, a two-stage approach that makes these representations more useful for classification without changing the ASTROMER 2 encoder architecture. First, unsupervised contrastive learning on single-band MACHO light curves brings together representations of augmented views of the same object. Supervised contrastive learning, supported by an auxiliary classification loss, then uses a separate labeled Alcock sample to strengthen class discrimination. We evaluate the resulting representations by freezing the encoder and training a separate classifier. On a held-out set of 600 objects, this classifier achieves a macro-F1 of 0.7943 with 500 labeled examples per class, exceeding our reproduction of the ASTROMER 2 finetune-and-classify pipeline by 5.10 percentage points. With downstream classifier training budgets of 20 and 100 examples per class, macro-F1 reaches 0.7078 and 0.7704, respectively, also surpassing this baseline. Embedding-space analyses further show that supervised adaptation improves local class consistency and global class separation. These results show that contrastive adaptation makes pretrained light-curve representations more effective for classification and more informative about the structure of variability classes.

title: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification
abstract: Chronic kidney disease is characterized by structural alterations in renal tissue and progressive loss of kidney function. While glomerular subtype ratios provide a compact and clinically meaningful summary of glomerular composition, representing pathomic information using whole-slide image (WSI)-level mean values diminishes glomerulus-level heterogeneity and the contribution of less prevalent patterns. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated whether modeling individual glomeruli using multiple-instance learning (MIL) could provide complementary information to conventional subtype ratios for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classification. We analyzed 162 kidney-biopsy WSIs from 162 patients, categorizing renal function as eGFR < 60 or >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Quantitative size, shape, intensity, and texture features were extracted from segmented glomeruli, representing each patient as a bag of glomerular instances. An attention-based MIL model was trained to aggregate these heterogeneous pathomic profiles. We evaluated subtype ratios, pathomics, and their combination using ABMIL, with a mean-pooled multilayer perceptron baseline. In five-fold cross-validation, the subtype-ratio-only model achieved an AUC of 0.7262 +/- 0.0596. MIL using pathomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.7362 +/- 0.0788, whereas integrating pathomics with subtype ratios produced the highest mean AUC of 0.7630 +/- 0.0665. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine individual feature contributions. These results demonstrate that MIL-based pathomics can complement established glomerular subtype ratios by capturing additional glomerulus-level information for quantitative kidney-biopsy analysis.

title: Inference in an interactive multi-type branching network
abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between $d$ individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available. This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.

title: On Small Universal Reversible Turing Machines
abstract: A reversible Turing machine (RTM) is a Turing machine in which every instantaneous description has at most one predecessor. Writing URTM(m,n) for a universal RTM with m states and n symbols, we construct URTM(3,600), URTM(4,41), URTM(5,37), URTM(6,30), URTM(7,28), URTM(8,21), and URTM(85,2); each of them has fewer states or fewer symbols than each of the nine URTMs in Morita's book (2017). They come from improved versions of Morita's conversions to three states, to four states, and to two symbols; for example, the improved conversion to three states uses O(mn^2) symbols instead of O(m^2n^3). We also show that the halting problem of RTMs with at most two states is decidable for finite instantaneous descriptions, so that no RTM with at most two states is universal under any notion of universality that reduces the halting problem of Turing machines to it by a computable encoding into finite instantaneous descriptions; in particular, there is no URTM with at most two states in our formalization of Morita's definition. We also show that no three-state, two-symbol RTM is universal in that formalization.

title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot satisfy odd periodic boundaries. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one. Thus selection reduces an exponential degeneracy to polynomial growth, while the whole-sample orientation fractions remain broadly distributed. We also derive explicit two-sided entropy-density bounds for periodic spin ground states and honeycomb dimer coverings on $M\times N$ tori, where $M,N$ are the periods along the two primitive lattice directions. For all $M,N\geq3$, the errors relative to the bulk residual entropy are bounded by explicit constants times $\min(M,N)^{-2}$, without an aspect-ratio restriction. These bounds give finite-size accuracy guarantees and control the exponentially small fraction of unperturbed ground states that survive the selection.

title: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Toward Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models
abstract: Post-incident analysis of a robot foundation model poses a singular causal question: which internal components caused this failure, and to what degree? Mechanistic interpretability (MI), however, establishes general causal claims by decoding the concepts a policy has learned, yet knowing which concepts are encoded is insufficient for identifying the actual cause of a specific incident. In this position paper, we analyze this concept-malfunction gap by posing fault isolation in the framework of actual causality. Specifically, we formalize a fault-isolation query as a tuple of intervened internal components, counterfactual values, contingencies, and read-outs, and lay out conditions for it to be well-specified. Through this lens, we identify shortcomings of current MI approaches: they assume fixed contingencies and read out only immediate effects, letting backups obscure actual causes. We demonstrate on a toy example that these shortcomings can lead to conflicting verdicts. Lastly, based on the well-specification conditions, we outline four open research tasks toward closing the gap.

title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
abstract: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.

title: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
abstract: Fourier phase retrieval aims to reconstruct images from magnitude-only measurements; however, the absence of phase information, noises, and channel ambiguities make the recovery of natural color images challenging. Although diffusion-prior-based methods impose strong image constraints, their recovery performance degrades under higher measurement noise, and repeated generative updates incur substantial computational overhead. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel method, termed FlowFPR, that integrates a pretrained flow-matching prior with the relaxed averaged alternating reflections (RAAR) algorithm for oversampled Fourier phase retrieval. In the basic version of FlowPR (Flow-RAAR-basic), a color image is estimated by repeatedly performing four steps at each outer iteration, where the flow-prior prediction step exploits single-step straight-line prediction, considerably reducing the generation cost. Nevertheless, Flow-RAAR-basic still suffers from two critical issues: (i) the predefined fusion weights, \(λ_n\), might lead to either ineffective or excessive correction, and (ii) the fixed iteration number used by RAAR algorithm does not allow adaptation to measurement noise. To address these two issues, we develop two improved algorithms, Flow-RAAR-adaptive and Flow-RAAR-controlled, respectively. Moreover, these two improved algorithms naturally lead to a joint variant, Flow-RAAR-joint, which combines their advantages. Extensive experiments on a natural face image dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the four proposed methods compared with other relevant competing methods, as well as their acceleration over two recent diffusion-based methods. In the noise setting, Flow-RAAR-joint performs best among the four proposed methods.

title: Scaling Trusted Autonomy: Towards Generally Capable Verifiable Robots
abstract: Robots powered by foundation models are increasingly able to interpret open-ended language, recognize unfamiliar objects, and operate across diverse environments. Yet broader capability does not establish that a robot has understood a request, that its actions will produce the intended effects, or that its internal representation still corresponds to reality. Classical symbolic planning provides explicit structure for composition and verification, but traditionally depends on hand-engineered skills and representations. Learned policies can broaden the robot's repertoire, but provide weak guarantees about what will happen and why. This thesis argues that scaling trusted autonomy requires a neurosymbolic approach that unifies the generality of learned models with symbolic structure for robust robot behavior. It explores three complementary directions. First, LIMP uses foundation models and spatial reasoning to ground natural-language instructions in explicit task constraints and instruction-specific semantic maps, enabling task-and-motion planning while exposing the robot's interpretation for inspection. Second, REALM maintains an editable, photorealistic 3D Gaussian scene, predicts the consequences of planned manipulation, and locally reconciles the scene so that subsequent instructions obtain their grounding and planning geometry from an updated state. Third, PACTS learns visuomotor skills that jointly generate action trajectories and predictions of their symbolic effects, supporting skill composition, progress monitoring, and recovery through replanning. Together, these contributions preserve explicit structure for reasoning and verification while broadening how it is obtained, providing a foundation for generally capable robots whose behavior can be assessed under the assumptions of their models.

title: A Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering Framework with Automated Cluster Cardinality Estimation Ability
abstract: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown. To address these limitations, we introduce in this paper the Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering (GSFC) framework, which incorporates a continuous sparsity penalty into the fuzzy objective function. Because closed-form solutions are precluded by the simultaneous presence of fuzzifier and sparsity exponents, we propose an efficient primal-dual bisection search coupled with specialized analytic pathways to rigorously enforce the partition constraint while organically driving trace memberships to exact zero. This mathematically enforced sparsity empowers the algorithm to autonomously estimate the true number of clusters by dynamically pruning redundant clusters, provided that it is initialized by a larger than the true number of clusters. Furthermore, we integrate a virtual noise sink to insulate outliers from the rest of the data points. The usage of the proposed framework is also extended to line segment detection. Extensive empirical evaluations across synthetic toy datasets, high-noise geometric stress tests, and real-world benchmarks (UCI wine dataset and hyperspectral images) demonstrate that GSFC effectively exceeds conventional fuzzy benchmarks while autonomously resolving cluster cardinality. Additionally, it significantly outperforms existing sparse possibilistic and probabilistic soft-clustering alternatives in line detection tasks.

title: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
abstract: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$μ$s, 100\,$μ$s, and 6\,$μ$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

title: How timing and mode of selection shape ancestral genetic contributions
abstract: We examine a population that evolves according to a biparental Moran model with two distinct types of individuals. Each individual's type is determined by the allele they carry at one biallelic locus, which is transmitted in a Mendelian way. This type influences the individual's mating preferences. We investigate two specific mating patterns: (i) where the type determines the level of attractiveness, and (ii) where the type dictates the level of homogamous choosiness. In both scenarios, one type has an advantage over the other. Assuming an initial proportion b of individuals are of the advantaged type, we give an explicit formula for the asymptotic proportion of the population's genome that originates from these advantaged ancestors under an infinite population size approximation. Our results enable a comparison of the relative strengths of homogamous choosiness, attractiveness, and viability selection in terms of genome transmission, and prove notably that viability selection is always more efficient than both forms of reproductive selection.

title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. Using NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.

title: Claude for Excel is Transformative for Basic Spreadsheet Modeling and Analysis
abstract: We used the Claude Excel plug-in to build and analyze spreadsheet models for five semi structured problem statements (including a test-piece teaching case with data in multiple exhibits) and evaluated performance on modeling (what is to be coded), spreadsheet engineering (quality of coding), analysis (algorithms applied to the spreadsheet), and insight generation. Claude's ability to create a high-quality spreadsheet model from a semi structured problem statement is astoundingly excellent. Given very simple prompts, Claude generates extensive, accurate sensitivity and scenario analyses and reasonable plain English insights. Claude is Solver-aware and builds optimization models without specific prompting. Analyst productivity gains will likely be high. Business school quant courses will have to change. The way we develop human expertise will have to change.

title: Excel: A Financial Modelling System
abstract: Since the calculation engine of Excel was the subject of a major upgrade to accommodate Dynamic Arrays in 2018, there has been a series of seismic changes to the art of financial modelling. This paper will show the traditional financial modelling techniques for spreadsheets can be replaced by radically different approaches that have significant gains in readability, performance and flexibility. With so much power added to the Excel engine in recent years, it is the responsibility of financial modellers to ensure that they are building in the simplest and most auditable way possible going forward.

title: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail
abstract: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks. We design a posterior-sampling agent for it. Each period it draws a market from an exact posterior and posts the bid and discount of that market's exactly solved season plan, so every action is one a fully informed seller could take. In a simulated online florist it has the lowest regret averaged over markets. In weak markets it gives up 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons, four to seven times less than drawing once per season. A planner acting on point estimates can stop bidding and never learn that bidding pays. The agent escapes after about three seasons on average, against fifty with one draw per season. Where displayed scarcity keeps willingness to pay above the posted price, the discount needs no learning. Customers waiting for the discount to return to its recent level look like lost sales, so frequent waiting makes the agent underrate its market. One discount per season removes waiting at a cost of 5.9% of clairvoyant revenue in a weak market and none in a strong one.
