Under a career inducement the LLM agents revise their estimates less, not more, and they name the inducement as a threat to independence. Furthermore, some models revise only toward the more conservative estimate, while others revise in both directions. LLM agents thus do not respond to social influence pressures as human auditors do, and LLM-based decision support systems should be designed with the differences in mind.

title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

title: Beyond Blackwell: Constrained Data Processing Inequalities
abstract: We study the comparison of statistical experiments from a decision-theoretic standpoint, working with Markov transitions as basis-free linear maps on dual spaces. Our starting observation is that the data-processing inequality, that adding noise to an experiment cannot lower its Bayes risk, is the functoriality of fibrewise minimisation over a presheaf of decision rules: the rules available after an experiment form a presheaf, garbling acts on it by precomposition, and a risk functional is a natural transformation from it to the ordered reals. The argument refers to neither probabilities nor expected values, and it survives replacing the decision presheaf by a sub-presheaf of admissible rules. Any constraint imposed on the strategy that a rule induces fairness, unbiasedness, is automatically of this form, and so yields a data-processing inequality with no counterpart in the unconstrained Blackwell theory. Our main result is their quantitative companion. For constraints closed under post-processing we define a constrained deficiency and prove a constrained randomization theorem: one experiment dominates another on every admissible decision problem exactly when the constrained deficiency is small. The classical theorem is the case of no constraint, where the identity is itself an admissible rule; in general it is not, and the constrained deficiency is an optimisation over the coarsenings of an experiment that render it compliant. Specialising to equalized odds, we exhibit a pair of experiments that unconstrained Bayes risk identifies at a given loss and prior but that the constrained risk separates, giving a one-line certificate of Blackwell-incomparability. We work throughout with finite sets.

title: Efficient and Scalable Multi-View Masked Autoencoder for Heterogeneous Graph Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the flourishing of self-supervised learning on heterogeneous graphs, e.g., masked autoencoder-based methods. However, existing methods suffer from three issues, including the prohibitive computational cost of constructing meta-path-induced subgraphs, the limitations of uniform random masking, and the suboptimal objective of reconstructing potentially noisy or uninformative original node features. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-View Masked Auto Encoder (MVMAE), a novel, efficient, and scalable framework for heterogeneous graph self-supervised learning. First, MVMAE introduces a novel multi-view mask-then-reconstruct strategy. Instead of masking individual nodes or features, MVMAE randomly masks entire meta-path views and guides the model to reconstruct their representations from remaining visible views. This approach shifts the learning objective to a high-level and semantic task, providing a more robust and informative supervisory signal that is effective even when initial node features are absent or flawed. Then, to handle the computational demands, MVMAE employs an efficient offline aggregation mechanism that pre-computes and reuses representations for each meta-path view, completely avoiding the costly construction of meta-path-induced subgraphs. Next, to fuse the representations of each view, MVMAE uses a Transformer-based multi-view fusion encoder to capture the complex correlations between views, and a deliberately simple MLP decoder to compel the encoder to learn highly expressive and robust node representations. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets, including three large-scale graphs, demonstrate that MVMAE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art self-supervised and even semi-supervised baselines, confirming its superior effectiveness and scalability. Our source code is released at https://github.com/hcmdgh/MVMAE.

title: Practical Preimages for 19- and 20-Step SHA-256 with Standard Padding
abstract: We present practical preimage attacks on 19- and 20-step SHA-256 that respect the standard IV, Davies-Meyer feed-forward, and full FIPS 180-4 padding, for arbitrary prescribed 256-bit targets. Building on Basra's algebraic selector saturation and backward padding absorption, we introduce three techniques: an exact $O(1)$ inversion of the low padding byte $(W_{13} \bmod 256) = \mathtt{0x80}$ that leaves $(a_5, a_6)$ free for exact context shaping; a causal bit-slice equivalence theorem that prunes $99.74\%$ of right-hand candidate nodes across seven stages; and a closed-form $\mathbf{F}_2$ upper-half inverse paired with compact $Q_0^{-1}$ lookup tables. One CPU core solves arbitrary 19-step padded targets in $1.2$--$86.4$ s (median $19.5$ s) after an $18$ s table build. A 20-step padded preimage costs $2^{46.6}$ CPU-reference evaluations: $191$ node-hours on one 10-core Apple M4 CPU node (16 threads), or $9.0$--$22.2$ GPU-hours on one NVIDIA L4. A companion Zero-$a_3$ bridge inverts the unpadded 20-step compression function in $2^{38.1}$ evaluations. We provide 46 self-verifying witnesses, including 55-byte preimages of SHA-256("abc") and $0^{256}$. These attacks cover 19--20 of 64 steps and do not threaten full SHA-256.

title: WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation
abstract: Most agentic robotic systems use vision-language models (VLMs) either to orchestrate predefined skills or to directly generate actions, constraints, and control programs. The former is limited by the available skill library, while the latter requires VLMs to reason about precise geometry and contact. In this paper, we propose WorldSketch, a new paradigm for agentic robotics in which a VLM constructs a world model rather than generating robot actions. The VLM acts as an agent that actively queries perception tools to build and visually validate a minimal kinematic world model, capturing only task-relevant objects, their interaction geometry, and possible motions. A geometric planner then jointly optimizes contact and whole-body motion on the resulting model. Moreover, the world model is self-improving: execution feedback verifies outcomes, updates uncertain hypotheses, and enables the agent to revise the model when its predictions are contradicted. We demonstrate the generality of this paradigm across RoboCasa, LIBERO-PRO, and R2R-CE navigation, achieving zero-shot success rates of 91%, 97%, and 76%, respectively. On RoboCasa, WorldSketch outperforms the next-best zero-shot agent baseline by 58 percentage points while using 10 times fewer VLM input tokens; on LIBERO-PRO, it exceeds CaP-X by 82 percentage points. In navigation, it matches the success rate of step-by-step VLM agents while using 6 times fewer input tokens.

title: Unconstrained support points can leave a convex support
abstract: Support points provide a practical and effective way to approximate a probability distribution by a small set of equally weighted representatives through energy-distance minimization. In many applications, the variables satisfy convex constraints that the representatives should also respect. We investigate whether unconstrained support points automatically satisfy such constraints and show that this is not guaranteed. We construct counterexamples using three planar observations, a density with full triangular support, and positive-definite matrix data admitting an indefinite optimal representative under the Frobenius norm. We also identify cases in which containment holds, establish stability under distributional perturbations, and quantify the objective cost of imposing a convex-hull constraint. For a fixed number of representatives and a positive population constraint gap, empirical configurations with vanishing global objective error eventually leave the sample convex hull almost surely.

title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions. AStockArena reconstructsthe actions actually posted to accounts by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states, and audits them with eight checks spanning execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B), combining record verification with consensus expert annotation. Of 1,070 trading points, 72.99% exhibit at least one audit gap; model-level rates range from52.2% to 91.2%, with evidence gaps most prevalent. Historical trade-filtering replay further shows thatportfolio outcomes are sensitive to these flagged trades. Decision-process auditing thus offers a verifiable complement to return-based evaluation of financial agents.

title: Fast Neural Noise Stabilizes Associative Memory against Slow Synaptic Noise
abstract: Neural systems operate under multi-timescale stochastic dynamics, yet reliably maintain stable functions. We investigate how fast neural fluctuations and slow synaptic variability asymmetrically influence the structural robustness of associative memories. While synaptic noise degrades memory formation, neural noise stabilizes the network against structural perturbations. For sequential learning of multiple memories, the average recall performance is maximized at an intermediate neural-noise amplitude, whereas increasing synaptic noise rapidly degrades memory performance. Using an adiabatic mean-field framework, we derive an analytical stationary distribution of stability factors. Our theory reveals that fast neural fluctuations push the system away from marginal stability, serving as an indispensable prerequisite for systemic stability.

title: Limits and Constants of OpenAI's Claimed ETH Refutation
abstract: A recent OpenAI preprint claims a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF formula in time $2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, and $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ at bounded clause density, which would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The headline bound is proved by tensor contraction; the body develops an interpolation algorithm with the weaker exponent $n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n}$. This note does four things. First, it explains the interpolation algorithm in plain terms. Second, it asks how large $n$ must be for the bounds to bite. The preprint states no constants, so we treat the hidden constant $C$ as a parameter: the general bound beats the $2^n$ of brute force only beyond $n\approx 10^{32}$ for $C=2$, $10^{126}$ for $C=3$ and $10^{3517}$ for $C=10$. We then extract the constants from the tensor-contraction proof: for every input with $m$ clauses at bounded density, the running time it certifies stays above $2^n$ unless $\log_2(n+m)>10^9$, and on random 3-CNF at the satisfiability threshold unless $\log_2 n>5\times10^{11}$. So the bounds are subexponential as $n\to\infty$, but the proof certifies no speed-up over brute force for any input of bounded density that could ever be written down. Third, for the clause-product form of the interpolation algorithm we prove limits in a cost model matching the preprint's evaluation. By a short algebraic lemma, polynomial cost needs components of $O(\log^3 n)$ variables with per-point evaluation, or primal treewidth $O(\log^2 n)$ with dynamic programming over the groups. So the scheme costs $2^{Ω(\sqrt{\mathrm{tw}})}$ at treewidth $\mathrm{tw}$, $2^{Ω(\sqrt n)}$ with high probability on random 3-CNF above clause density 3, and $2^{Ω(n^{1/3})}$ even on trivially countable path formulas. We explain why the preprint's sharper routes escape these limits. Fourth, we report experiments.

title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
abstract: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious. An analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning while extracting the specification can do worse than no intervention, and instructing it to ignore them did not close the gap, so we exclude assistant turns structurally. On Lost in Conversation (replaying difficulty-selected instances), where AO is an oracle by construction, AC3 closes 55-84% of the gap between full context and AO on three of four tasks and exceeds AO on the fourth, and an LLM that faithfully summarizes the history does not reproduce the gain even with more compute. On real WildChat conversations, a GPT-5-mini judge prefers AC3's next turn over both full context and AO in every configuration of our main table, though this preference depends on the judge; on CollabLLM results are mixed. In stateful tool use (tau2-bench), AO collapses to 0% on every model; AC3 does not collapse, though it falls slightly behind full context. Detector studies show that Reset removes injected pollution but is not span-selective: the gain comes from rebuilding the specification.

title: Simulation analysis of a direct/indirect conversion dual-layer X-ray detector for early identification of coronary artery calcium
abstract: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a strong predictor of future cardiovascular events, and CAC burden is commonly used to stratify patient cardiovascular risk. Although CAC is typically quantified using computed tomography, routine chest radiography offers an opportunity for lower-dose, widely available opportunistic screening. Single-exposure dual-energy chest radiography using multilayer flat-panel detectors can generate low- and high-energy images without motion artifacts and provide material decomposition parameters, including calcification density. In this work, we investigate a direct/indirect dual-layer detector consisting of an amorphous selenium (a-Se) direct-conversion top layer and a cesium iodide scintillator-based indirect-conversion bottom layer for enhanced visualization of small CAC. A cascaded linear systems model (CLSM) simulated task-based detectability for a 1 mm calcification embedded in soft tissue. A complementary image-domain contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) analysis using CT-derived patient anatomy with inserted 1 mm calcifications evaluated CNR as a function of a-Se thickness and dual-energy weighting factor. The CLSM analysis revealed peak task-based detectability at an a-Se thickness of 500-550 um and a tissue-cancellation weighting factor of 1.08. Detectability remained within a few percent of this maximum across a broad range of a-Se thicknesses (300-1000 um). The image-domain CNR analysis yielded maximum CNR at 300 um a-Se and weighting factor of 0.93, with a smaller range of 200-500 um giving acceptable CNR. These results indicate that near-equal weighting of the two detector layers improves anatomical-noise suppression and CAC conspicuity, while a 300 um a-Se top layer provides a practical design compromise between detectability, operating voltage, and manufacturability.

title: Ground States of a Coupled Fractional Schrödinger System under a Total-Mass Constraint: Complete Classification and Concentration Behavior
abstract: We consider a coupled fractional Schrödinger system with trapping potentials under a total-mass constraint, in which both the intraspecies and the interspecies interactions are attractive. For every fractional order $s\in(0,1)$ and dimension $N\ge1$, we obtain a complete classification of the existence and non-existence of minimizers: minimizers exist if and only if both intraspecies coefficients lie below the single-component critical mass and the interspecies coupling coefficient lies below an explicit critical threshold $β^*$, and no minimizer exists otherwise. The threshold $β^*$ is characterized by means of an auxiliary intensity function, which yields a lower bound for the energy functional without invoking a new coupled Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. As the coupling coefficient approaches $β^*$, we analyze the concentration behavior. In the one-dimensional half-Laplacian case, the two components are shown to blow up at a common zero of the trapping potentials and, after rescaling, to converge to the same fractional ground-state profile, with the mass ratio determined explicitly by the intraspecies coefficients and the critical mass. For polynomial trapping potentials whose flattest common zero has order $q_0\in(0,1)$, the sharp blow-up rate is established, and both components concentrate simultaneously at the flattest common minimum.

title: Optimal Estimation in Weak Value Amplification with a Position Pointer
abstract: We experimentally evaluate five estimators for weak-value amplification (WVA) using a position pointer to measure birefringence time delays. Two general approaches are considered: measuring the position shift $Δx$ and measuring the probability change $ΔP_w$ of successful postselection. Specifically, five estimators are investigated: CCD-detected fringe shift $Δx$, quadrant photodiode (PDQ) transversal voltage difference (XDIFF), and lock-in amplifier output phase $η$ (for $Δx$ measurement), as well as PDQ total output voltage (SUM) and CCD-detected average photon number $N_r$ (for $ΔP_w$ measurement). The measurement precision is characterized by the Allan deviation over a range of input laser powers $P_0$. Generally, measuring the position shift $Δx$ yields higher precision than measuring the probability change $ΔP_w$. At $P_0=0.5$~mW, corresponding to a laser-power-limited regime, direct measurement of the fringe displacement with the CCD achieves a minimum Allan deviation of $(5.30\pm0.10)\times10^{-3}$~as, approaching the corresponding photon-statistical Cramér--Rao bound (CRB). At $P_0=50$~mW, corresponding to a detector-limited regime, PDQ detection combined with lock-in demodulation provides the best precision, reaching $(1.80\pm0.06)\times10^{-3}$~as and remaining close to the corresponding CRB. These results demonstrate that the optimal readout depends on the available optical power, detector dynamic range, and technical noise, providing practical guidance for selecting readout strategies in high-precision WVA-based metrology.

title: Behavioral Steering of Vision-Language-Action Models in the Low-Parameter Regime
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to adapt pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs). We investigate the problem of behavioral steering: adapting a VLA's execution style to preferences such as carrying objects higher. To investigate how little trainable capacity such steering requires and how much pretrained capability can be retained, we freeze an OpenVLA-OFT 7B policy and optimize TinyLoRA adapters with 8 to 384 trainable parameters using either policy-gradient RL (GRPO) or evolutionary search (CMA-ES). With just 256 trainable parameters, we raise carry height by 120 mm on trained tasks at 92% success and by 74 mm on a held-out task at 80% success. By rescaling the learned update, we can tune the trade-off between style gains and capability retention without retraining. Increasing adapter capacity generally improves this trade-off, retaining more pretrained capability at comparable style gains. The choice of optimizer also depends on capacity, with CMA-ES being competitive at low parameter counts, while GRPO offers better trade-offs as capacity grows. These findings show that extremely low-dimensional updates can steer pretrained VLA behavior, with adapter capacity, optimizer choice, and update scaling offering practical control over adaptation and retention.

title: SASFormer: Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
abstract: All-in-one image restoration aims to recover high-quality images from multiple degradation types using a single unified model. Recent methods improve unified restoration with hybrid attention, prompt learning, or routing mechanisms, but generally focus on enhancing degradation adaptivity while employing similar feature modeling strategies across network stages. Consequently, the distinct representation requirements of encoding and decoding under diverse degradations remain insufficiently explored. In this paper, we propose SASFormer, a Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for all-in-one blind image restoration. SASFormer follows a stage-aware design principle: the encoder uses established hybrid channel-spatial attention to build robust content-preserving and degradation-aware representations, while the decoder employs adaptive selective attention for restoration-oriented reconstruction. To address the stage-specific requirements of decoder reconstruction, we develop Adaptive Selective Channel Self-Attention (ASCSA) and Adaptive Selective Spatial Self-Attention (ASSSA), enabling the decoder to dynamically identify restoration-relevant channel responses and spatial contexts. Specifically, ASCSA performs adaptive query-channel selection and attention masking, while ASSSA adaptively integrates spatial attention across multiple window sizes. Compact implicit prompts further modulate the selection process without requiring explicit degradation labels. Extensive experiments on 3-, 5-, and 11-degradation settings demonstrate that SASFormer achieves strong restoration performance with favorable parameter efficiency. Moreover, stage-wise representation analysis and ablation studies provide empirical support for the proposed stage-aware design and the effectiveness of decoder-side adaptive selection.

title: Reflex: Fast Robot Policy Serving by Reusing and Correcting Past Actions
abstract: Modern robot policies often perform expensive inference to generate action chunks, making serving a latency bottleneck for real-time control and a throughput bottleneck for multi-robot serving. Building on the success of caching in image, video, and audio generation, recent robot-policy advances have reported promising speedups by reusing intermediate denoising states to avoid redundant computation. Surprisingly, we find that such reuse often offers little advantage over simply running fewer denoising steps from fresh noise, without any cache. Moreover, accelerating denoising leaves the expensive policy backbone intact, which can account for 70% of GPU time. We present Reflex, a serving layer that turns past policy executions into a backbone-free path for future decisions. Rather than reusing intermediate computations, Reflex caches complete action chunks to bypass both the backbone and action head. This introduces two challenges: similar observations can demand different actions, and small action deviations (errors) in reuse can compound into execution stalls. Reflex addresses these through two-level cache correction. At the action level, it learns action-aware similarity from past policy decisions, assembles compatible chunks, and applies lightweight residual correction to limit action mismatch. At the execution level, it captures task progress and adaptively refreshes the original policy to limit accumulated errors and balance inference cost. Without modifying the underlying policy, Reflex improves inference latency by 1.4x to 11x and throughput by 2.0x to 2.2x on representative workloads and real robots, while preserving comparable task success.

title: A power-saving asymptotic for a Möbius-weighted GCD quadratic form
abstract: For the Möbius-weighted quadratic form $T(N)=\sum_{m,n\leq N}μ(m)μ(n)(m,n)^2/(mn)$, we prove that $T(N)=cN+O_{\varepsilon}(N^{2/3+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $c>0$ is given by an absolutely convergent series of finite Möbius sums multiplied by a convergent Euler product. The proof combines the classical Jordan-totient decomposition of the GCD kernel with a mean-value estimate that is uniform in a coprimality parameter. Grouping the resulting squares according to $\lfloor N/d\rfloor$ gives the error term and a nonnegative series for $c$.

title: Constraint Qualifications and Regularity Conditions for Nonlinear Constraint Systems
abstract: Constraint qualifications (CQs) and regularity conditions (RCs) play a fundamental role in establishing global iteration and oracle complexity results for first-order methods on solving functional constrained optimization problems. Various conditions have been proposed and employed in the literature, with their validity established for different classes of applications. However, the use of different conditions across existing studies makes it difficult to directly compare their theoretical results and underlying assumptions. In this report, we systematically review several widely used CQs and RCs and investigate their relationships. In particular, we establish implications among these conditions and identify cases in which the implications are strict, thereby clarifying their relative strengths. Our results provide a unified perspective on existing regularity assumptions and offer guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in the complexity analysis of first-order methods.

title: 3D Neural Rendering for Automated Ultrasonic Laser Scans
abstract: Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

title: Physics-informed X-ray tomography of magnetization and material parameters
abstract: Three-dimensional spin textures are stabilized by microscopic interactions within their host materials. X-ray vector tomography can image these nanoscale structures, but weak magnetic contrast and a limited range of viewing angles often leave parts of the magnetization poorly determined. Here we show that a reconstruction constrained by the micromagnetic energy recovers the three-dimensional magnetization from such data and gains sensitivity to the underlying material interactions. Applied to the chiral magnet Co$_8$Zn$_9$Mn$_3$, the method resolves the three-dimensional helical texture even from a small fraction of the dual-axis projections typically required for a successful tomographic reconstruction, or from a single tilt axis alone. By testing which ratio of exchange to Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in the reconstruction best reproduces the measured projections, we obtain a value for the sample that differs by about 10 % from the literature value derived from the helical winding period. Taken together, our findings suggest a way to reduce the time needed for vector tomography and to extend it to determining fundamental magnetic interactions in a material.

title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
abstract: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. A comparison of results from Geant4 and FLUKA Monte Carlo simulations are presented. We perform detailed Monte Carlo simulations of muons reaching the underground SNOLAB environment using both Geant4 and FLUKA to study the production of radioactive isotopes from both direct spallation reactions or subsequent neutron-induced reactions. We find that, of the isotopes produced, the only one of concern for nEXO is $^{137}$Xe, produced by neutron capture on the xenon target. We develop a veto strategy that achieves an anticipated 92\% \xe{137} rejection efficiency while keeping dead time to less than 1 day over a 10 year exposure.

title: WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search
abstract: We present WeSearch, a unified, model-centric retrieval framework for large-scale, continuously evolving content search. Prevailing methods assign documents fixed hierarchical Semantic IDs, implicitly assuming each document follows a single coherent semantic path-an assumption that often breaks down for multi-topic documents. WeSearch instead retrieves query-relevant clusters and then ranks atomic documents within the resulting query-specific candidate space, decoupling candidate pruning from fine-grained relevance modeling. Combined with relevance-aware training, compact document representations, and incremental index updates, this design enables weekly-or daily when needed-model refreshes. Deployed as the primary semantic retrieval path in WeChat Search alongside a lexical syntax tree, WeSearch shows consistent one-week A/B gains on corpora from hundreds of millions to billions of documents, and a one-month full-traffic A/B test confirms stable improvements of +0.68% CTR and +2.27% per-user article clicks, together with a 41% reduction in retrieval resource cost and a 19 ms reduction in graphic-text retrieval latency. WeSearch is now fully deployed in WeChat Search, serving 100% of production traffic.

title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.

title: When Does Spatial Cooperation Help? Contamination Regimes in Decentralized Online Spectrum Anomaly Learning
abstract: Learning-based spectrum monitors adapt online to benign propagation changes, but persistent rogue transmissions can gradually become incorporated into the learned background. Spatially distributed receivers provide additional evidence for detecting such anomalies, while decentralized model mixing can also spread contamination to receivers with clean measurements. We study this tradeoff using a decentralized online learner with sample gating and model sharing. We show that, without defenses, contamination propagation is governed by the occupancy rate and is independent of cross-receiver correlation. In contrast, the benefit of spatial fusion depends strongly on correlation and the detector operating point, so cooperation can either improve or degrade detection. We also show that fragmented transmissions can evade gating based on temporally smoothed statistics. Combining smoothed and per-sample gating substantially improves robustness to such intermittent contamination.

title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
abstract: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML). Importantly, incorporating ML-predicted charge transfer as an input feature to a subsequent ML model enables physics-informed predictions of binding energies. Additional DFT calculations on four representative cases were performed to validate the ML predictions. SHAP analysis reveals that the majority of key descriptors are associated with delocalized electrons, highlighting the role of electronic properties in governing binding strength. Combined DFT and ML screening identifies 65 and 73 promising boride surfaces for the v1/6 and v1/9 phases, respectively. Al- and Ag-based borides, including AlB2 and AgB2, emerge as predominant candidates for both phases. The computationally predicted candidate substrates and the deduced design guidelines provide a charge-transfer-informed ML strategy for substrate selection and represent promising steps toward the experimental realization of freestanding borophene.

title: Nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity driven by charge fluctuations in monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$
abstract: Monolayer FeSe and Fe(Te,Se) grown on SrTiO$_3$ exhibit some of the highest superconducting transition temperatures among iron-based superconductors, yet their pairing mechanism and symmetry remain elusive. Motivated by the recent surprising discovery of nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM) [T. Wei et al., arXiv:2610.38421 (2026)], we investigate superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$3$ (1L-FeSe/STO) within an extended Hubbard model incorporating both onsite and intersite Coulomb interactions among Fe $3d$ and Se $4p$ orbitals. We show that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion strongly enhances small-momentum $p$-$d$ charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate attractive intraorbital spin-singlet pairing interactions. These electronic fluctuations may be further enhanced by forward-scattering optical phonons of the SrTiO$3$ substrate. The resulting intrapocket attraction, together with residual repulsive interpocket interactions, stabilizes a mirror-odd, nodeless $B_{1g}$ ($d$-wave) superconducting state with opposite gap signs on the two electron pockets. Both Fe $t_{2g}$ and Se $4p$ orbitals contribute substantially to this multiorbital superconductivity. The calculated superconducting gap and density of states exhibit a two-peak structure, while the Josephson tunneling conductance displays a half-lattice-period modulation, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. Our results establish electronic charge-transfer fluctuations as a viable pairing mechanism for unconventional nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/STO.

title: Dynamic programming principle for controlled systems driven by fractional Brownian motions and related backward stochastic Riccati equations
abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.

title: Dual-Axis Policy Entailment: A Benchmark for Policy-Change Reasoning
abstract: Whether a policy shifts domains and, by extension, continues, broadens, narrows, or reverses previous policy is of paramount importance to the study of public policy. We propose Dual-Axis Policy Entailment (DAPE), which evaluates an ordered pair of policy directives on both dimensions at once: a binary judgment determines whether the two directives govern the same policy domain, and a five-way judgment determines whether the later directive continues, broadens, narrows, or reverses the earlier policy, or governs a different domain altogether. Read together, the two judgments form one five-category label, our primary metric. The two-axis design captures two central dimensions of policy change without conflating errors on either dimension into a generic "irrelevant" label, and it makes annotation more rigorous: a coder cannot dismiss a difficult pair as domain-irrelevant without an explicit, checkable decision. We introduce an expert-annotated benchmark of 1,000 ordered directive pairs drawn from a large corpus of Chinese government policy, together with an annotation-calibration protocol (an adjudication packet with pre/post agreement measurement) that we contribute as a methodological artifact. Fourteen open-weight models and four frontier API flagships fail the task zero-shot: even the best frontier flagship's chance-corrected agreement with expert labels is far below the human ceiling (Cohen's $κ\approx 0.29$ vs. $0.53$). A fine-tuned open-weight model (LoRA SFT of Qwen3-14B, five-fold cross-validation) closes this gap, reaching the coder-mutual human ceiling ($κ= 0.524$ vs. $0.527$). Finally, we apply our method to China's AI policy (1980-2024) and map the direction of policy change across eras.

title: Gravitational Capture of Large Interstellar Planetesimals by Collapsing Prestellar Cores
abstract: We investigate the capture of free-floating planetesimals by the time-varying gravitational potential of a collapsing prestellar core. We use one-dimensional collapse models to estimate the volume of space from which planetesimals are captured. We combine this calculation with an estimate of the size distribution and velocity dispersion of the free-floating planetesimal population to determine the largest planetesimal that is typically captured, as well as the total mass of all planetesimals captured by a given protostar. We consider two cases: one in which the free-floating planetesimal population comes from the birth cluster of the star, and one in which the planetesimals are captured from the Galactic population of free-floating planetesimals. We find that the details of the collapse matter substantially, with the predicted diameter of the largest captured body from the Galactic population ranging from $2.8$ km to $6.4$ km depending on collapse model, and the largest body from our model birth cluster environment ranging from $70$ km to $1200$ km, for assumed velocity dispersions ranging from 0.7 to 8.5 km/s. The total solid mass captured by this mechanism does not exceed 0.07 Earth masses in all cases. We discuss the effect of these captured objects on the planet formation process, and argue that while the total solid mass captured is likely not significant, the largest captured bodies may grow to planet size via accretion of pebbles present in their host disks. This process may accelerate planet formation, or enable it in disks that have difficulty in forming their own planetesimals.

title: Robust Inference for Spiked Eigenspace under Elliptical Distributions
abstract: In this paper, we study two eigenspace testing problems under high-dimensional elliptical spiked models: whether the spiked eigenspace equals a given subspace, and whether a given vector is a spike eigenvector. We propose a \textbf{Robust Functional Projection} (RFP) test and a \textbf{Robust Spike Direction} (RSD) test for these two problems, respectively. Based on the spatial-sign covariance matrix $\bm C_n$, both tests achieve robustness by remaining invariant to the radial distribution without moment conditions and allowing the background level to be unknown. To construct and analyze both tests, we establish central limit theorems for \textbf{G}eneralized \textbf{E}lliptical \textbf{S}patial-sign \textbf{S}pectral statistics (GESS) $\operatorname{tr}\{f(\bm C_n)\bm B_n\}$. The results cover a general class of deterministic weighting matrices $\bm B_n$ whose ranks are either comparable to the dimension or of smaller order, providing a common theoretical foundation for both tests. The central idea in constructing both tests is to avoid the need for consistent estimations of individual spike eigenvalues by working directly with GESS. Simulations illustrate the finite-sample performance of the procedures, and an analysis of LOCATA acoustic data demonstrates their use in assessing a signal subspace and a steering direction, both constructed from measured source and array geometry.

title: Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit
abstract: Imitation policies inherit the operator's pace, and re-timing the demonstrations to run faster works only until success collapses at two to three times demonstration speed. Recent methods attribute that collapse to distribution shift and answer it with finer rules for which segments may be sped up; we show it has a mechanical cause that segment selection cannot address. A low-level controller realises only a bounded displacement per control period, so merging consecutive commands produces sums outside that bound: training pairs that promise a transition the plant cannot deliver. The share of such pairs in the re-timed data, which we call the exceed share, tracks where the retrained policy collapses. The rule that follows has a single parameter: merge greedily while the sum stays realisable. Every command is then realisable by construction, the demonstrated geometry is preserved, and the speed-up lands only where the demonstrator left slack. On four simulated robomimic tasks, 200 held-out seeds per cell, a merge cap of two is at or above the frozen policy's success on all four, by 14 points on Square, and shortens the successful episodes. At matched tempo, uniform re-timing loses 9 and 16 points on Can and ToolHang, is within noise on the other two, and reaches zero on the hardest at 2x. Placement also matters: no shuffled, entropy-guided or speed-conditioned alternative beats the rule on three of the four tasks, by margins the exceed share alone does not explain; on the fourth, at a tempo the task absorbs, every placement lands in the same band. The same principle carries to a simulated humanoid whole-body tracker: re-timing 429 reference motions within its velocity envelope succeeds on 71% of clips at 2.3x, against 51% for uniform time scaling at 2x.

title: RIXS study of strain-tuned coupled valence and spin-state transition in epitaxial $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ films
abstract: Strain-tuned $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. Here, we use Co $L_{2,3}$ and Pr $M_{4,5}$ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), along with Co $L_{3}$ edge Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS), to probe the local electronic structure across the strain-controlled VSST in epitaxial (Pr,Y,Ca)CoO$_{3}$ thin films. In compressively strained films on YAlO$_{3}$ (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr$^{4+}$-like spectral weight, suppresses Co$^{4+}$-like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co$^{3+}$. The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co--O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La$_{0.18}$Sr$_{0.82}$Al$_{0.59}$Ta$_{0.41}$O$_{3}$ (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local $dd$ excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co$^{4+}$-like local excitations and a broader particle--hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co--O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.

title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
abstract: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric Pöschl-Teller problem. This yields the exact threshold spectrum $ ζ_{n\ell}=(n+\ell+1)^2/2 $, closed-form Gegenbauer profiles, and an exact count of negative radial eigenvalues in each angular sector. The s-wave thresholds are zero-energy resonances at which the growth rate rises linearly, whereas the $ \ell \geq1\ $ threshold states are square integrable and the growth rate rises as a square root. At the first threshold we also obtain the next-order term, $ σa=(π/4)g-(3π/16)g^2+O(g^3) $ with $g=2ζ-1 $. For a probe field with quartic self-interaction, we show that no nontrivial spherical static solution exists for $ζ\leq1/2 $ and derive local branch expansions near the s-wave thresholds. Numerical evolutions are consistent with saturation on the nodeless branch. These nonlinear results refer to the probe-field model; they do not establish the existence or stability of fully backreacted scalarized wormholes.

title: Multiplicity and Uniqueness of Stationary Expected Payoffs in Coalitional Bargaining
abstract: I study uniqueness of stationary expected payoffs in random-proposer coalitional bargaining with transferable utility. Proposer independence of coalition surplus does not guarantee uniqueness, even when the surplus is strictly monotone and every equilibrium features immediate agreement. For $M^\natural$-concave characteristic functions, including non-monotone ones, I show that stationary expected payoffs are unique and continuous in the primitives, provided that every equilibrium features immediate agreement. To prove uniqueness, I identify an equitable grouping property of maximizing coalitions and show that $M^\natural$-concavity implies it at every no-delay candidate payoff vector. Using equitable grouping, I show that every no-delay equilibrium payoff vector is isolated and has positive local index. For parameter changes that preserve immediate agreement in every equilibrium, a uniform increase in a player's contribution to every coalition containing her strictly increases her expected payoff, while an increase in her discount factor weakly increases it. I apply these results to joint ventures with coordination costs and government formation with ministerial expertise.

title: FIXP-Completeness in Second-Price Auctions
abstract: Computing equilibria is a fundamental algorithmic problem in game theory and economics. Although general frameworks are available for proving membership in FIXP, the class capturing exact fixed-point computation, establishing FIXP-completeness often remains challenging. We prove FIXP-completeness of exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models: (1). pacing with return-on-investment constraints, with multiplier cap $1+δ$ for every fixed rational $δ>0$ [Filos-Ratsikas, Hansen, Høgh, and Hollender (2024)]; (2). budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping [Hansen, Li, and Nie (2026)]; (3). budget-constrained throttling [Liu (2026)]. These results resolve open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding. Our technical ingredient is a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem using only clipped affine gates and the reciprocal $x\mapsto1/(1+τx)$, for any fixed positive rational $τ$. This gate basis provides a common framework for the three auction reductions: simulating these gates in each model establishes FIXP-hardness without directly implementing multiplication or squaring.

title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents extend their capabilities with skills, each with a name, a description, and a body. Under progressive disclosure, an LLM router selects skills by name and description alone and loads only the selected bodies. Skill libraries grow continually as users and agents add new skills. Because the router relies on this metadata, a similar new skill can displace an earlier one, breaking previously correct routing even though the earlier skill and the router are unchanged. This routing interference is aggravated for public skills, whose descriptions may not match their bodies. We formulate the problem as lifelong skill routing, a class-incremental continual learning problem. A solution must keep earlier skills selectable without suppressing new ones. Existing approaches fall short, since continually retraining the router risks catastrophic forgetting and rewriting methods either ignore similar skills or require per-skill feedback. We therefore propose Skill++, which rewrites only the name and description of each incoming skill, without router training or labeled data. The new description states what the body supports, how the skill differs from its closest predecessor, and what related work it excludes. As a library grows to 731 skills over ten sessions, Skill++ selects all required skills for 76.3% of queries, versus 36.4% under the original metadata. Across three benchmarks and five LLM routers, it outperforms all compared approaches, and its gains carry over to the Codex CLI agent harness.

title: The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem and Dynamical Love Number in Schwarzschild Black Holes
abstract: We study the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to an external massless scalar field. Using a complexified radial contour to represent the Schwinger-Keldysh closed time path, we describe dissipation, thermal fluctuations and conservative tidal response within a common framework. Before performing tidal matching, we derive the equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation relation directly from the radial construction for every scalar multipole at arbitrary real frequency. In the low-frequency tidal expansion, we recover the known relation between the logarithmic running of the conservative dynamical Love coefficient at order $ω^2$ and the leading dissipative response at order $ω$. We explain how the same leading absorptive coefficient enters both relations at low frequency and trace the unit coefficient of the running relation to the Schwarzschild horizon slope. In the Hartle-Hawking state, this common coefficient relates the logarithmic running directly to the zero-frequency thermal noise. Kubo-Martin-Schwinger analyticity determines the thermal noise from the dissipative response, whereas the near-zone radial equation and tidal matching determine the conservative logarithmic running.

title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberatio
abstract: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch substantially more often than margin-increasing con- trols. We then continue selected realized branches through the committee to distinguish textual persistence from preference and final-decision changes. The contribution is a controlled audit for local branch susceptibility in this specified protocol, not an estimate of deployment frequency, decision correct- ness, or a phenomenon unique to multi-agent systems.

title: BitLLM: Efficient Low-Bit, Conversion-Hiding LLM Decoding on Mobile GPUs
abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) has unlocked remarkable capabilities across various domains. However, deploying LLMs on mobile devices remains challenging because of their high computational and memory requirements. Low-bit quantization (e.g., 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) can reduce model size while preserving accuracy, but its practical efficacy on mobile GPUs has been limited so far. In this paper, we identify that the performance gap stems primarily from frequent data type conversions between quantized and floating-point values, and dynamic and inefficient memory access patterns caused by the growing Key-Value (KV) cache during autoregressive decoding. We introduce BitLLM, a mobile inference engine that addresses type conversion overhead and suboptimal memory accesses in quantized LLMs. Our approach features an adaptive layout and packing strategy for the KV cache that ensures efficient memory access throughout LLM decoding. This is coupled with an integer-native execution pipeline that defers and overlaps type conversion outside the compute hot path, keeping the critical MatMul stages in the integer domain. Implemented on off-the-shelf mobile GPUs, BitLLM outperforms leading engines, i.e., LLAMA.CPP, MNN-LLM, LiteRT-LM, and MLC-LLM, achieving average speedups of 1.78$\times$, 1.73$\times$, 1.58$\times$, and 1.47$\times$, respectively, across various models and quantization levels. Under long-context generation, BitLLM reduces average energy consumption (per token) by up to 88.9%.

title: Elucidating the topological nature of molecular beam epitaxy grown high Curie temperature (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is used to elucidate the band structure of (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x, a new magnetic quantum material grown using molecular beam epitaxy that has a Curie temperature (TC) above 100K, much higher than those reported for other materials of the MnxSb2-xTe4 class. Conflicting and sparse theory and experiments, as well as the complex disordered structure of the materials make it difficult to establish their topological nature. Here we explore this question by performing ARPES studies for two samples with x=0.65 and x=0.92, respectively. Images of the band structures of these two samples were acquired using photon energy dependent studies. The bulk and surface states of this complex material system, and the effects of composition on the band structure were investigated. Evidence of surface state features as well as bulk related ones were obtained, supporting their non-trivial nature. No signature of Fermi-arcs consistent with Weyl semimetals were seen. A shift in the Fermi level of the two samples due to different carrier densities allowed observation of the onset of a Dirac point in the surface states. Temperature dependent ARPES suggests possible band splitting as the materials undergo magnetic transitions, helping to understand the magnetic interactions. Our results point to their likely magnetic topological insulating nature.

title: Characterizing Estimator-Regime Transitions in Adaptive Enrichment Trials
abstract: Adaptive enrichment trials that identify responsive subpopulations allocate a fixed sample across them and estimate each one's effect from the resulting data. For a synthetic control design with adaptive recruitment and borrowing of control outcomes, we ask whether a doubly robust family of targeted maximum likelihood estimators should replace its sample mean; the choice can be made largely at the design stage. A crossing condition weighs the bias removed and the efficiency gained by the doubly robust family against the finite-sample inflation of nuisance estimation; an equal-error boundary, located by simulation, separates the families in the plane of sample size and bias. A consistency principle prices recruiting with the wrong family's variance functional. With three and eight simulated subpopulations the boundary's sign prediction for the mean squared error difference holds in $99.6\%$ of $10{,}302$ comparisons decided at two standard errors. A pre-specified selector commits to the doubly robust family where the squared anticipated bias exceeds the net variance term. Recruiting along that family's path costs up to $0.035$ in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; recruiting with the sample mean functional and routing only the analysis removes this cost and about nine tenths of its error excess.

title: Governing Equations of Human Sleep Macro-Structure:Symbolic Discovery from 1,106 Nights
abstract: Human sleep is organized into a small number of cycles per night: deep sleep dominates early cycles, REM lengthens toward morning, and light sleep clusters at cycle boundaries. These regularities have long been described qualitatively but never distilled into closed-form laws from large-scale data. A total of 1,106 nights (Sleep-EDF 153 + SHHS 953) are segmented into REM-anchored cycles, and four cycle-indexed statistics follow simple closed-form equations: cycle length declines nearly linearly (R^2=0.996), REM duration follows an inverted U (R^2=0.873), deep-sleep (N3) run length decays exponentially (R^2=0.987) with a time constant of 2.94 cycles, consistent with the homeostatic Process S of the two-process model, and light-sleep (N1) run length follows a U shape (R^2=0.956), confirming a "long-short-long" pattern across the night. The laws are reproduced by per-night differentiable fitting (142/142 and 773/773 nights converge), by unconstrained symbolic regression (PySR), and by a 500-night generative synthesizer built from them. Their robustness is established against the two main methodological threats: bootstrap CIs computed by resampling whole nights (1,000 replications) exclude zero for every shape term, and a five-level scan of the REM-merge segmentation threshold preserves every qualitative form. These appear to be the first closed-form laws governing the macro-structure of sleep, distilled and tested across an age-mixed sample (healthy young adults and community-based older adults).

title: RATR: Training-Free Material Rebinding via Role Assignment and Temporal Routing
abstract: Material rebinding aims to transfer the material appearance from a reference image while preserving the target object's geometry and identity. Existing methods typically struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation due to the coupled influence of structural and appearance cues in their visual conditions. We identify role entanglement in the target and reference conditions as a contributing factor the target condition carries both geometry and its original appearance while the reference condition contains material cues alongside object-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose RATR, a training-free material rebinding method built on a diffusion-based image editor that assigns complementary roles to the two conditions and coordinates their influence during denoising. To make the target condition primarily convey structure, we introduce an albedo-resolved surface release mechanism, which suppresses the target's original surface appearance while retaining geometric cues, yielding a structure-oriented condition for material transfer. On the reference side, the designed material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues while reducing interference from object-specific structure, yielding a complementary material-oriented condition.

title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.1-2.6$\times$.

title: Efficient Causal Survival Inference under Limited Surrogate Monitoring
abstract: Post-treatment surrogate endpoints can improve the efficiency of causal survival effect estimation, but their monitoring may end before follow-up for the primary outcome. We investigate the impact of limited recurrence monitoring on semiparametric efficiency when mortality follow-up continues. We derive the efficient influence function under limited monitoring and establish an exact expression for the efficiency gain from extending monitoring between any two durations. Our framework encompasses the absence of surrogate information and the usual shared-censoring scheme as boundary cases, and allows comparison with fully observed surrogates. We develop a doubly robust estimator under limited surrogate monitoring and establish asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency for its cross-fitted version under suitable conditions. Simulations and an application to breast cancer data illustrate the proposed method.

title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
abstract: Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often requiring weeks of computation. In this work, we propose SFTProbe, a fundamentally different approach that bypasses this pipeline by directly predicting the quality of reasoning data. We show that a brief LoRA-based adaptation, combined with evaluating loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace, suffices to estimate both difficulty and diversity. SFTProbe is grounded in a geometric view of post-training, where pretrained LLMs lie in a low-rank, anisotropic loss basin. By probing this basin via low-rank perturbations, we construct compact loss signatures whose clustering captures diversity, while loss at curvature inflection points provides a robust proxy for difficulty. We also provide a simple criterion for teacher selection. Empirically, our approach reduces data curation time from weeks to hours while maintaining or improving performance. Remarkably, on mathematical reasoning, 5k generated examples match the highly filtered 89k-example in OpenThoughts-Math dataset, and 7.5k generated examples outperforms it by 2.5% in accuracy. We further introduce a high-quality physics reasoning dataset, and use it to train a model that outperforms an IPhO 2025 silver-medal-winning model. The code and the dataset are released at https://bigml-cs-ucla.github.io/SFTProbe-page/.

title: Distinguishing among reasoning levels of GPT 5.5 Pro via a grammar lens benchmark
abstract: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. Using this data, we tested GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.5-Pro-Medium, -High, and -XHigh, showing incrementally increased acceptance of test data: 16, 40, 43, and 52\%, respectively, illustrating the benchmark's ability to discern fine-grained differences among models' added test-time reasoning levels. Additionally, as test-time compute effort increases, model responses diverge from human responses to the same data. This increasing disagreement may turn out to be broadly characteristic of more capable language models, introducing the potential of a general capability-versus-alignment conflict.

title: Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation
abstract: Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem. By unfolding the classical iterative solver, our network integrates physical consistency with dual-domain deep priors via learned transforms, soft thresholding, and exact data reinsertion. Within the learned prior, a spatial Restormer branch captures local waveform structures, while a fast Fourier convolution (FFC) branch extracts global context, effectively suppressing incoherent components and enhancing spectral energy concentration in the $f-k$ domain. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges these complementary features via bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation, yielding substantial interpolation improvements. To overcome the severe loss of lateral continuity caused by large gaps, we introduce structural similarity (SSIM) supervision, complemented by focal frequency loss (FFL) and transform consistency constraints to suppress incoherent high-frequency components and regularize training. Experiments on a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset under 50% random and consecutive trace removal demonstrate the effectiveness of SSI-POCS. It significantly enhances event continuity across large gaps and mitigates artifacts, achieving a 3.285~dB SNR improvement over the best competing method while reducing parameters by 75.66%.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Development: Building Rigorous, Decision-Ready Evidence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the pharmaceutical lifecycle, from discovery and clinical development through manufacturing and regulatory review to safety surveillance and health economics, creating evidentiary challenges that predictive performance alone cannot address. This review examines the inferential, causal, validation, and documentation requirements for AI-enabled evidence generation in high-stakes settings and argues that they must be built into workflows. We outline the evidentiary functions that AI-derived outputs must satisfy before supporting consequential decisions: estimand definition, fit-for-purpose data collection, bias control, uncertainty quantification, validation, interpretability, and decision-grade documentation. Because AI both depends on and accelerates large-scale, non-randomized data collection, the integration of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with real-world data (RWD) is where its evidentiary risks concentrate; we therefore present a five-step causal roadmap for that integration, in which external data supplement but never replace a concurrent control, and characterize the safeguards required across development, pharmacovigilance, regulation, and health technology assessment. Priority frontiers answer recurring implementation problems: conformal prediction for overconfident predictions, randomization-based inference for scarce data, and federated causal inference and privacy-preserving generative modeling for data that cannot be pooled. Evidence generation depends not on competition between RCTs and RWD, or between statistics and AI/ML, but on their principled synthesis under causal and inferential frameworks, with statistical expertise central to decision-ready evidence.

title: Can agents reliably design therapeutic antibodies?
abstract: Recent work has demonstrated agents driving protein design workflows, either through orchestration of specialized tools or direct manipulation of sequences. Yet the fidelity with which agents follow protein design instructions and the factors contributing to their effectiveness remain understudied. We examine agentic antibody design under two settings: when explicit molecular-editing instructions are provided and when agents receive only previously-scored sequences and are prompted to propose improvements. We call the first task-guided and the second black-box design. For the task-guided setting, we curate ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and show that LLM judges closely reproduce programmatic evaluations of instruction following. We then study two augmentations: access to antibody-relevant tools and to previously scored design history. Tools improve instruction following (IF) and sequence space exploration while reducing optimization performance, whereas design history reduces IF but improves optimization performance at the expense of exploration. Finally, we combine taskguided and black-box design within an in silico optimization loop and show that our agentic optimizer performs comparably to an established Bayesian optimization baseline.

title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
abstract: We study the Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow of the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model, a four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory with chirally invariant four-Fermi interactions, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group~(GFERG). Our gauge-invariant ansatz (truncation) for the 1PI Wilson action keeps a general photon kinetic function~$\mathcal{K}_τ(k^2)$, the fermion mass, and the scalar and vector four-Fermi couplings. For a fixed gauge coupling~$e^2$, the Gaussian and NJL (quasi-)fixed points on the critical surface merge at~$e_c^2\simeq17$, as anticipated by the ladder Schwinger--Dyson equation and the conventional Wilsonian renormalization group. We then let $e^2$ itself flow. Owing to the manifest gauge invariance of the GFERG, the flow of~$e^2$ is governed solely by the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$, which remains positive along both branches up to the merging point. Hence, no fixed point with~$e^2\neq0$ exists. Flows from a sufficiently large~$e^2$ in the ultraviolet (UV) reach the chirally broken phase even for vanishing four-Fermi couplings, so the gauge interaction does trigger chiral symmetry breaking. The merging point, however, is not a fixed point, and the gauge coupling vanishes in any continuum limit within our truncation.

title: RayAR: Autoregressive Dominant Path Generation for Low-Overhead MIMO Beam Alignment
abstract: Beam alignment in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems requires selecting suitable transmit and receive beam pairs with limited measurement overhead. Although 3GPP Release 18 investigates beam prediction from partial measurements, collecting these measurements still incurs probing overhead. Geometry can focus this probing through the departure and arrival directions of dominant paths, whose identification requires accounting for coupled diffraction interactions. To address this challenge, we propose RayAR, an autoregressive method that generates dominant propagation paths from urban geometry. RayAR conditions candidate ranking on the path prefix, local diffraction geometry, and receiver reachability, updating this context after each selection until the receiver becomes visible. The completed path's departure and arrival directions rank beam pairs for probing, allowing the pair with the highest received power to be selected from a small candidate set. Under 3GPP Release 18 beam-management metrics, RayAR reduces probing by 96.88\% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves the highest optimal-pair hit rate among compared methods at the same budget. Real-world measurements further demonstrate the accuracy of this geometric guidance, with simulation-trained RayAR achieving the lowest departure and arrival angular errors among compared methods without fine-tuning and a mean arrival-direction error of 9.07$^\circ$.

title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 {\textmu}m
abstract: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 {\textmu}m is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 {\textmu}m has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 {\textmu}m. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 {\textmu}m relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.

title: TabAbax: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable in-context prediction on unseen tabular datasets without task-specific training. Mechanistic work has shown that increasing the depth of the ICL Transformer yields weak gains, leaving the main headroom for gains in the synthetic pretraining prior and column-row encoder upstream of the ICL backbone. We introduce TabAbax, a TFM built on TabICLv2 that focuses all modifications on these two upstream components. On the prior side, we further improve the quality and complexity of the synthetic pretraining prior. On the encoder side, a two-pass column-row stack strengthens cross-feature interactions before row compression, using learned Fourier scalar encoding from TabFM and Causilo. Evaluations on BeyondArena and TabArena show strong regression-centric gains: TabAbax reaches 1,238 Elo on the 142-dataset BeyondArena suite (10th of 41 evaluated methods), 1,676 Elo on TabArena's overall 51-dataset suite (11th of 99 methods, +115 over TabICLv2), and 2,024 Elo on TabArena's regression benchmark (7th of 99 methods, +336 over TabICLv2, +21 over TabFM). A prior-only ablation confirms the attribution: the improved prior alone yields +228 Elo for regression, demonstrating that prior quality is the dominant knob for improving regression performance.

title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
