We formulate adaptive surface cleaning as a partially observable Markov decision process and propose a belief-aware planning framework that uses observed cleaning outcomes to update a latent local cleaning-response model and adapt subsequent cleaning motions, forces, and passes. Preliminary grid-world simulations demonstrate the resulting closed-loop planner adapting its spatial decomposition and cleaning actions as the surface evolves.

title: FOCUS: Closed-Loop Attention Feedback for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding
abstract: Processing every video frame through Vision-Language Models (VLMs) adds significant inference cost and limits their ability to comprehend real-time video. Existing approaches either sub-sample frames uniformly, ignoring content and missing important events, or prune visual tokens inside the VLM to cut per-call cost while still invoking the model on every sampled frame. We introduce FOCUS, a training-free three-layer framework that reduces the number of invocations and steers each one towards what matters. Temporal gating measures inter-frame dissimilarity in the patch-embedding space of a smaller VLM from the same family, triggering burst captures only when the scene changes in a semantically meaningful way. Patch-level dissimilarity is then accumulated across the burst and fused with a top-down attention prior into a spatial focus map that encodes where motion and semantic relevance coincide. That map calibrates the VLM's value cache during generation, progressively amplifying vision tokens in task-relevant regions and attenuating off-target ones, without removing any token from the context. The loop closes after each response: text-to-vision cross-attention is extracted from the decoder and fed back as the prior for the next burst, letting the system converge on semantically important regions over successive observations. We evaluate FOCUS on the 500-video EgoSchema subset in streaming mode, with a single Qwen3-VL-8B backbone shared by every method. It reaches 74.8% accuracy using 25.4 VLM calls per clip, against 74.6% with 55 calls for uniform sampling and 74.2% with 55 calls for BOLT. On egocentric video captioning across four domains, it matches the best baseline's quality while issuing 57% fewer VLM invocations than uniform sampling.

title: Parameters and lim CM sequences: the Q-sequence conjecture and Lech's formula
abstract: We prove that if a local ring has a weakly lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence of modules, then it satisfies the conjecture that every system of parameters is a Q-sequence. We also give a generalization of Lech's formula for the multiplicity of a local ring $(R,m)$ with respect to a system of parameters that allows a very large class of sequences of $m$-primary ideals generated by monomials in the parameters to be used in the calculation. The cases where the sequence of ideals consists of the powers of the ideal generated by parameters, or where the ideals in the sequence are generated by varying powers of the individual parameters all of which tend to infinity, which is Lech's original formula, are included.

title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

title: Renormalized Cellular Intelligence: When Does Model Reduction Preserve Collective Capability?
abstract: As multi-agent systems grow in size and complexity, understanding which features of their interactions support collective capability becomes increasingly difficult. Can a simpler description preserve both task performance and the measured contribution of interactions between agents? Preserving collective dynamics alone is insufficient: reduction can alter decision-relevant information or give a non-communicating baseline access to pooled observations, distorting the measured advantage of interaction. We introduce Renormalized Cellular Intelligence (RCI), a framework for specifying and auditing capability preservation across scales. RCI treats the task, interacting dynamics, matched baseline, decision interfaces, and resource budget as a joint object of reduction. It specifies dynamical closure, decision compatibility, and preservation of the intended baseline comparison, and bounds the resulting error in relative capability gain. An exact analytical construction demonstrates task-score preservation, while a counterexample shows how closed reduced dynamics can erase the measured interaction gain. Using cellular systems as models of locally interacting agents, we evaluate three reduction candidates on five frozen learned models without retraining. The final candidate reduces the evolving state from eight to five dimensions per cell (37.5%). Within-run uncertainty bounds support relative gain above a prespecified threshold for the fixed model collection, yet the candidate fails the closure and decision-preservation requirements for a complete RCI certificate. RCI provides explicit criteria for distinguishing positive interaction gains from

title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/

title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $π_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2π/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle τ\rangle$, where $τ$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
abstract: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{τ,δτ,τδ,δτδ\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $δ$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langleδ\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.

title: I-PTC: Interactive Programmatic Tool Calling for Stateful Tool-Augmented Agents
abstract: Large language models are increasingly capable of writing and executing code, suggesting a natural paradigm for tool-augmented agents: expressing tool use as programs rather than isolated calls. Programmatic tool calling (PTC) captures this idea through loops, batching, abstraction, and structured computation, but existing PTC approaches are largely stateless, limiting their ability to reuse intermediate results and adapt over time. This is problematic for real-world tasks, where tool environments and problem-solving processes are inherently stateful. We therefore present I-PTC, an interactive framework that executes stateful PTC: models issue code snippets that call tools, maintain reusable state, and evolve the tool interface through API corrections. To evaluate the effectiveness of I-PTC and the general PTC setting, we introduce PTC-Bench, a benchmark of long-tail, production-style user requests whose difficulty comes from large initial environments, many dependent API interactions, extended planning, and recovery across follow-ups and transient failures. Experiments on PTC-Bench show that I-PTC improves performance on complex multi-step tasks with large tool sets while substantially reducing token consumption over conventional tool-calling baselines and the original PTC baseline, highlighting stateful programmatic tool calling as a promising direction for scalable tool-augmented agents.

title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
abstract: Uncertainty estimates from fuzzy regression are informative only when the implementation is correct and the comparison protocol makes the sources of variation visible. We revisit a first-order Takagi--Sugeno--Kang (TSK) regression implementation and rebuild its dense, conjugate Bayesian, BIC-based, and rule-level spike-and-slab estimators using corrected code. The corrected pipeline freezes the Gaussian membership partition at training time, uses a scaled conjugate prior, evaluates firing strengths in the log domain, and reports direct posterior-predictive quantiles for Bayesian methods. Across 30 outer 80/20 splits on three targets from two UCI regression datasets, corrected TSK-LS obtains $R^2=0.957$, $0.923$, and $0.786$ on Energy-Heating, Energy-Cooling, and Concrete, respectively; rule-level Gibbs sampling with Bayesian model averaging obtains $0.957$, $0.922$, and $0.784$. We then evaluate the same workflow on a bounded chronological sample of the Building Data Genome 2 meter data that covers 158 buildings across 17 sites. In a common-unit evaluation, every method is scored on the same 47,400 test rows and every trained model uses 94,800 train--validation rows. Persistence has RMSE $27.710$, compared with $29.083$ for both TSK-LS and Bayesian TSK; the pre-specified building-level mean RMSE difference between Bayesian TSK and persistence is $+0.0447$ with a 95% site-cluster bootstrap interval of $[-1.5536,1.5665]$. The Bayesian TSK 90% intervals have PICP $0.980$ and MPIW $116.469$. Taken together, the evidence supports a narrower conclusion: spike-and-slab model averaging is a reproducible implementation option, but it does not provide a demonstrated accuracy or calibration advantage across the tested tabular and building-meter settings.

title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain Ωin \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (Δt=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);

title: CONFIRM: Governing Scientific Reporting for Trustworthy Agentic Neuroimaging
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can autonomously run neuroimaging analyses from research questions to reported findings. Existing agentic systems use tools to check that code runs and reported values match its output, but rely on LLM judgment to decide which results warrant scientific reporting. We show that LLM judges endorse site-confounded findings even when the confound is presented as evidence. We present \textbf{CONFIRM}, a framework that separates running an analysis from deciding which findings to report. CONFIRM encodes each hypothesis as a machine-readable, pre-specified analysis plan that fixes the claim and its pass criteria before computing results. It then filters results through five deterministic gates (search history and multiplicity, confounds, power, analytic stability, and replication) under three configurable reporting standards, from least to most demanding: \textit{Screen}, \textit{Replicate}, and \textit{Full}. Failed claims receive diagnoses that guide follow-up analyses. To evaluate reporting decisions at the claim level, we introduce \textbf{NeuroClaimBench}, comprising 489 executable neuroimaging claims with frozen data, including literature-supported findings and 150 controls designed to violate individual methodological requirements. On NeuroClaimBench, CONFIRM falsely supports at most 3\% of controls, compared with 23--38\% for the baselines, while recovering up to 61\% of literature-supported claims. When auditing an existing agent, CONFIRM reduces false support on controls from 23\% to 0\% while retaining the agent's literature-supported claims. Its diagnostic feedback also produces more supported revisions than Self-Refine with fewer LLM calls. Together, CONFIRM and NeuroClaimBench show that basing reporting decisions on pre-specified analysis plans and deterministic gates is essential for trustworthy autonomous scientific discovery.

title: CipherFlow: Compiling AI Programs for Efficient Cryptographically Secure Inference
abstract: Cryptographically secure inference faces two practical challenges: making secure programming accessible to AI developers and data scientists, and achieving efficient execution across deployment environments. Developers must compose cryptographic primitives correctly, while performance depends on hardware, networks, and evolving ciphertext states. We present CipherFlow, a compiler framework that takes a high-level AI computation graph, available cryptographic primitives, and a target hardware and network configuration to generate an executable, latency-optimized secure inference program. CipherFlow automates cryptographic execution decisions through three techniques: MicroBench profiles deployment-specific primitive costs; state-expanded planning jointly optimizes homomorphic encryption (HE) and secure multi-party computation (MPC) placement, conversions, and ciphertext maintenance under cryptographic-state constraints; and BlockFold summarizes branched regions to scale planning to Transformer graphs. Evaluation using measured HE/MPC backend costs across CPU/GPU and network settings shows up to 16.5$\times$ speedup on BERT-base and over 22$\times$ on ViT compared with static hybrid placement baselines. CipherFlow separates model programming from cryptographic execution decisions, enabling developers to express AI computations while the compiler constructs efficient secure programs.

title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet \(L\)-functions over \(\Q\) with conductors coprime to \(3\), with a main term of order \(Q\) and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order \(Q^{\frac{5}{6}}\) in the same family, with error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)\). We explicitly evaluate the secondary coefficient and prove that it is strictly negative. We also prove unconditionally that the secondary polynomial in the squarefree second moment of the natural cubic Hecke \(L\)-functions over \(\Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has degree one and strictly positive leading coefficient, which we evaluate explicitly.

title: Improved first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions
abstract: We study the smoothed first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions for which every nontrivial power of the character remains primitive. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet and finite order Hecke $L$-functions occurring in the proof, we obtain asymptotic formulas with errors $O(Q^{\frac{49}{58}+\eps})$ and $O(Q^{\frac{23}{26}+\eps})$, respectively. We follow the double Dirichlet series approach of Gao and Zhao. The main ingredient is a joint estimate for the two sums arising from the removal of rational prime divisors, with the Möbius coefficients retained. This gives a quotient of Dirichlet $L$-functions. Under GRH, we bound both the Dirichlet $L$-functions and their reciprocals. Combining the joint estimate with estimates for the generating series of Gauss sums gives larger regions of meromorphic continuation. These regions do not separate the possible secondary terms.

title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
abstract: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $φ\circΦ^{-1}$. For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $Λ_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+Φ(-b_p))=φ(b_p)$. We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern. An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

title: PROBE: Learned Proxy-Based Execution for Highly Selective Multimodal Semantic Queries
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enable semantic queries over unstructured data, but invoking an LLM on every row is prohibitively expensive. Proxy-based execution can reduce this ple with the LLM and training a lightweight proxyto label the remaining rows. Nevertheless, in practical scenarios where semantic queries are highly selective, it remainschallenging to identify representative samples foLM budget and to achieve accurate predictions overthe remaining data using the proxy. We present PROBE, a learned proxy-based execution framework for highly selective multimodal semantic queries. PROBE uses selectivity-adaptive sampling to discover rare polightweight proxy on the acquired labels. It thenrefines proxy predictions through residual correction and homogeneity smoothing over a similarity graph. To address sampling bias, PROBE jointly calibrates refined scores usiarate calibration sample, then selectively routescandidates to the LLM by optimizing the tradeoff between estimated F1 and evaluation cost. On queries from SemBench and LRO-Bench with positive rates as low as 2.17x10^-5 budget yields a geometric-mean F1 of 0.762,compared with 0.797 for exhaustive LLM evaluation, at a geometric-mean speedup of 4.87x and a maximum speedup of 9.3x.

title: Local Limit Theorem for Branching Processes in Varying Environments
abstract: Let $Z_{i,n}$ be the population at time $n$ descended from one particle at time $i$ in a branching process in a varying environment. Under two-sided bounds on products of offspring means, an integrable uniform second-moment tail condition, and nondegeneracy and unit positive-support gcd of all weak limits, we prove $\mathbb{P}(Z_{i,n}=k)\le C(n-i+1)^{-2}$ uniformly in $0\le i<n$ and $k\ge1$, and obtain a local limit theorem as $n-i,k\to\infty$ with $k\le L_0(n-i)$, without third-moment assumptions. These results extend the classical local probability estimates for critical Galton--Watson processes to varying environments.

title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.

title: ContactCut: A Partition-Aware Contact Selection Framework for False-Merge Correction in Connectomics
abstract: Localized false-merge correction in connectomics requires converting an identified error into an executable native 3D partition. Still, neither intermediate correction predictions nor seeded graph solvers alone determine which native source-sink constraints should define that partition. We formulate this problem as a 3D-native partition-aware contact selection problem: selecting candidate contacts based on the complete partitions they induce. Our solution comprises two components: ContactCut (CC)-Auto, which uses learned single-contact selection, and ContactCut (CC)-Search, which enables bounded paired-contact search, generates compact alternatives, and applies learned panel ranking. On historical two-way false-merge corrections from MICrONS and FlyWire, CC-Auto improves failure-aware 3D partition (FA-3D Part.) mIoU by 5.9 and 3.4 points over the strongest graph-based controls and by 12.5 and 10.0 points over the best learned baselines. A MICrONS-trained ranker transfers to FlyWire with negligible degradation. CC-Search expands oracle reachability and prioritizes near-oracle alternatives. The code is available at https://github.com/bentake/ContactCut.

title: Convergence of many-body truncations in the in-medium similarity renormalization group
abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) is a leading \textit{ab initio} method for describing atomic nuclei. Most applications truncate the flowing operators at the normal-ordered two-body level, neglecting induced higher-body terms. Convergence with increasing operator rank remains poorly understood, particularly in strongly correlated systems. We systematically assess the many-body truncation hierarchy in the single-reference and multi-reference IMSRG, retaining normal-ordered operators through the four-body and three-body levels, respectively. Using an exactly solvable pairing-plus-particle-hole model, we quantify successive higher-body corrections over a broad range of interaction strengths, spanning weakly to strongly correlated regimes. The multi-reference formulation exhibits faster and more robust convergence than its single-reference counterpart, with the advantage becoming most pronounced at strong coupling. In this regime, higher-rank irreducible density matrices play an essential role in achieving convergence of the many-body expansion.

title: Vehicle and UAV Detection and Tracking with LTE Downlink Reference Signals: A Ray-Traced Evaluation on a Mapped Suburban Site with Licensed Base-Station Records
abstract: Passive sensing on the cellular downlink places the receiver at the user equipment and changes nothing in the network. We report simulation results for an LTE band-3 cell-specific reference signal arm on a ray-traced channel. On a synthetic street canyon the arm is compared with an uplink sounding reference signal arm on the same band, target and scorer: missed-detection probabilities of 0.667 and 0.772. On a surveyed site built from OpenStreetMap footprints and the licensed site record, nine receiver positions along the street track the vehicle at coverage between 29.9 % and 61.7 %; a 283 m lap separates target height from trajectory at 1.6 to 30 m; a 137 m lap on the built-up street tracks a vehicle and a 15 m airborne target on every cell, and 8 receivers at 135 m spacing carry one illuminator's coverage over 1140 m of the street. Potential future work includes extending the analysis to multiple illuminators and varying receiver configurations, and confirmation through over-the-air measurements.

title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
abstract: Humans continuously acquire knowledge from carefully crafted materials such as books and tutorial videos, carrying that understanding into future tasks. Millions of such instructional videos are uploaded online every day, yet LLM agents remain unable to exploit this ever-expanding wealth of human teaching. Their capabilities are frozen after training, while parameter updates at scale remain prohibitively expensive. This raises the central question: can LLM agents learn from this vast instructional resource without parameter updates? We introduce Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured tutorialbook memory through a two-stage adversarial process that harvests hard, video-grounded questions and uses them to refine the memory. At inference time, TAL retrieves through a Table-of-Contents (TOC) tree, tying retrieval directly to the model's reasoning rather than to embedding similarity. To study this setting, we introduce VidLearn, a multimodal QA benchmark built from 72 chess tutorial videos spanning 12 openings. On VidLearn, TAL outperforms all evaluated baselines and improves monotonically as more videos are consumed, achieving up to 113% and 91% relative gains over the corresponding vanilla MLLMs on the training and test splits, respectively. In actual gameplay, TAL reaches a stronger opening-phase position than its vanilla counterpart in 69% of head-to-head games. Evaluation in a second domain further demonstrates the generality of TAL. Together, these results highlight instructional videos as a scalable resource for parameter-update-free agent continual learning.

title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
abstract: Assigning GWAS variants to causal genes requires evidence from multiple resources. We present V2G, an agentic pipeline that records evidence retrieval and returns ranked genes alongside the retrieved evidence. We evaluate whether language-model reranking improves gene prioritisation and whether its gains depend on the retrieved evidence or recall of known associations. On 135 held-out loci where candidate retrieval succeeded and Open Targets L2G predicts, reranking by a language model improves Precision@1 over the evidence ordering it receives, 0.793 against 0.711 (+0.081, 95% CI +0.038 to +0.129), and over nearest-gene assignment (+0.178); no difference from Open Targets L2G or from training-membership baselines was detected. Given only the trait and the candidate gene symbols, in shuffled order, the same model scores 0.864 on these loci (three seeds, 0.859 - 0.867) and names the reference gene at 0.594 of the loci where the pipeline never retrieved it; with each gene's symbol moved to another gene's evidence row it follows the top-scored row and scores 0.284. The gain over the evidence ordering is recall of known genes, and the evidence as presented anchors the model to the ordering rather than informing it. Across the 296 held-out loci (five seeds each) the model keeps the given top candidate at 86% of decisions; at naturally retrieved loci its departures select a reference gene in 85% of departure decisions (31 of 37 loci), and none displaced one. Its calls carry trait-matched mouse mutant or Mendelian phenotype annotations more often than other candidates at the same locus. Train-test overlap is reported throughout. The study includes a frozen benchmark, cached predictions and reproduction code.

title: Optimizing synthetic jet placement for control stability in increasing Reynolds number flows based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: This study utilizes reinforcement learning algorithms to develop advanced control strategies for manipulating synthetic jets positioned on a cylinder, aiming to achieve effective flow control. It addresses critical challenges in achieving robust performance across moderate to high Reynolds numbers (Re) and varying jet placement configurations. The results demonstrate that placing synthetic jets near flow separation regions yields optimal control performance. At Re = 500, the multi-objective flow control strategy achieves up to 37.4% drag reduction and 99% suppression of lift oscillations, while completely suppressing vortex shedding. At Re = 1,000, drag reduction improves to 49.1%, with equally effective lift suppression and complete vortex shedding suppression. At Re = 2,000, the strategy achieves a maximum drag reduction of 58.8% and suppresses 90% of lift oscillations, although some residual wake instabilities persist. Additionally, synthetic jets effectively disrupted detached vortices and stabilized the wake, resulting in streamlined flow and suppressed vortex shedding. These findings underscore the pivotal influence of jet placement in optimizing flow control efficacy, while affirming the advanced capability of control strategies to tackle intricate challenges.

title: DIMWIT: Directly Invoking Models Without Intensive Tuning
abstract: Resource managers typically encode what to do in a task-specific policy---a heuristic, an optimization procedure, or a model trained for the task---that must be developed before use and may need revision as the workload or system changes. We propose bypassing policy development and instead asking pretrained models to make resource-management decisions directly, given the current system state, desired outcome, and available choices. We evaluate this approach on microservice autoscaling, DRAM sizing, and video encoding, using a frontier LLM and two small decision models. On two microservice applications, a small decision model meets latency targets while using within 10% of the replicas allocated by policy-based autoscalers and within 13% of the frontier LLM. In DRAM sizing, a small decision model reduces DRAM usage by up to 27.5% relative to static provisioning while maintaining at least 95% of baseline performance. In video encoding, it completes encodes up to 4.3$\times$ faster than the frontier LLM, with an imperceptible 1.1-point decrease in Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), a metric of perceptual video quality. Making individual resource-management decisions may be considerably simpler than developing a general strategy for making them.

title: Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules
abstract: Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $ϕ_T=T+g_1τ+\cdots+g_rτ^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. Ordering the coefficient tuples $\vec{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ by their maximum degree, we prove that, for a density-one set of tuples, the $λ$-adic Galois representation is surjective for every prime $λ$ of $A$, and the adelic Galois image contains $\mathrm{SL}_r(\widehat A)$. Moreover, for every tuple in this set, the index of the adelic image equals the index of the corresponding rank-one determinant representation and hence divides $q-1$. These results extend Zywina's theorem in rank $2$ to arbitrary ranks $r\geq 3$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

title: Extremal permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with many good slopes and applications to quantum Latin squares
abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We prove the sharp upper bound $φ(n)$ on the number of good slopes, where $φ$ is Euler's totient function. We classify and count the equality cases for prime powers and products of two distinct odd primes. Non-affine equality cases exist for every composite $n\ge6$. We also prove the sharp bound $p_0-1$ for the size of a set of good slopes with invertible differences between distinct elements, where $p_0$ is the least prime divisor of $n$. Finally, we establish gap results below $φ(n)$ and apply our bounds to a construction of quantum Latin squares due to Ball and Simoens.

title: Resolve, Clear, or Defer: Training-Free Active Prototype Triage for Ecological Detection Pipelines
abstract: Ecological monitoring increasingly relies on camera traps and aerial surveys that generate large image collections. High-recall animal detectors can localize candidate animals at scale. However, they also produce many detections that still require expert review, including false positives, ambiguous cases, and animals difficult to identify at the species level. Since exhaustive review requires substantial effort, we propose training-free active prototype triage, where reviewed detections become reusable evidence to (1) Resolve supported foreground classes, (2) Clear likely background false positives, or (3) Defer insufficiently supported cases for expert review. Across camera-trap and aerial datasets, foreground recognition and false-positive rejection benefit from different pretrained representations: BioCLIP2 provides foreground evidence while DINOv3 provides background evidence, reducing erroneous foreground clearing while improving automatic foreground recovery. Deferring unsupported cases avoids the higher error rates caused by forced decisions. Compared with confidence-thresholded multiclass k-NN and uncertainty-sampling logistic regression, prototype triage improves foreground recovery while maintaining competitive or lower review burden. Acquisition goes beyond class discovery: even after classes are represented, prototype choice determines how reliably evidence propagates through the remaining detections. Our results suggest that once animal localization reaches high recall, the challenge shifts from finding animals to deciding which examples to review, how to reuse them, and when evidence does not support an automatic decision.

title: See, Think, Use: Diagnosing Perception and Reasoning Failures in VLMs
abstract: We present See, Think, Use, a protocol that traces each answer of a vision-language model to perception, reasoning or the use of perception. The diagnosis shows a developer which stage to improve and directs test-time compute to the stage that fails. Benchmarks score the final answer, and an answer that rests on the image earns the same credit as a guess or a memorized prior. The protocol asks the model two extra questions per item and needs no access to its weights. A localization probe asks for a box around every instance and measures seeing, and a text-replacement probe answers from a description and measures thinking. Use is the rate at which the answer follows the model's own perception across counterfactual image pairs. The rate needs no answer labels, because the question and its prior are the same on both images. On two model families and six datasets the protocol shows that the knob that helps follows the task family. Answers follow the model's perception except on images that contradict a common prior, and asking the model to localize first repairs this failure when its boxes are right. Allocating compute by the measured stages comes close to the best uniform policy at lower cost and beats a random allocation of the same compute wherever a knob raises the short stage. We will release the code, the prompts and the per-question outputs.

title: The Stability of Data Exchange in Competitive Markets
abstract: We study the stability of data exchange among competing firms. Unlike tangible goods, data is non-rival: sharing it does not deprive the giver of its use. On one hand, competing firms-- often operating as machine-learning-driven predictors that collect observations from a shared environment to solve similar tasks-- can improve their predictive accuracies from pooling data. On the other hand, they compete for market share, which may depend on their relative predictive performance. This raises the central question of this paper: can there be a stable data exchange in such competitive environments? We formalize this via a model of $n$ firms exchanging fractions of their datasets, with predictive performance feeding into market competition. We adopt core stability as our solution concept, accounting for externalities via worst-case responses by non-participating firms. Our main results reveal a sharp contrast driven by demand structure: (i) in fully rational markets, where customers flock entirely to the top-performing firm, a core-stable exchange always exists for any monotone continuous prediction functions; (ii) in partially rational markets with logit-style demand, core-stable exchanges may fail to exist-and even approximate cores can be empty. Our impossibility results suggest that internal profit-sharing within coalitions can restore stability in partially rational markets. We formalize this intuition by showing that when co-operating coalitions equally redistribute market-share revenues among members, a core-stable data exchange exists. Finally, we propose a natural exchange dynamic and demonstrate empirically that it converges to a core-stable data exchange in fully rational markets on simulated instances derived from real datasets.

title: Dynamically defined bulges reveal that early-type galaxies with compact bulges host more massive black holes
abstract: We revisit the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation for early-type galaxies by introducing a uniform bulge defined by dynamical decomposition. From the set of nearby galaxies with accurately measured black hole masses, we select 30 early-type galaxies that have been observed with wide-field integral-field unit instruments (MUSE, ATLAS3D, or PPAK). For each galaxy, we construct an orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model and obtain its stellar orbit distribution. In this framework, we define the bulge uniformly as comprising stellar orbits with circularity $λ_z < 0.7$ (or, in an alternative definition, $λ_z < 0.2$) and lying within $r < 3$ kpc. From these orbits, we reconstruct the spatial density distribution of the bulge and measure its mass ($M_{bulge}$), size ($R_{bulge}$) and surface density slope ($γ_{bulge}$). We find that the dynamical bulge defined by $λ_z < 0.7$ yields masses that are systematically consistent with the photometric bulge masses. Comparing to the bulge from photometric decomposition, using this dynamical bulge definition slightly decreases the scatter around the best-fitting from 0.56 to 0.47. More interestingly, we identify a clear trend: at a given bulge mass, galaxies hosting more compact bulges (i.e. smaller bulge sizes or steeper bulge density slopes) systematically contain more massive black holes; eight outliers show overmassive BHs together with ultra-compact bulges. We interpret this as direct observational evidence that the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation evolves over a galaxy's merger history, with that history imprinted in bulge compactness. Incorporating compactness via an $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}-R_{e, bulge}$ (or $γ_{bulge}$) relation brings the outliers into agreement and reduces the overall scatter of the sample to $\sim 0.3$.

title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Multi-User OFDM ISAC Systems
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a key enabling technology for 6G networks. Efficient resource sharing between communication and sensing is a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ISAC systems, particularly in multi-user scenarios, where channel diversity can be exploited to improve resource utilization. This paper investigates joint subcarrier assignment and power allocation for a downlink multi-user OFDM ISAC system, with the objective of minimizing the delay Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) subject to constraints on the normalized integrated sidelobe level (ISL) over the region of interest (RoI), per-user data rates, and total transmit power. We first derive a convex formulation for sensing power allocation given fixed subcarrier assignments, and then develop an equivalent mixed-integer conic formulation of the joint optimization problem. To obtain computationally tractable solutions, we propose a conic relaxation-guided fix-and-optimize (CRG-FO) algorithm that integrates continuous relaxation, power re-optimization under fixed subcarrier assignments, and restricted neighborhood search. Simulation results demonstrate that joint subcarrier and power allocation reduces the distance CRLB relative to uniform subcarrier and power allocation across the tested ISL thresholds, rate loads, and user configurations. Power optimization on uniform sensing supports captures most of this gain, while adaptive subcarrier assignment provides only modest additional improvement.

title: Almost global solutions of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains without the second null condition
abstract: For 3-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and small initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$, the authors of two papers [M. Keel, H. Smith, C.D. Sogge, Amer. J. Math. 122 (2000), no. 4, 805-842; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004), no. 1, 109-153] have shown that the lifespan ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions satisfies ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ or ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon}$, depending on whether the null condition holds or not, respectively. However, for the corresponding 2-D problem in exterior domains, it remains a difficult and unsolved problem to determine the precise lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions. In our previous papers, we have established that $T_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ holds when both the first and second null conditions are satisfied; and that $T_{\varepsilon}\ge\frac{C}{\varepsilon^2}$ holds when the first null condition is violated. In this paper, we will prove $T_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon^2}$ when the first null condition holds but the second null condition is violated. Combining these results, we have systematically established sharp estimates for the lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moreover, our series of results for quasilinear wave equations in 2-D exterior domains are consistent with the corresponding results for the classical Cauchy problem.

title: Causal Optimal-Transport Attention: Positional Priors and Length Extrapolation
abstract: Causal masking obstructs the column balancing used by optimal-transport (OT) attention. We study an unbalanced OT operator that uses only current and earlier rows and characterize its induced positional prior. For bounded scores and any fixed balancing strength below one, its fixed point assigns vanishing mass to every fixed window as context grows. With constant scores, the prior has an exact scale-invariant form. We classify positional encodings by whether they prevent this dilution. We also derive finite-length window-mass bounds for log-distance priors with exponents near one. Preregistered experiments use 25M- and 100M-parameter language models. The OT operator improves loss extrapolation over softmax, while exploratory comparisons favor an explicit distance bias at a fraction of the cost. Changing only the bias beyond the training length moves long-context loss in the predicted direction on all 30 tested checkpoints. During training, learned exponents approach one even when constrained above it. A margin chosen from prior calculations controls distant-mass growth in the tested setting.

title: A Surrogate Model for Variation-Aware Clock-Mesh Analysis and Design-Space Exploration using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Clock meshes are widely used in high-performance VLSI systems to minimize skew and tolerate On-Chip Variation (OCV) in nanometer technologies. However, analyzing meshes is difficult because reconvergent paths and multi-source drivers prevent static timing analysis (STA) tools from handling mesh loops, making SPICE the industrial standard. SPICE simulations are accurate but slow, so clock-mesh synthesis relies on approximate models that overlook critical effects such as non-linear buffer driving caused by input slew and input skew. We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture that predicts power while also improving the delay and slew predictions at the sinks and capturing the skew histogram under OCV. Trained on SPICE data and tested on unseen real designs, our model achieves average errors of $3.40$~ps in delay, $4.14$~ps in slew and $4.46$~ps in skew, compared with $6.28$~ps, $12.35$~ps, and $11.62$~ps for our prior model, and $74.37$~ps delay and $27.51$~ps skew for the approximate method used in current state-of-the-art works. Our model predicts power within $3.4\%$ of SPICE on average, while delivering $18\times$-$1706\times$ speed-ups over the approximate method under OCV modeling, enabling faster and more accurate clock-mesh design-space exploration. A case study on a real design further shows that our surrogate model finds buffering candidates that, at a balanced tradeoff, improves $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile skew by $49.1\%$, reduces power by $25.7\%$, and reduces area by $37.3\%$ at the cost of a $6.8\%$ increase in $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile maximum slew as compared to the state-of-the-art work.

title: Accounting for Irregular State Transitions through Belief Estimation in Online Medical Consultation
abstract: While online medical consultation broadens access, unprompted patient disclosures and topic shifts frequently disrupt clinician inquiry, leaving clinical states progressively revealed. We characterize these dynamics using both existing evaluation metrics and task-specific interaction metrics designed in this work. Through an empirical study across 16 medical dialogue datasets, we show that authentic online interactions exhibit substantially lower contextual continuity and higher unpredictability than offline and simulated benchmarks. We propose PRISM (Policy Reasoning with Inferred States for Medicine), a framework inspired by partially observable Markov decision processes that decouples latent state estimation from action selection to address drifting dialogue trajectories. Specifically, PRISM factorizes clinical triage into belief estimation, policy optimization, and response realization. By maintaining an evolving posterior belief over consultation states and conditioning action selection on the maximum a posteriori state, PRISM advances clinical goals while accommodating patient-initiated shifts. Extensive evaluations show that PRISM substantially outperforms frontier LLMs and clinical agents, achieving a 22.40 percentage point gain in clinical decision accuracy alongside decisive improvements in response generation, surpassing the strongest baseline by 5.51 points in BERTScore_F1. Furthermore, ablation studies show that providing oracle consultation states consistently boosts response quality across all evaluated baselines by guiding their action reasoning, yielding average gains of 5.58 points in BERTScore_F1.

title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.

title: Low-Latency Joint Source-Channel Coding with Multiple Constant Curvature Curves
abstract: We propose constant-curvature curve multicode (C3M), a multi-branch extension of constant-curvature curve tube (C3T) analog joint source-channel coding for one-shot transmission over fixed isotropic AWGN channels. Instead of mapping a scalar source to a single curve on the power sphere, C3M partitions the source interval across a union of constant-speed branch curves in even-dimensional Euclidean space. This construction increases the available geometric degrees of freedom while preserving a low block length analog encoding structure. We derive the induced mixture output distribution, posterior representation, MAP and MMSE estimators, and mutual-information decomposition into branch-identification and along-curve components. We then introduce geometry- and classification-aware branch allocation rules based on tube density, curve length, and branch-classification reliability. The resulting design procedure fixes the optimal C3T curve as a starting branch and sequentially selects additional branches, thereby reducing the combinatorial cost of exhaustive multi-curve search. We use NORM-inspired branch-conditioned spectral decoders based on Fourier-feature lifting of the received ambient vector. Numerical experiments in four and six dimensions show that adding candidate branch curves improves the finite-dimensional end-to-end signal-to-distortion ratio, with selected two- and three-candidate C3M systems outperforming the one-curve baseline at +10 dB SNR. The results show that multi-curve analog mappings provide a practical finite-dimensional design route for low block length joint source-channel coding.

title: Spectral gaps near one quarter for Weil--Petersson random surfaces with growing cusp number
abstract: We prove that the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ with $n=n(g)\ge1$ labelled cusps converges in probability to $1/4$ as $g\to\infty$, for every sequence $n=o(\sqrt g)$. More precisely, for each fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, there are constants $C_\varepsilon\ge2$ and $g_\varepsilon\ge3$, independent of $n$, such that the expected number of nonzero $L^2$ eigenvalues in $(0,1/4-\varepsilon]$, counted with multiplicity and including residual eigenvalues, is at most $C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2/g$ whenever $g\ge g_\varepsilon$ and $g\ge C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2$. This proves a conjecture of Shen and Wu. A matching lower bound shows that the count estimate is optimal up to constants for each fixed $\varepsilon$, and that $n=o(\sqrt g)$ is necessary for convergence of the gap to $1/4$. The proof combines volume estimates uniform in the cusp count with polynomial approximation and a positive trace on truncated surfaces.

title: Robust Appointment Scheduling with Heterogeneous Costs
abstract: Designing simple appointment systems that under uncertainty in service times, try to achieve both high utilization of expensive medical equipment and personnel as well as short waiting time for patients, has long been an interesting and challenging problem in health care. We consider a robust version of the appointment scheduling problem, introduced by Mittal et al.\ (2014), with the goal of finding simple and easy-to-use algorithms. Previous work focused on the special case where per-unit costs due to under-utilization of equipment/personnel are homogeneous i.e., costs are linear and identical. We consider the heterogeneous case and devise an LP that has a simple closed-form solution. This solution yields the first constant-factor approximation for the problem. We also find special cases beyond homogeneous costs where the LP leads to closed form optimal schedules. Our approach and results extend more generally to convex piece-wise linear costs. For the case where the order of patients is changeable, we focus on linear costs and show that the problem is strongly NP-hard when the under-utilization costs are heterogeneous. For changeable order with homogeneous under-utilization costs, it was previously shown that an EPTAS exists. We instead find an extremely simple, ratio-based ordering that is 1.0604 approximate.

title: Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
abstract: We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $λ$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-λt$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.

title: A solution to the Erdős-Sárközy product-density problem
abstract: Color each positive integer red or blue, and call an integer a same-color product if it is the product of two red numbers or of two blue numbers. Does there exist a universal constant $c > 0$ such that: For each fixed coloring, and for all sufficiently large $M$ (where "sufficiently large" may depend on the coloring), at least $cM$ of the integers among $1$, $2$, $\ldots$, $M$ are same-colored products (allowing for equal factors, and where each distinct product is counted once)? This problem was given (in an equivalent way) in Guy's famous text on unsolved problems in number theory, and was posed (in equivalent ways) by Erdős and Sárközy in 1990, in the proceedings of the 1988 Banff number theory conference, and 1993 [Colloq. Math.], and this problem seems to have remained open. We succeed in solving this problem, by proving that no such universal constant exists.

title: Linear-exponent bounds for the automatic complexity of rational diagonals modulo prime powers
abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be the diagonal of $N/Q$ in $m$ variables over the $p$-adic integers, with $Q(0)$ a unit. We prove that the $p$-kernel of the coefficients of $G$ modulo $p^α$ has size $K_α(G)\le p^{(|J|+1)α-1}+(p^α-1)/(p-1)$, where $J$ is an explicit finite support set determined by the Newton polytopes of $N$ and $Q$, and $|J|\le\prod_i(h_i+1)$ for $h_i=\max(°_{z_i}N,°_{z_i}Q)$. Thus the minimal automaton has $p^{O(α)}$ states for fixed input and prime. The general upper bounds of Rowland and Yassawi have exponents that are cubic in $α$ for Furstenberg series and of order $α^{m+1}$ for diagonals in $m$ variables. The proof combines a $δ$-decomposition with synchronous Cartier sections and a count of compatible histories; it requires no smoothness or ordinarity assumption. We give explicit transitions and derive bounds for Furstenberg series. For the Furstenberg series $F$ of $bx^2y^2+(1+ax+dx^2)y+cx^2$ with odd $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove $K_α(F)\ge9\cdot8^α/(64α-32)$ and $\lim_{α\to\infty}α^{-1}\log_2K_α(F)=3$. This exponent result rests on primitive reachability, parameter-independent normalized window frames, and an overlap estimate certified in a finite quotient of a rational Cartier lattice. An appendix also proves that the zero orbit in the Rowland-Yassawi automaton for $x^2y^2+(1+x+x^2)y+x^2$ has exactly $2^{α+1}+α+1$ states, resolving their orbit-size conjecture.

title: Global straightening of solution manifolds for state-dependent delay equations
abstract: Let $U$ be an arbitrary open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuously differentiable. Suppose that each derivative $Df(ϕ)$, $ϕ\in U$, admits a continuous linear extension $D_ef(ϕ):C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb R^n$, such that $D_ef(ϕ)χ$ depends jointly continuously on $ϕ\in U$ and $χ\in C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$. We construct a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$ which maps the solution manifold of $x'(t)=f(x_t)$ onto an open subset of the closed subspace defined by $ϕ'(0)=0$. This resolves an open problem posed by Walther concerning regularization of the entire solution manifold. The diffeomorphism preserves the value at zero and agrees with the original history on $[-h,-τ]$ for any prescribed $τ\in(0,h)$, and is uniformly arbitrarily close to the identity in the supremum norm. It is connected to the identity by a jointly $C^1$ family of diffeomorphisms. The same conclusions hold under the weaker assumption that the finite signed measures representing the derivatives of $f$ have no atom at zero. We also establish a corresponding theorem for separable real Hilbert-valued histories.

title: $TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering
abstract: Tactile sensing plays a crucial role in everyday human interaction. Consider inserting a plug into a tight socket, vision alone provides limited guidance during the final insertion stage, and we instead rely on both anticipated contact and realized tactile feedback to ajust the insertion motion. The same capability is equally important for robots, particularly in dexterous manipulation tasks. Yet many contemporary robot policies remain vision-dominant. This visual bias, compounded by limited tactile data and sparse contact events, can cause directly incorporated tactile signals to be ignored or even compromise the policy's pretrained capabilities, yielding degrading performance as observed in our experiments. We present $TF^2$-Steering, which refines actions via learned residual steering of the flow-matching action expert's velocity field, using a tactile mixture-of-experts architecture to integrate both tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback. Together with specific designed three stages training recipe, $TF^2$-Steering enables tactile signals to correct and, when necessary, redirect the flow-matching action-generation process, while building on the strong action-generation capacity of the vision-based foundation policy. Extensive experiments across six simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of $TF^2$-Steering. It outperforms the strongest evaluated baselines by 10.7 percentage points in average simulation success rate and 9.1 percentage points in average real-world progress success rate. Project page: https://yiming-cc.github.io/tf2-steering/.

title: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Cross-Repository Joint Development for Coding Agents
abstract: As coding agents achieve increasingly high success rates on software engineering benchmarks, recent efforts have sought to increase task complexity through longer horizons and more extensive code modifications. However, real-world software development often spans multiple interdependent repositories, introducing additional challenges in dependency reasoning, change propagation, and interface consistency. Rather than further increasing complexity within individual repositories, we introduce CrossSWE, a benchmark for cross-repository joint development comprising 171 real-world instances spanning 165 repositories, 20 technical domains, and 13 programming languages. CrossSWE verifies the necessity of coordinated changes by testing whether partial repository modifications are insufficient to achieve the intended behavior. Our evaluation of five LLMs reveals substantial challenges, with the strongest model, GPT-6.1 Sol, achieving only 58.48% Pass@1. Furthermore, cross-repository inconsistencies emerge as the most prevalent failure mode (44.2%), highlighting the difficulty of maintaining consistency across interdependent repositories.

title: A Debiased Machine Learning Single-Imputation Framework for Item Nonresponse in Surveys
abstract: Machine-learning methods offer flexible alternatives to parametric models for imputing missing survey values. However, using their predictions in the customary imputed estimator does not automatically yield valid inference. We explain why the error from estimating the regression function can prevent root-$n$ consistency and develop inference for a finite population mean using a cross-fitted augmented inverse-probability-weighted (AIPW) estimator. The analysis combines an imputation model, a sampling design, and a missing-at-random response mechanism, while allowing dependence among sampling indicators. We establish double robustness and show that, under suitable regularity conditions, consistency of both nuisance estimators together with a product-rate condition yields oracle equivalence and asymptotic normality. We also derive consistent variance estimators accounting for sampling and nonresponse. To obtain a completed survey variable, we construct adjusted imputed values that preserve observed responses and whose weighted mean reproduces the AIPW estimate exactly. We further discuss aggregation of nuisance learners and the conditions under which it preserves the prediction rates needed for inference. Simulations show that cross-fitting can substantially reduce undercoverage, but may increase mean squared error when nuisance predictions are inaccurate.

title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avilés, Japón, Lennard, Martínez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avilés et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.

title: Sequential convergence in the lower topology and co-sobriety of Scott spaces
abstract: We investigate how order structure controls sequential convergence in the lower topology of a poset and how this, in turn, governs topological duality and co-sobriety of Scott spaces. We first give a purely order-theoretic characterization of lower convergence. For complete lattices this yields a lower-limsup formula, and on complete chains the lower limsup coincides with the usual lattice limsup. We also characterize first countability of the lower topology at a point by the existence of a countable coinitial subset outside its principal ideal. We prove that every compact saturated subset of a Scott space is sequentially closed in the lower topology and deduce that, for every poset, the lower topology and the co-compact (de Groot dual) topology of its Scott space have exactly the same convergent sequences and limits. For coherent Scott spaces we identify the lower closure of a $k$-irreducible compact saturated set with its double-cone closure and obtain an infimum criterion for co-sobriety. Consequently, every bounded-complete dcpo with sequential lower topology has a co-sober Scott space. In particular, every countable bounded-complete dcpo, and hence every countable complete lattice, has a co-sober Scott space.

title: Polarization instability of unpolarized excited states in trapped two-component Bose--Einstein condensates
abstract: A binary Bose--Einstein condensate in an elongated trap supports unpolarized excited states, in which both components share the same spatial profile. Within mean-field theory we show that the interspecies repulsion at which these states demix rises with the excitation level. Since each component keeps its atom number, the components separate by moving in opposite directions in the trap, and demixing sets in when the interaction energy released by the separation balances its cost in kinetic and trap energy. We show that the threshold also marks the onset of an exponential, non-oscillating growth of the separation, which divides the cloud into domains of opposite polarization, with walls at the density nodes and further walls interlaced with them. In the Thomas--Fermi regime of a quasi-one-dimensional condensate the rise of the threshold follows power laws in the ratio of the trap oscillator energy to the chemical potential. The trap raises the ground-state threshold, in units of the intraspecies repulsion, by 1.82 times the square of this ratio. Each density node of an excited state near the trap center raises the threshold further by 1.24 times the cube of this ratio. Because the steps between successive levels scale as the cube of this ratio, they fall as the inverse square of the atom number, and the dependence on the excitation level is a mesoscopic effect, appreciable only when the chemical potential is no more than a few times the oscillator energy. In a hyperfine mixture of $^{87}$Rb a Feshbach resonance tunes the interspecies repulsion across the thresholds of the lowest states.

title: CCD: Context-Calibrated Open-Entity Out-of-Distribution Detection in In-Context Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: In-context tabular foundation models (TFMs), such as TabPFN, predict from a labelled context without updating their parameters and are increasingly used for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in Web applications, whose test rows come from entities absent from that context. Such applications need open-entity OOD detection: a new entity must not be mistaken for an unknown class, and an unknown class must still be caught. Existing detectors fail in this setting, and an entity-split gap hides the failure: random splits also place the test entities in the context. The failure arises because every TFM score reflects how unfamiliar a row is to the context. This produces an entity-over-class bias: known-class rows of new entities look more OOD than familiar ones, sometimes more than unknown classes. Specifically, the two OOD scores most widely used with in-context TFMs face an entity-class trade-off: the TFM's predictive confidence misses unknown classes, whereas the distance of a test row to the context flags new entities. To address this problem, we hold a group of entities out of the context and score them with the remaining context, which turns them into new entities of known classes and tells us how such rows should score. To measure detection on new entities, we build NEO-Tab (New-Entity OOD detection on Tables), 14 grouped and temporal tables on which all test rows come from new entities. We then propose Context-Calibrated Detection (CCD), which uses these group-out swaps on in-distribution data to calibrate three distances and the confidence against new-entity references. CCD weights them by their sensitivity and sharpness, keeps the model frozen and uses no OOD data. On NEO-Tab, CCD outperforms 16 existing detectors on every metric we report, and its lead holds on three TFM backbones.

title: No infinite cluster at criticality for long-range percolation with fast-decaying interactions
abstract: We consider independent long-range bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are joined with probability $1-e^{-βJ(x-y)}$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $J$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes, positive on nearest-neighbour pairs, and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^d\sum_{\|x\|>n}J(x)=0$. We prove that there is no infinite cluster at the critical parameter. Together with Berger's theorem for heavy tails, this gives continuity of the phase transition for $J(x)\asymp\|x\|^{-d-α}$ for every $α>0$ except $α=d$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for every exponentially decaying kernel satisfying these hypotheses. Previously the fast-decaying case was known for nearest-neighbour and uniform finite-range kernels, in $d=2$ for finite-range and exponential kernels, and in high dimension for sufficiently spread-out kernels. The proof adapts a recent renormalization argument for nearest-neighbour percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is driven by a gluing inequality conjectured by Kozma and Nitzan. Long edges enter in two places: they can jump over the surfaces that a nearest-neighbour path must cross, and they let a cluster outside a box enter it from far away. We control the first with thick outer faces and the tail condition, and the second by measuring entrances through the total edge weight between a cluster and a box rather than through the number of boundary vertices.

title: Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer for Joint Multipath Parameter Estimation: Applications to mmWave Positioning and Radio SLAM
abstract: Future 6G wireless networks are expected to evolve toward AI-native systems that support intelligent, environment-aware services, including positioning and mapping. Current research has already integrated AI into several aspects of communication, particularly wireless channel estimation. However, most learning-based channel estimators focus on communication-oriented objectives rather than explicitly estimating multipath parameters such as delay, angle of arrival (AoA), and angle of departure (AoD). These parameters provide essential geometric information for downstream tasks including positioning and radio simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). In this work, we propose a Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer (SCFT) for joint multipath component (MPC) estimation from noisy complex channel estimates and physical beam-pair descriptors. SCFT combines local spectral convolution, permutation-equivariant beam-set attention, and a query-based Transformer decoder to detect and classify line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths and estimate their observed delays, AoAs, and AoDs. Experiments on realistic ray-tracing data show that SCFT reduces the generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment (GOSPA) error by 13.4% compared with ResNet, the strongest competing baseline. We further demonstrate this advantage in independent snapshot positioning and radio SLAM, where SCFT reduces position RMSE by 18.5% and 65.0%, respectively, relative to ResNet. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly recovering multipath geometry, as improvements in MPC estimation can translate into substantial gains in downstream tasks.

title: Purity maxima, absolute separability, and spectral volumes of absolutely PPT states
abstract: For $m\otimes n$ systems with $n\ge m\ge3$, we determine the exact maximum purity of absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) states and the unique maximizing ordered spectrum when $n\ge2m^2-4$ for even $m$ or $n\ge2m^2-m-4$ for odd $m$. Under these dimension assumptions, absolutely separable states have the same maximum purity, attained at the same unique ordered spectrum. The proof uses an outer polytope defined by two linear head--tail inequalities, each comparing a sum of the largest eigenvalues with a sum of the smallest. Under explicit multiplicity assumptions, we derive an exact matrix criterion for APPT membership of full-rank spectra with three distinct eigenvalues. For every $m\ge10$, this criterion gives explicit APPT boundary spectra at $n=4m-2$ and $n=4m$ that disprove both cases of the maximum purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter. We also determine the exact completely absolutely separable (CAS) purity maximum and its unique maximizing ordered spectrum in every bipartite dimension. We prove that the inner APPT polytope consists entirely of absolutely separable spectra. The resulting linear sufficient condition for absolute separability strictly improves the reduction-map and eigenvalue-ratio tests. Finally, we compute the exact relative volumes of the CAS set and an outer polytope defined by a single head--tail inequality. Under the uniform measure on spectra, the CAS, absolutely separable, and APPT volumes have the same asymptotic order $\sqrt n\,e^{-κ_m n}$ for every fixed $m\ge2$, with explicit $κ_m>0$.

title: TopoSteer: Topological Layer Selection for Activation Steering in LLMs
abstract: Activation steering controls large language models at inference time by adding a vector to their internal representations. Most work asks how to build that vector, and far less attention has gone to where to add it, even though steering at a poorly chosen layer can be worse than not steering at all. Prior selectors choose a layer without ever steering the model to test it: they score how separable the target behavior is at that layer, and how consistently the individual examples point along the steering direction. We argue that what matters is not the separability of the two activation clouds, nor the alignment of individual displacements with their mean, but the extent of the cloud of per-example displacements that mean-difference steering averages. We propose a topology-based layer selection method, called TopoSteer, which scores a layer by the total H_0 persistence of its displacement cloud, computed as the length of the cloud's Euclidean minimum spanning tree. We show that the score focuses on the displacement cloud's relative geometry, while class separation affects it only through standardization. We also provide a theoretical explanation for our method by proving that, as example-level variation increases, TopoSteer and discriminability move in opposite directions, so the two criteria can rank layers in opposite ways. Across multiple language models and steering tasks, TopoSteer provides a principled alternative to discriminability- and separability-based layer selection and yields more effective steering without requiring held-out validation.

title: A Counterexample to Wooley's $L^1$ Question for Beatty Sequences
