For variable-length training and full prefill, attention-balanced placement can leave token loads uneven, while ring execution repeats overhead at each computation and communication step. In stage-serialized decode CP (DCP), long-running tasks delay dependent work and leave substantial GPU hardware idle. We propose LiquidCP, which unifies training and inference through a common model of Transfer, Compute, and Reduction tasks with tile-level dependencies, decoupling attention tasks from communication and kernel boundaries. For training and full prefill, MegaRing incorporates BuddyRing placement to balance attention and token loads, and coalesces ready KV regions during forward attention to amortize overhead. For decoding and mixed batches, MegaDCP selects history-KV splits by jointly modeling the completion of attention and its dependent reductions. A shared persistent GPU-resident engine executes both designs. Compared with the fastest baseline per configuration on eight H100 GPUs, MegaRing achieves geometric-mean core-attention speedups of $1.23\times$ forward and $1.18\times$ backward, and accelerates a Transformer layer by $1.08$--$1.16\times$. MegaDCP achieves geometric-mean core-attention speedups of $1.20\times$ for decode-only and $1.35\times$ for mixed batches. In vLLM serving with KV prefix cache, it achieves an average time-to-first-token speedup of $1.22\times$.

title: TT-SCHA for Thermodynamics of Binary Alloys
abstract: The free energy of a crystal is an integral over the positions of all its atoms, in 3N dimensions. We evaluate it without random sampling for the ordered alloys B2 NiAl and gamma-TiAl with embedded-atom potentials, using a self-consistent harmonic approximation (SCHA) corrected to third order in temperature, calculated via thermal averages of tensor-train (TT) integrals built from one atom and its neighbors, which we call TT-SCHA. The result is for an infinite crystal without sampling error; its numerical error is set by the starting pivots of the interpolation (up to 9 MPa in the pressure, reduced by averaging three runs; SM Table S26). Against the molecular dynamics of 65,536 atoms (Frenkel-Ladd free energy at 600 K, integrated energy above), TT-SCHA free energy agrees to 0.13 meV per atom at 600-1000 K, using 420-500 times fewer core-seconds for one run. At zero pressure, results agree with published calculations that use the same embedded-atom potential: the published elastic constants of gamma-TiAl (to 1 GPa, by a static lattice calculation) and its thermal expansion from Monte Carlo sampling (to 0.012 percentage points).

title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Quasi-Newton SQCQP Method for Nonlinear Programming Problems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a variance-reduced stochastic quasi-Newton sequential quadratic constrained quadratic programming method (VR-QN-SQCQP) for finite-sum nonlinear optimization with equality and inequality constraints. Exact nonlinear-constraint Hessians are replaced entirely by safeguarded symmetric rank-one (SR1) curvature models built from first-order constraint gradients, while PAGE estimates the objective gradient and an exact \(L_1\) merit function provides globalization. Under explicit regularity, boundedness, relative QCQP-accuracy, and step-length assumptions, the analysis establishes almost-sure subsequential convergence to Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) points and, under stronger uniform step-length and error-control conditions, an expected \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer-iteration bound for the squared KKT residual. A conditional local stability result also compares learned-curvature directions with their exact-Hessian counterparts. Numerical experiments compare VR-QN-SQCQP against Exact-SQCQP-PAGE on Sparse PCA using 253,680 CDC BRFSS 2015 observations and on a dense nonlinear benchmark. Over ten seeds, both methods converge in all Sparse PCA runs, while on the dense benchmark the proposed method converges in 10/10 runs versus 9/10 for the exact-Hessian variant. The proposed method performs zero exact constraint-Hessian evaluations and reduces median curvature-construction time on the dense benchmark from 0.1230 s to 0.0111 s. Overall runtime benefits remain problem-dependent.

title: Ergodic full measures and entropy spectrum for countable observables on compact spaces
abstract: We investigate conditions and obstructions for the existence of ergodic full measures in the context of countable observables on compact spaces. Extending the theory in a unified way, we are able to show a complete picture via thermodynamic formalism for symbolic, uniformly hyperbolic and related systems. We prove conditional variational principles for the topological entropy, showing good approximations by ergodic full measures, and we give conditions where we precisely get ergodic full measures. In contrast with the case with a finite number of observables, new phenomena appear: we exhibit explicit examples of level sets with a null measure with respect to any invariant measure but having large entropy. On the other hand, based on induced ergodic systems in the sense of Kakutani-Rokhlin and heavily utilizing the formalism for countable Markov shifts, we go beyond the classical thermodynamic approach and show a different way of building ergodic full measures. Additionally, we study the regularity and shape of the entropy spectrum and, in the end, we also give some applications of the main conditional variational principles.

title: DR-LiteNet: A Lightweight Explainable Hybrid CNN Framework for Imbalanced Diabetic Retinopathy Grading via Adaptive SMOTE Fusion
abstract: Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from colour fundus photographs is held back by two compounding challenges: severe class imbalance across five severity grades and the heavy computational cost of large scale architectures in resource constrained clinical settings. We introduce DR-LiteNet, a dual branch hybrid convolutional neural network that tackles both problems at once. The CNN branch extracts 1,280 dimensional deep features through EfficientNetB0, while the handcrafted (HC) branch produces a compact 51 dimensional lesion descriptor capturing vessel density, exudate intensity, texture entropy, and HSV colour histograms. Concatenating both branches yields a 1,331-d hybrid embedding, on which Adaptive SMOTE (ADASYN) is applied during training to synthesise minority class feature vectors, correcting distributional skew without touching the image space. A two phase training protocol first warms up the classification head on balanced features, then fine tunes the full network end to end. Grad CAM saliency maps deliver post-hoc clinical explainability. Tested on APTOS 2019 under five fold stratified cross validation, DR-LiteNet reaches 88.77% +/- 0.61 accuracy, a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.884 +/- 0.010, and a macro F1 of 0.792 +/- 0.008 with only 4.69 M parameters beating ResNet50 (23.5 M) by DeltaQWK = 0.022 while staying practical on a single Google Colab T4 GPU. The source code of this project is available at: https://github.com/Nishi-Kanta-Paul/DR-LiteNet.

title: The Min-Max theory of language behavior
abstract: The "Min-Max" theory of language behavior proposes that humans engage simultaneously in minimization of processing effort and maximization of information content, and that this is a primary driver in language evolution (Ring, 2025). This claim seeks to unify observations from language processing (Mahowald et al., 2013; Futrell et al., 2015; Yadav et al., 2020; Hawkins, 2014), interaction (Hörberg and Sjons, 2023; Tucker et al., 2025; Jaeger and Tily, 2011; Smith and Culbertson, 2025), and corpora (Levshina and Moran, 2021; Levshina, 2023; Newmeyer, 2017), which suggest that considerations of processing efficiency and information content are both implicated in human communication. The interaction between these two processes provides an explanation for human linguistic behavior at various levels (Linders and Louwerse, 2023) and predicts historical developments in language, i.e. related to word order (Ring, 2025). Given that the original formulation of the Min-Max theory is based on observational data, the current paper seeks to validate the theory mathematically. Through a series of experiments that use computational models to investigate the theory's predictions, pretrained and iterated learning models are queried with synthetic data. The experiments show that manipulating the variables of token length and the weight of information content in a tabula rasa model results in word order change, as predicted by the theory. The experiments also identify important differences between computational models and observations of human language data, suggesting that current transformer-based language models may not accurately represent psycholinguistic processes. The overall findings indicate that evolutionary trajectories in language are highly susceptible to minimization of processing and maximization of information content.

title: Competition, Switching, and Control in Coupled Adoption-Opinion Dynamics
abstract: We propose a Multi-technology AdopTion-opinion co-Evolution (MATE) model to describe the diffusion of $m \geq 2$ competing alternatives within a networked population whose opinions evolve under social influence and the feedback generated by adoption. Communities interact through two layers: a physical network governing exposure to adoption, and a social network shaping opinion evolution through social imitation. Individuals can adopt a technology, eventually becoming dissatisfied at a rate reflecting the quality of the technology, and switch to an alternative at a rate driven by their opinion of that alternative. For an arbitrary number of competing technologies $m \geq 2$, we characterize the equilibria and establish the existence of an adoption-diffused equilibrium in which all technologies coexist. For $m > 2$, the equilibrium configuration depends on the broader competitive environment: unlike the two-technology case, within-community relative adoption generally depends also on equilibrium opinions and on the other alternatives. Finally, we formulate finite-horizon opinion-shaping control problems, derive necessary optimality conditions via the discrete-time Pontryagin maximum principle, and compute numerical extremals using a forward-backward sweep method.

title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
abstract: A frontier AI model is trained in an AI data center, on tens of thousands of accelerators joined by a dedicated network, and every training step ends with all of them exchanging data at once. Between racks, that network is optical, and each of its four layers, from lasers to switches, runs a fixed or after-the-fact policy. Lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can fail together. At a fixed spare ratio, correlated failure provably caps a pool's availability however large it grows. In this paper, we present a comprehensive predictive control plane framework, called Halley, that reads each resource's next state and acts before the failure occurs. It has four components, each carrying a formal guarantee: LightReserve that sizes the laser pool to provide a coverage bound, FoldFit that schedules the switch within $11/9$ of the optimal, ThermaLead that holds a microring with one-step-ahead control, and TriageGuard that protects the highest-risk modules first. Halley gives each layer a predictive controller that defers to the deployed policy when unsure. Composed from simulations at that point, effective goodput, the share of ideal throughput kept, rises from 65.2\% to 76.5\% if a window that exhausts its spares is lost. If only the dark channels' bandwidth is lost, it reaches 67.4\%. Per megawatt, that is up to 1.03--1.17 times the training; for the same training, up to 3.3--14.7\% less data center capacity. \textsf{Halley}'s fallback circuits are formally verified and are shown to achieve close timing on a commercial FPGA, and pass a 130~nm signoff.

title: LCM-UNet: Scale-Selective Mamba with Reparameterizable Multi-Basis Local Modeling for Lightweight Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Accurate lesion segmentation underpins automated dermoscopic analysis: masks enable measurements of asymmetry, border and size. Deployment in primary care or on mobile devices requires a compact network. Existing ultra-light Mamba U-Nets offer global context, but global-modeling cost depends on each Mamba block's resolution, while their local branches rely on a single square kernel. We introduce LCM-UNet, a 33,474-parameter U-shaped network that fuses every skip at its native resolution, restricts bidirectional Mamba to stages at one-sixteenth of the input resolution or coarser, and uses local convolutions at finer scales. A multi-basis reparameterizable adapter augments each local branch during training with dilated, horizontal and vertical depthwise kernels, then folds them into the host kernel before inference. Each skip connection also learns a stage-specific gain. Nine networks were retrained on the official ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018 partitions under a harmonized protocol, with PH$^2$ reserved for external validation and ablations run on a development split. LCM-UNet achieved Dice scores of 88.62%, 89.73% and 90.46% on ISIC 2017, ISIC 2018 and PH$^2$, respectively, ranking first on both ISIC test sets and second on PH$^2$ among the compared models. In the native-resolution host, removing Mamba from the one-eighth-resolution decoder stage eliminated 63% of Mamba operations, corresponding to 5.3% of all operations, with a Dice change of $-0.03$ percentage points. The adapter improved Dice by 0.48 percentage points over a single host kernel without adding deployed parameters or operations. With latency so far measured only on a GPU, LCM-UNet is a candidate for resource-constrained deployment.

title: Spectral analysis and shape optimization of Steklov--Dirichlet eigenvalues on shell-type domains
abstract: We investigate the Steklov--Dirichlet eigenvalues on shell-type domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 2$, where the Steklov and Dirichlet conditions are imposed on the outer and the inner boundaries, respectively. We introduce the Green function associated with the problem, which is well-defined for spectral parameters outside the spectrum and exhibits blow-up behavior at eigenvalues, and establish its spectral representation. We also examine its differentiability and derive its shape derivative under translations of the inner boundary. Using these results and a layer potential approach, we propose a computational framework for optimizing the eigenvalue with respect to the position of the inner boundary, incorporating an eigenvalue estimator for which a local error bound is established. Numerical experiments for various inner and outer boundary shapes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying configurations that maximize the first eigenvalue.

title: TxBench: A Benchmark of Attack Transactions and Evidence-Backed Negatives on Seven EVM Chains
abstract: Researchers evaluate detectors of malicious smart-contract transactions on datasets that each paper assembles anew. Their positives come from incident trackers, whose citations mix attacks with setup steps and transactions that never ran, or from a detector's own output, which makes the evaluation circular; their negatives are ordinary transactions. A shared benchmark needs positives whose own execution shows the attack and negatives that use the attacks' mechanisms, with no detector deciding either label. We present TxBench, a benchmark of attack transactions and evidence-backed negatives on seven EVM chains, with the five-step pipeline that builds it. The pipeline collects every transaction that BlockSec's incident library or the EVM Hack Registry cites, maps its weakness to OWASP's SCWE taxonomy, and rebuilds its execution from free data sources. A cited transaction qualifies as a valid TxBench attack only if it extracts value from others during execution, is consistent with all verified source claims, and is independently linked to the reported incident by corroborating evidence. Negative examples are sampled from each chain's traffic near the attacks and retained only when positive evidence confirms their legitimacy. Of 1,850 cited transactions, TxBench accepts 1,012 attacks from 602 incidents, worth USD 868.1 million: 846 contract exploits and 166 key compromises. A blind review under rules fixed in advance confirms 98 of 100 sampled attacks (97.7% weighted) and all 100 sampled negatives. As baselines, four zero-shot LLMs reading anonymized traces are precise but find at most 0.43 of the attacks and no key compromise, leaving ample room for better detectors.

title: Bandwidth rules for Dirichlet kernel density estimation on the simplex
abstract: Dirichlet kernels provide a natural tool for density estimation on the simplex, but data-driven bandwidth selection for them has been mostly limited to likelihood cross-validation (LCV). We develop bandwidth selectors for Dirichlet kernel estimators of densities and projected first derivatives for compositional data. Using a Dirichlet mixture as the reference model, we derive an exact representation of the mean integrated squared error (MISE) and define the exact MISE (EMI) selector. We also derive a closed-form least-squares cross-validation (LSCV) criterion and introduce the reference-smoothed least-squares (RSLS) selector, which replaces the unstable leave-one-out term of LSCV with the fitted Dirichlet mixture. For derivative estimation, we obtain projected derivatives of the Dirichlet density and their integrability conditions, extend the new bandwidth selectors, and carry out kernel mean shift clustering on the simplex. Simulations show that EMI is the most competitive selector for larger samples and Dirichlet-like targets, RSLS generally performs best for small samples and is more stable than LSCV for derivative estimation, and LCV remains competitive for non-Dirichlet targets in density estimation. Applications to wholesale customer expenditure and sectoral employment data illustrate density estimation and clustering, respectively.

title: CaliSplat: Sparse Gaussian Fitting and Calibrated Rate Allocation for Image Compression
abstract: 2D Gaussian representations provide an explicit and lightweight alternative for image representation, enabling fast deterministic decoding without a heavy neural synthesis network. However, existing per-image Gaussian codecs still require costly image-specific optimization to determine how limited Gaussian capacity should be distributed across heterogeneous regions. We introduce CaliSplat, an optimization-efficient Gaussian image codec that selectively explores candidate representations and globally allocates a constrained Gaussian budget. We exploit the closed-form reconstruction error of the single-Gaussian case as an inexpensive measure of local difficulty, fitting higher-capacity candidates only in regions where additional Gaussians are likely to be useful. To reduce selection errors caused by mismatched convergence rates across candidate sizes, a small set of longer-horizon fits is used to calibrate short-horizon distortion estimates before global budget-aware selection. The selected representation is then compressed into a bitstream. Across standard and large image datasets, CaliSplat achieves competitive or superior rate--distortion performance while reducing per-image fitting time by $3.0\times$--$15.7\times$ compared with representative Gaussian codecs. It further maintains high-throughput deterministic decoding at $175.9$--$478.2$~MP/s. These results demonstrate that content-adaptive Gaussian compression can substantially reduce per-image optimization cost while preserving strong reconstruction quality and efficient explicit decoding.

title: SphereFlow: Missing Modality Imputation via Geometric Transport on Hypersphere
abstract: Missing modality imputation aims to synthesize unobserved modalities from observed ones. Existing methods treat each modality as living on its own latent manifold, forcing the generator to learn a long, unstructured jump between them. We present SphereFlow, which takes a fundamentally different view: by projecting all modalities into a shared hyperspherical latent space via a frozen self-supervised encoder, cross-modal imputation reduces to short-range geometric transport between nearby points on the sphere. Realizing this idea with flow matching, however, exposes two geometric conflicts: the standard Gaussian noise source is catastrophically mismatched with the unit-norm data manifold, and the linear interpolation path departs the sphere surface into a region where the decoder has no training signal. We resolve both with simple, geometry-aware modifications: replacing the noise source with the observed-modality latent so that the velocity field learns only the cross-modal displacement, and training the decoder with a time-weighted loss that extends its domain to the near-surface region traversed by the flow. We prove that this data-as-source formulation reduces the worst-case off-manifold deviation from a quantity that grows with the latent dimension to a small, dimension-independent bound governed by inter-modality similarity. Experiments on BraTS multi-modal MRI imputation and CT-MRI translation demonstrate state-of-the-art generation fidelity across all settings, while downstream brain tumor segmentation with our imputed data closes roughly eighty percent of the gap to the full-modality oracle. Code is available at https://github.com/WTHH031230/SphereFlow.

title: Mixed-Integer Program Sensitivity Analysis via Branch-and-Bound Trees
abstract: We study how to compute valid dual bounds for mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) with finite variable bounds under data perturbations. In an offline-online setting, a nominal instance is solved once and its information is reused to evaluate perturbations. We develop a framework for linear programs under simultaneous perturbations to the objective coefficients, right-hand side, and constraint matrix. Our construction is based on a bounded Lagrangian dual evaluated at nominal optimal dual multipliers. We prove that its gap to the perturbed LP optimal value grows at most linearly with perturbation magnitude under suitable conditions. We extend this construction to MILPs by reusing the nominal branch-and-bound tree and node-level dual information, generalizing the sensitivity analysis framework of Schrage and Wolsey (1985) to all problem data. To strengthen the dual bounds, we adapt their subtree-selection dynamic program. The online computations support GPU acceleration and highly parallel evaluation of dual bounds, which can also certify optimal variable fixings and accelerate reoptimization. Experiments on generalized independent set, combinatorial auction, capacitated facility location, and unit commitment instances produce tight dual bounds at low computational cost. For single-parameter ``what-if'' perturbations, gaps are typically a small fraction of a percent, with GPU evaluation times below a millisecond per perturbation. Relative to the time Gurobi needs to obtain bounds of the same quality, GPU evaluation is approximately 2,000--240,000 times faster for single-parameter perturbations and 120--50,000 times faster for multi-parameter perturbations. Using exact perturbed optima as supplied primal cutoffs, variable fixing accelerates exact reoptimization by up to a factor of 10 for generalized independent set instances, with little or no improvement for unit commitment.

title: Efficient and Faithful High-Resolution Image Editing with Sparse Cross-Resolution Denoising
abstract: Instruction-based image editors still primarily operate at 1K, whereas practical editing increasingly requires faithful 2K/4K outputs. Dense high-resolution adaptation preserves the editing trajectory but incurs expensive target-source attention; editing at 1K followed by external refinement is cheaper but can separate detail restoration from the editing trajectory. We introduce FLASH, a native high-resolution editor based on sparse cross-resolution denoising. A frozen 1K branch provides a semantic and structural anchor, while a target-resolution branch reconstructs local detail within the same Transformer. An asymmetric topology retains full 1K attention, guides high-resolution queries with spatially aligned low-resolution noisy-target states, and confines high-resolution target-reference interaction to local Halo neighborhoods. Resolution-specific diffusion-state mapping and spatial YaRN adapt the pretrained editor to larger grids. An optional, training-free progressive path replaces early high-resolution denoising with a 1K prefix and completes refinement in the same editor. On VINS-4KEval, the direct model achieves the strongest structural fidelity among the compared methods at both 2K and 4K. A separate 4K forward benchmark with R = 1 records 4.2x faster total forward execution and 25.3x faster attention than dense target-reference attention. Progressive inference reduces end-to-end 4K latency by 30.5%, with a modest quality cost.

title: Weak uniqueness and autonomous approximation for the SLE-reversible Weil-Petersson response diffusion
abstract: We study the self-consistent common-noise equation associated with the Weil--Petersson response differential of the rotationally marked SLE welding probability. For $0<κ\leq4$, we prove joint weak uniqueness among continuous adapted weak solutions whose law at each deterministic time is the welding probability, and obtain the Markov property in the original filtration. A conditional Gaussian lift and capacity localization give the required $L^1$ generator-range density. Identification with the canonical law gives stationarity and reversibility. We also construct autonomous Fejér and Poisson regularizations with pathwise-unique global strong solutions. Their joint state-noise laws converge to the canonical law for every initial probability absolutely continuous with respect to the welding probability.

title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
abstract: The advancement of multimodal learning is heavily constrained by the scarcity and high annotation cost of high-quality instruction data. While raw videos offer an abundant and dynamic source of visual knowledge, transforming them into precise instruction data remains highly challenging. To bridge this gap, we present VidUEU-Agent, an automated pipeline that synthesizes instruction data from raw videos for multimodal understanding, editing, and unified tasks. VidUEU-Agent follows a four-stage pipeline: it performs global perception to filter low-quality shots, mines keyframes and multimodal signals, constructs metadata and routes the metadata to synthesize instruction samples. More importantly, our agent framework can autonomously iterate the data distribution based on downstream training results, thereby optimizing data quality, balance, and training effectiveness. Scaling this pipeline, we construct VidUEU-100K, a large-scale dataset of 100K training samples spanning multiple domains and tasks, providing a robust foundation for developing comprehensive multimodal capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning baseline models on VidUEU-100K yields significant and consistent performance gains across diverse representative benchmarks, validating the effectiveness of our proposed agent framework and dataset.

title: Stress-Testing Small-Scale Cosmological Inference With Empirical Galaxy--Halo Connection Models
abstract: Small-scale galaxy clustering contains substantial cosmological information, but extracting it reliably requires robust modeling of the galaxy--halo connection. In this work, we compare two widely adopted families of empirical models, subhalo abundance matching (SHAM) and the halo occupation distribution (HOD), testing their predictions for galaxy clustering and their recovery of the input cosmology. Using Aemulus-$β$, a new multi-cosmology simulation suite with substructure merger trees, we fit multiple SHAM and HOD models to the small-scale clustering of a stellar-mass-selected mock galaxy catalog generated with the more physical semi-empirical model UniverseMachine. We then use cosmological evidence modeling to infer the structure growth parameter $S_8$. Our results show that the SHAM model, regardless of the treatment of numerically disrupted subhalos, is able to offer tight, unbiased constraints on $S_8$ with ~2-3% precision, using simulations of relatively small volumes that span a limited number of cosmologies. In contrast, HOD models, even when accounting for assembly bias, yield weaker and potentially biased cosmological constraints that are sensitive to implementation choices: the inferred $S_8$ degrades in precision to ~6-11% and can be offset by ~1$σ$. This suggests that the excessive parametric flexibility and model misspecification of most commonly adopted HOD models can degrade and bias the resulting cosmological constraints. We further evaluate each model's performance in predicting higher-order statistics not used in the fit and find that SHAM generally reproduces them more accurately than the tested HOD models. These results highlight the potential of leveraging predictive subhalo-level information from simulations to enable robust cosmological inference on small scales.

title: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
abstract: Automated research pipelines pair an LLM proposer with a verifier on an implicit bet: discovery quality rises with verification strength. Under a pre-registered protocol we test this bet in two real-data domains -- job-shop scheduling and vehicular edge offloading on Beijing T-Drive trajectories -- across 100 matched LLM/random pairs per domain and three verifier tiers. The manipulation binds -- a 429-case mutation battery shows scores rising across tiers -- yet the paired LLM-over-random advantage does not scale with it (A, one-sided p=0.1115; D, p=0.9994), and in D shrinks under the strict tier (margin contrast -0.040, p=0.0013). The two lower gates promote identical candidates in 100/100 and 99/100 pairs, so the strict order is untestable when they coincide. Constructively, LLM proposals carry a real paired advantage over random controls, but a post-hoc union-pool analysis shows the fastest path to better discovery is widening the pool, not tightening the gate: mixing the two pools adds +1.52 holdout-value units in domain A (one-sided Wilcoxon, n=100, p=0.0002) -- evidence that pool composition, not verification strength, is the lever. Criteria, ledgers and scripts are archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23308866).

title: Typological Feature Induction as a Benchmark for Inductive Metalinguistic Reasoning
abstract: Existing metalinguistic reasoning benchmarks require both inference of rules and their application, making failures hard to diagnose. We introduce typological feature induction (TFI) which targets the former step. Given sentences in an unnamed language paired with translations in a known pivot language, models must predict a typological feature of the unnamed language. From Grambank and multi-parallel corpora, we automatically build evaluation questions over 195 languages. We find that LLMs identify 59--80% of these languages from only 16 sentence pairs; and misaligning the translations barely affects their accuracy, suggesting reliance on prior knowledge of the language. Enciphering text to prevent recognition increases the corpus' utility, but mainly for features where target and pivot languages agree. On languages which models cannot identify, neither open model outperforms a majority-value baseline. Since induction from raw text aligns with field linguists' use-case, this work indicates the models tested are not yet ready for this role. TFI offers a scalable path to track progress in this direction.

title: GVT3D: Gesture-Vision-Text Token Enrichment for 3D Embodied Reference Understanding
abstract: Natural human-robot interaction requires robots to interpret language and gestures within a 3D environment to support tasks such as pick-and-place and object retrieval. 3D Embodied Reference Understanding (3D-ERU) supports this by identifying the 3D location of a target object from a scene (point-cloud) containing a human pointing gesture and an accompanying language description. However, current 3D-ERU models lack alignment of cross-modal representations and incur high processing costs that increase with the point-cloud's size. To address this, we propose GVT3D, which employs an Embodied Fusion module that jointly models language, gesture, and vision inputs within a shared embedding space, promoting cross-modal alignment. We additionally introduce a foveation approach that selectively processes the point cloud within a coarse region around the estimated pointing direction to reduce computations. GVT3D achieves ~8% higher accuracy and foveation enables 2.95x faster execution while maintaining comparable accuracy, relative to prior 3D-ERU models.

title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression
abstract: Visualizing multivariate scientific simulation data is essential for understanding complex physical phenomena, yet the massive scale of such data imposes a severe storage bottleneck in high-performance computing environments. Implicit neural representations (INRs) have emerged as a promising continuous alternative to traditional lossy compressors, but existing methods struggle to explicitly capture cross-variable interactions and to adapt to the diverse spectral characteristics of physical variables. To address these limitations, we propose SWAP-INR, an architecture for high-fidelity compression of multivariate, time-varying simulation data. SWAP-INR introduces two key components: (1) The switchable attention path (SWAP) module explicitly models cross-variable interactions through a cross-variable attention layer, then routes each variable to an attention or non-attention path by a deterministic, loss-driven criterion, and prunes the inactive layers for structural compression. (2) The adaptability amplification SIREN (A2-SIREN) replaces rigid frequency scaling with channel-wise learnable modulation, adapting to heterogeneous physical features with negligible overhead. Combined with post-training 16-bit quantization, SWAP-INR achieves state-of-the-art performance on small modular reactor (SMR) datasets and remains competitive on public physics simulation datasets, while maintaining a constrained memory footprint. Our code is https://github.com/hvcl/SWAP-INR.

title: ReflexArc: Bottom-Up Integration of Instantaneous Tactile Reflexes into Whole-Body Humanoid Control
abstract: Humanoid robots operating in cluttered environments must react to unexpected contacts before the first impact peak, which arrives within tens of milliseconds. Learned whole-body policies running at 50 Hz introduce a policy-cycle delay and may suppress a protective withdrawal as a tracking error. To address these challenges, we propose ARC (Ascending Reflex Control), a bottom-up framework that integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes with learned whole-body control. ARC consists of two components: an instantaneous reflex pathway and bottom-up reflex integration. The reflex pathway detects hazardous contacts from full-body tactile sensing, solves a whole-body withdrawal pose, and delivers it directly to the motors within 10 ms. Bottom-up reflex integration combines reflex-in-the-loop policy learning, reflex-transparent policy alignment, and reflex-informed policy adaptation to sustain the withdrawal, maintain balance, and complete longer-horizon recovery. We deploy ARC on a Unitree G1 and evaluate three categories of hazardous contact. Compared with an otherwise identical reflex delayed by 20 ms, ARC reduces the first force peak by 34.1% and reduces the contact impulse from 0.2632 N s to 0.1225 N s (a 2.15x ratio). We further demonstrate protected motion tracking, teleoperation, and vision-free obstacle traversal guided by foot tactile sensing. Project page: https://minusmodulo.github.io/reflexarc-website/

title: Minimizing Bottleneck Overload Risk in Online Edge Task Placement under Workload Uncertainty
abstract: In edge computing, tasks must be placed on servers of finite capacity before workloads are realized, often with only workload means and variances known. An assignment balanced on expected load can still leave a server with more fluctuations than its residual capacity can absorb. Per-server risk constraints can enforce a prescribed overload tolerance but do not distinguish the assignments that meet it by how close the riskiest server comes to the limit. We show that, for independent tasks, placement preserves a period's total variance and total residual capacity, and decides only how fluctuation, measured by standard deviation, is paired with residual capacity across servers. The risk ratio, the ratio of fluctuation to residual capacity, parameterizes a server's worst-case overload probability over all aggregate workload distributions with given mean and variance. We minimize the largest risk ratio, attained at the risk bottleneck. Risk-Bottleneck Placement (RBP) places tasks in descending order of standard deviation, each on the server with the smallest post-assignment risk ratio, and refines the assignment with relocations and swaps within a finite per-period online budget. On small instances solved exactly by enumerating every assignment, minimizing the maximum expected utilization leaves the largest risk ratio 25.66-29.19% above its exact minimum on average, even with risk-minimizing tie-breaking, and the corresponding gap for RBP is 1.77-2.64%. In trace-derived multi-period simulations at two workload pressures, RBP reduces the worst-server overload probability by 26.0% and 18.0% relative to the best baseline and remains the lowest at every tested pressure and scale.

title: Sharp decay of the spherical averages of the Fourier transform of open sets
abstract: For a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, the spherical average $E_Ω(R)=\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}|\widehat{\mathbb{1}_Ω}(Rω)|^2dω$ is never $O(R^{-a})$ with $a>d+1$, and for smooth boundaries it is $O(R^{-d-1})$, as it is for the ball, whether or not the boundary is curved. In 2003, Brandolini, Hofmann and Iosevich extended this to every convex domain and to every domain with $C^{1,\frac{1}{2}}$ boundary, and this regularity condition has not been improved since. How much regularity does the decay $R^{-d-1}$ require? We show that among Hölder classes the answer is $C^{1,\frac{1}{4}}$. Every bounded domain with $C^{1,\frac{1}{4}}$ boundary satisfies $E_Ω(R)\leq C_ΩR^{-d-1}$, while for every $0<s<\frac{1}{4}$ any smooth domain can be altered near a single boundary point to produce a $C^{1,s}$ domain for which this bound fails along a sequence of radii. More generally, when the boundary has fractional Sobolev regularity $W^{1+s,p}$, we determine the optimal decay exponent under a Dini condition on the normal, and in a large range of $s$ and $p$ without it. The upper bounds follow from $L^2$ estimates for nondegenerate oscillatory integral operators whose phases are distances between points of two graphs with Dini or fractional Sobolev gradients, and hence barely better than $C^1$. These are far too rough for the integrations by parts techniques from the smooth theory. We replace derivatives by finite differences adapted to the phase, a device that we expect to be useful in a variety of related problems.

title: Reference-Beam-Assisted Perturbation-Resistant Imaging Through A Single Multimode Fiber
abstract: Multimode fiber (MMF) imaging is highly sensitive to mechanical perturbations, which alter modal coupling and disrupt the speckle-to-target mapping. Here, we propose a reference-beam-assisted method for image reconstruction across multiple fiber configurations. An independent reference beam propagates through the same MMF as the imaging signal without target modulation, providing target-independent transmission-state information through its speckle patterns without requiring a separate configuration-sensing structure. A neural network jointly processes the signal and reference speckles to reconstruct target images. Experiments with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across 10 fiber configurations demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, faster training convergence, and more accurate configuration identification. Further evaluation across 40 configurations confirms the reconstruction benefit of reference-beam assistance over a larger set of perturbed fiber states. These results provide a foundation for developing perturbation-adaptive MMF imaging systems for flexible endoscopy and minimally invasive optical diagnostics.

title: Topology Does Not Determine Defect Mobility in Active Polar Matter
abstract: Topological defects are commonly characterized by their charge, although defects with the same charge can have different internal morphologies. We study the annihilation of isolated $\pm1$ defect pairs in a two-dimensional compressible Toner--Tu model, varying the morphology of the $+1$ defect while keeping the initial charges and separation fixed. Activity produces a morphology-dependent mobility asymmetry: reversing the radial orientation of an aster reverses which defect travels farther, and asters show the strongest response. An early-time analysis reveals that the initial morphology selects distinct density modes whose gradients subsequently feed back on the polarization. Consistently, removing the density-gradient coupling strongly suppresses the asymmetry. These results establish defect morphology, in addition to topological charge, as a dynamical variable governing defect-pair motion in active polar matter.

title: Annealing-Induced Structural and Optical Evolution of Ion-Beam-Sputtered Ta2O5 Films for High-Power Laser Applications
abstract: Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) thin films deposited by ion beam sputtering (IBS) are essential components in high-power laser systems, where post-deposition annealing is routinely used to optimize film quality. In this work, we systematically investigate the structural and optical evolution of IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers subjected to post-deposition annealing at temperatures from 400 to 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The films undergo an amorphous-to-polycrystalline transition between 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, accompanied by a marked increase in surface roughness. Argon bubbles inherently incorporated during IBS serve as structural markers: their size correlates positively with the surface roughness from the as-deposited to 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ but decouples at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, revealing a transition from matrix-relaxation-dominated to surface-diffusion-dominated behavior. Transmittance spectra show a red shift at 400 and 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ which can be explained by physical thickness increase. Weak absorption decreases from ~6 ppm in as-deposited films to ~2 ppm at 400-600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to annihilation of oxygen vacancies, rises markedly at 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to grain-boundary defects and then drops again at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as grain boundaries relax. We identify 400 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as the optimal annealing window for IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers, with the lowest surface roughness and effectively reducing weak absorption while preserving the amorphous phase.

title: Modeling fragmentation of $^{20}$Ne nuclei at the LHC
abstract: Fragmentation of relativistic neon nuclei was studied with the Abrasion-Ablation Monte Carlo for Colliders model (AAMCC-MST), which incorporates pre-equilibrium clustering of spectator matter via a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) algorithm, subsequent decays of the excited clusters, and Coulomb repulsion between final fragments. After validating the model against data on $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne fragmentation on various targets, the production of spectator nuclear fragments, neutrons, and protons in $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne collisions at the LHC was modeled at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$ TeV. The production cross sections, transverse and longitudinal momentum distributions for $^2$H, $^4$He, $^6$Li, $^{10}$B, $^{12}$C, $^{14}$N, and $^{16}$O fragments were calculated as these fragments may contaminate $^{20}$Ne beams circulating in the LHC. A simple parametrization describing relative width of the longitudinal momentum distributions calculated for these fragment species was constructed. To study the sensitivity of results to $α$-clustering and nuclear density distributions in neon nuclei, two density profiles for $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne were used: a deformed Woods-Saxon, and a five-$α$ bi-pyramidal configuration. In addition, a spherical profile was considered for $^{20}$Ne. Comparing results obtained with these profiles and with or without MST clustering shows that the calculated yields of spectator nucleons and fragments, their momentum distributions are sensitive to the details of nuclear structure of $^{20,22}$Ne and fragmentation modeling. The results provide the input for simulations of the transport of secondary forward nuclei in the LHC to estimate their interaction rates with circulating $^{20}$Ne beam nuclei, and also for calculations of responses of neutron and proton Zero Degree Calorimeters to $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne events.

title: Reducing the arithmetic cost of quantum derivative pricing with language-model circuit design
abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can estimate expected discounted payoffs with quadratically fewer oracle calls than Monte Carlo, but each call requires coherent computation. We use language-model-assisted circuit design to reduce reversible payoff arithmetic for a three-asset worst-of autocallable and a target accrual redemption forward (TARF). The constructions retain compact integer representations of market paths alongside contract history, reconstructing quantities temporarily for contract decisions and payoff-angle evaluation. Relative to matched internal references, the factor-sum autocallable and windowed TARF circuits reduce the product of Toffoli count and peak logical qubits $(N_{Tof} Q_{max})$ by factors of 2.39 and 4.84, respectively. At a second autocallable setting, fresh search recovers a 1.35-fold saving after the tested fixed adaptation loses its advantage. For the factor-sum circuit, we prove exact coherent execution of its integer specification for every input, incoming accumulator and measurement record, with clean workspace and phase cancellation. A separate lattice calculation gives a numerical angle-tolerance-violation probability of 6.248e-8 and evaluates pricing bias under the declared loading law, with bounded omission but no certified numerical enclosure. The results connect compact representations to lower-cost payoff arithmetic and separately assessed logical and financial correctness. Their resource scope excludes loading, payoff rotation and estimation.

title: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control
abstract: Advances in free-electron quantum optics are establishing free electrons as a versatile quantum resource. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drift provide elementary operations for shaping the longitudinal electron wavefunction, yet their full control capabilities remain unexplored. Here, we prove that a finite sequence of alternating monochromatic PINEM interactions and free drifts can approximate any prescribed inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the full ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy. We therefore call the protocol PINEMAD (PINEM And Drift). This framework encompasses state preparation, unitary gates, and isometric encoding. We further show numerically that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads, using experimentally accessible coupling strengths and tabletop-scale total drift lengths. These results establish electron energy sidebands as a programmable quantum resource.

title: Movable Antenna Aided Robust Wireless Transmission: From Model-Based Optimization to Scalable Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates robust joint antenna positioning and precoding for multiuser movable antenna (MA) systems under imperfect channel state information (CSI). First, we identify the mismatch between the spatial statistics of densely sampled MA channels and the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) basis used for conventional robust precoding. To address this, we develop a novel discrete prolate spheroidal sequence (DPSS)-based a posteriori channel model. By exploiting the spatial covariance structure of MA channels, this model is better suited to modeling MA channel uncertainty. Building on this model, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm for robust joint antenna positioning and precoding to maximize the expected sum rate. By transforming the coupled optimization of antenna positioning and precoding at each iteration into direct comparisons of closed-form scores, we design a low-complexity position replacement scheme that effectively reuses matrix computations across candidate sets. To further improve efficiency and scalability, we exploit the inherent tensor equivariance (TE) of the problem to develop a reinforcement learning framework. To explicitly account for channel uncertainty, we develop novel pairwise user-interaction and CSI-conditioned equivariant attention mechanisms to encode channel statistics and adaptively fuse them with the available CSI. We further introduce distance-biased spatial attention to incorporate the geometry of candidate positions into attention weighting, thereby enhancing spatial feature learning. Simulation results show that the proposed methods improve sum-rate performance while reducing online runtime under imperfect CSI. These methods also achieve near-optimal performance under perfect CSI, closely matching the exhaustive-search method. Moreover, the learning framework generalizes across different numbers of users and MAs without retraining.

title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
abstract: Language models are accurate on most long-arithmetic problems, but their accuracy is estimated on samples and carries no guarantee for an unseen input; tool use is exact but moves the computation outside the network. We show that exactness at all input lengths becomes a finite, checkable property of a network when each of its steps reads only a bounded view of an external working memory. In Sketchpad, Qwen3.5-0.8B with a low-rank adapter executes arithmetic procedures on a rendered sheet. Each forward pass reads a three-cell view and emits one step: a digit, a carry or borrow, and the next operation. A fixed runtime moves the view and writes no digit of a result. We prove in Lean that the model is then exact on all inputs of any length if and only if it is exact on the finite set of views the runtime presents, that no finite test suffices when steps also read earlier steps, and that the guarantee tolerates bounded numerical perturbation and extends to compositions of procedures. All 2,446 views pass on the deployment device, a laptop GPU running the model in a web browser. The certified model performs signed addition and subtraction, long multiplication and division, square roots and greatest common divisors at arbitrary length. It solved 200 of 200 pre-registered problems in the browser, and 220 of 220 sums of up to 1,000 digits and products of up to 20 digits, of which GPT-6.1 Sol, the strongest of ten other models, solved 217. A symbolic runtime built on these procedures solves, expands and factors polynomials with every number computed by the model, and a multiplicative gate on the adapter recovers the base model exactly when the sheet is not in use.

title: A Systematic Point Cloud Edge Detection Framework for Automatic Aircraft Skin Milling
abstract: The edge detection technique is an essential step for aircraft skin milling in aviation manufacturing. Most of the current detection methods focus on traditionally defined edge extraction tasks but disregard the crucial systematic requirement of edge milling. In this paper, we proposed a novel edge detection framework for automatic edge milling of aircraft skins. First, an edge probability detector is proposed by the spatial tangent continuity (STC) to provide the essential reference. Second, we propose a hierarchical branch searching (HBS) method to hierarchically strip the desired milling edges from the raw point cloud, which consists of three graded progressive steps: branch backbone generation, branch extension, and branch pruning. We demonstrate the performance of the proposed method on both synthetic models and aircraft skin workpieces. The proposed method outperforms the other baselines and shows accurate edges for the edge milling task.

title: Pick-up sticks problems for exponential and Pareto distributions
abstract: We deal with the following two pick-up sticks problems: given an integer n greater than or equal to 3, we choose n sticks with independent random lengths from an exponential distribution or Pareto type I distribution, and we are interested in the probability that no three of them can be the sides of a triangle. In case of exponential distribution, this problem has been solved by other authors: the probability in question is equal to $n!/\big((F_3-1)(F_4-1)\cdots(F_{n+2}-1)\big)$, where $(F_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ is the sequence of Fibonacci numbers. We give a new, self-contained and detailed proof for this formula, which uses a different method compared to the earlier ones. In case of Pareto type I distribution, we derive new formulae for the corresponding probability.

title: WiSI: Wireless-in-the-Loop Self-Improvement
abstract: The growing autonomy of AI agents has enabled self-improvement, where agents iteratively refine their programs through execution feedback and performance evaluation. As these agents increasingly operate in physical environments and rely on wireless connectivity, communication conditions become an integral part of their improvement process. However, existing approaches largely assume ideal communication, overlooking how wireless conditions shape both the feedback that guides program modifications and the evaluation outcomes that determine which modifications survive. This challenge is further complicated by the coupling between agent behavior and wireless connectivity, as agents influence their own communication conditions through mobility and transmission decisions. To address this problem, we propose WiSI, a wireless-in-the-loop self-improvement framework that integrates spatiotemporal wireless channels, edge-assisted perception, and Large Language Model-driven program improvement. By incorporating wireless execution into the improvement loop, WiSI reveals how wireless execution experience shapes the generation and retention of program structures, and investigates the wireless conditions needed for robust improvement. Experiments show that agents improved under ideal links achieve only 40.0% task success under congestion, compared with 77.2% when improved under realistic wireless conditions. More importantly, wireless-aware feedback and selection jointly enable agents to discover and retain communication-efficient program structures that outperform parameter tuning and remain robust even with inaccurate run-time channel observations. We further find that moderate-load or mixed-network evaluation maintains strong performance across deployment conditions, while simplified models preserving link-rate statistics achieve comparable results without detailed spatial channel information.

title: Entropy-Gated Dynamic Rectification for Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) routinely name objects that are absent from the image. Latent steering can reduce this failure in one model forward pass, but a fixed gate treats early and late decoding steps by the same criterion. We observe that predictive entropy varies sharply within free-running generation, while states that commit to short answers occupy a narrow, confident band. We exploit this temporal mismatch by using uncertainty as a causally available, token-local control signal for an existing steering gate. We propose Entropy-Gated Dynamic Rectification (EGDR), which lowers the intervention threshold when entropy derived from the preceding step's already available logits is high and retains the calibrated operating point when it is low. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, the underlying static gate lowers CHAIR CS/CI from 53.00/15.30 to 32.00/14.30; replacing only its constant threshold with EGDR further lowers them to 29.00/13.60. At a matched 58% intervention rate, the corresponding static control obtains 30.50/14.00. The gain over the static gate holds on LLaVA-NeXT-7B and grows with the generation budget, while POPE scores and general multimodal capability remain effectively unchanged. EGDR requires no additional model forward pass and adds roughly 2% measured latency. Our code is available at https://github.com/alvi-uiu/EGDR.

title: DualEvolve: Dual-Level Self-Evolution of Mechanism and Orchestration for Recommendation
abstract: Recommender systems are widely used in e-commerce and content platforms, where improvement requires repeated model design, training optimization, and experimental validation. Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate this development cycle. Sustained autonomous improvement requires agents to improve both recommendation models and their development workflows. However, task-performance-driven approaches select updates mainly by candidates' final scores, without a separate optimization signal for experimentation quality. We therefore present DualEvolve, a dual-level framework that co-evolves recommendation mechanisms and agent orchestration toward recursive self-improvement. Inner evolution revises model and training code using task feedback to improve recommendation performance. Outer evolution scores the inner-loop experimental process, updates harness and skill rules using these scores and execution traces, and adjusts orchestration choices based on next-round scores to improve the quality of subsequent experiments. Experiments on MovieLens-1M and three Amazon Reviews 2023 subsets cover four recommendation methods and 16 settings. DualEvolve achieves higher test means than Base, OpenEvolve, and DeepEvolve in all 64 setting-metric comparisons, with macro-averaged relative gains over DeepEvolve of 7.6% (HR@5) and 9.0% (NDCG@5).

title: Amplified transport variability in granular slope flows near the critical angle
abstract: Mechanical disturbances such as seismic shaking can set a granular slope in motion. Understanding the resulting transport before arrest is important for predicting topographic change, assessing landslide hazards and controlling powder flows in industrial processes. Experiments show that smaller disturbances can trigger avalanches and larger areas are mobilized as slopes approach their stability limit. Yet how much transport varies between events under the same macroscopic conditions and forcing remains unclear. Here we use numerical simulations to show that transport variability is amplified near the critical angle. We apply identical basal pulses to static granular layers with the same macroscopic conditions but different initial particle configurations. Although the mean transport increases approximately in inverse proportion to the angular distance from the critical angle, the standard deviation increases even faster and can exceed the mean. Thus, identical forcing can produce widely different transport amounts. Deterministic constitutive laws that assign a unique response to given macroscopic conditions cannot capture this variability. We introduce fluctuations into the energy balance to develop a stochastic model that captures the main features of the broadening transport distribution. These results show that assessing transport near the critical angle requires considering its distribution, not just its mean, and motivate constitutive descriptions that incorporate fluctuations.

title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
abstract: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.

title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
abstract: We introduce the Pauli-Correlator Autoencoder (PCAE), a hybrid quantum--classical architecture for image reconstruction. PCAE splits an image into patches and compresses each patch as a matrix product state (MPS). A small quantum circuit turns each compressed patch into a few measured numbers, and a classical neural network rebuilds the patch from these numbers and the patch position. A learnable energy term, taken from physics, is added to training and tracked as training proceeds. Two versions place the six qubits on a line (PCAE1D) or on a grid (PCAE2D). An averaging step makes the PCAE2D features follow rotations and reflections of the image exactly. Trained on one image at a time, PCAE2D rebuilds images from six public datasets with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 25.8 to 41.6 decibels. On CIFAR-10 images not used in training, a formula-based stand-in for the PCAE2D features performs within 1 decibel of several simpler classical methods. Five trained models also run on real IBM quantum computers without retraining, and rebuild images at 25.90 to 31.52 decibels. A short argument and a synthetic test show that, with a linear final layer, measuring qubits in pairs is needed for targets built from products of inputs. These results show that PCAE works as a hybrid model that rebuilds varied images and runs on today's quantum hardware at the six-qubit scale.

title: Transitional Fluid-Ablation Interactions on a Compression Ramp at Mach 8
abstract: Direct numerical simulations (DNS) are performed for a Mach 8 flow over a 15 degree compression ramp undergoing ablation to analyze fluid-ablation interaction (FAI) effects on instability growth and transition of the high-speed boundary layer. Wind-tunnel experiments at these conditions show characteristic heating streaks which are first replicated for laminar flow over an inert ramp. Perturbations superimposed on the laminar baseflow are informed by stability calculations. The ramp is then replaced by a low-temperature ablator in our DNS and the interaction of the streaks with the ablating surface is examined. Ablation models implemented in two independently-developed fluid dynamics solvers are used to study this problem. Overall, both solvers have shown an excellent agreement regarding heat fluxes, mass blowing rates, and recession patterns. Numerical experiments are performed to assess the impact of accelerating recession and of higher amplitude perturbations. We demonstrate accurate predictions of ablative recession and present novel findings regarding its influence on the perturbation evolution for this configuration.

title: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete
abstract: Binary prefix coding assigns prefix-free binary words to symbols to minimize their frequency-weighted cost. Huffman solved the equal-letter-cost case in polynomial time in 1952 [Proc. IRE'52]. For unequal letter costs, Karp gave an integer-programming formulation in 1961 [IRE Trans. Inf. Theory'61]. Exact polynomial-time algorithms for fixed integer costs were given by Golin and Rote [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory'98] and Bradford, Golin, Larmore, and Rytter [J. Algorithms'02]. For input-dependent costs, Golin, Mathieu, and Young gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme [SICOMP'12]. The exact complexity when letter costs are part of the input had remained unresolved. We resolve this $65$-year-old problem by proving that deciding whether there exists a binary prefix-free code of frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers $(M,M+1)$ supplied as part of the input. All frequencies, letter costs, and thresholds are encoded in binary. Consequently, finding an optimal code is NP-hard. Our proof uses two polynomial-time reductions, starting from Planar Independent Set. The intermediate problem prescribes the number of leaves at each depth of a full ordered binary tree and minimizes a signed linear score on their sorted right-edge counts. The first reduction represents an independent-set verification program by a tree growing level by level. A fixed-profile identity converts narrow coordinate restrictions into linear penalties that enforce the computation. The second reduction adds large dyadic terms to the symbol frequencies to force prescribed depths. These terms contribute a constant to the weighted number of ones, leaving smaller signed perturbations to reproduce the tree score.

title: Photometric calibration of the 4m ILMT data
abstract: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is a 4-meter survey telescope continuously observing towards the zenith in the SDSS g', r', and i' bands. This survey telescope is designed to detect various astrophysical transients (for example, supernovae) and very faint objects like multiply-imaged quasars and low surface brightness galaxies. Ensuring accurate and stable calibration of supernova (SN) and quasar measurements is essential for studying their intrinsic variability and long-term brightness evolution. In this work, we present a dedicated calibration approach tailored for ILMT point-like object observations obtained in Time Delayed Integration (TDI) mode. Using ZTF reference sources cross-matched with the Pan-STARRS1 catalog, we derive robust photometric zero-points along the ILMT scan. This calibration procedure enables the production of consistent, high-precision SN and quasar light curves, suitable for variability studies, structure-function analysis, and future reverberation-mapping applications.

title: Probabilistic Modeling of Photon Interaction Chains in a Silicon Detector
abstract: Compton camera imaging relies on the positions and energies of multiple photon interactions recorded in the detector. In silicon detectors that resolve individual interactions, these measurements do not directly provide the causal interaction order, and in nuclear medicine applications the photon may also have scattered in the object before entering the detector. We present a probabilistic model for photon interaction chains in a silicon detector and use it for two inference tasks at the event level: interaction order inference and classification of primary versus object-scattered photons. The model combines photon transport based on Compton scattering and attenuation with a detector response model. It is evaluated on Monte Carlo data for monoenergetic point sources at 140~keV and 511~keV, with and without a cylindrical water phantom. For interaction chains of length two to four, the maximum a posteriori order estimate gives high accuracy in the case without a phantom, exceeding 0.95 for all chain lengths at 511~keV, and decreasing with increasing phantom radius. The gap between the two highest posterior order probabilities provides a confidence measure for the ordering estimate and can be used to increase accuracy at the cost of reduced retention. For scatter classification, likelihood-ratio testing yields receiver operating characteristic curves with area under the curve above 0.85 across all phantom radii considered. These results support the use of probabilistic modeling of measured interaction sequences for inference directly at the event level, and show that both interaction ordering and scatter discrimination can be treated within a common framework.

title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
abstract: We present an approach to mathematically formalizing PTX, an approach that allows modeling and reasoning about patterns common in GPU kernels for Deep Learning, including acquire-release, tensor cores, proxies, async operations, multi-kernel pipelines and data-dependent control flow. We implement it in Lean and use it to prove the correctness of simple implementations of a WGMMA GEMM kernel, FlashAttention, and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline.

title: Relative-Error Composite Federated Optimization with One Server-Side Proximal Step per Round
abstract: We consider deterministic composite federated optimization, in which distributed smooth client objectives are combined with a shared, possibly nonsmooth, regularizer. We propose Relative-Error Composite FedDyn (REC-FedDyn), an inexact method that supports partial participation, with one server-side proximal evaluation per communication round. REC-FedDyn employs a directly testable relative-error criterion that allows each client to independently control the accuracy of its local subproblem, without a server-side acceptance test. We establish almost-sure iterate convergence for strongly convex and convex problems, almost-sure asymptotic stationarity for nonconvex problems, and communication and parallel gradient-evaluation complexity bounds, all under partial participation and without assuming bounded data heterogeneity. Experiments on image inpainting, fMRI prediction, and neural-network classification with structured regularization demonstrate efficiency and robustness across levels of data heterogeneity and client participation.

title: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models
abstract: Among 291 surveyed open-weight language model repositories (280 distinct embedding tables), 52.6% of untied gated and hybrid checkpoints (20/38) contain reachable input embeddings with norms below $10^{-6}$, compared with 0% of weight-tied models. Such near-zero rows can arise during pretraining when unseen rare or template tokens receive zero input gradients while AdamW weight decay shrinks untied embeddings. In tested Transformer configurations, non-initial positions or a BOS token prevent this failure mode. In gated sequence models (Mamba, Gated DeltaNet, xLSTM), a near-zero token can amplify input-embedding gradients by more than 30 orders of magnitude (up to 35). At zero input, current-token readout factors (SiLU gates or linear queries) vanish, suppressing historical-state readout. Residual RMS values can then fall below the square root of the RMSNorm floor across consecutive layers, causing Pre-RMSNorm to amplify backward gradients by up to $10^3$ per layer. When a gradient entry exceeds $1.84 \times 10^{19}$, FP32 global-norm clipping in PyTorch, Hugging Face Trainer, and FSDP2 can overflow to infinity and zero the current batch's gradients. In Telugu continual pretraining of Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, this discards updates on approximately 20% of steps and leaves triggered rows frozen. We propose two remedies. For released checkpoints, GroupClip decouples input-embedding clipping using a 64-bit or rescaled norm; its rescaled implementation eliminates update loss and heals triggered rows in one step with negligible measured end-to-end overhead. For pretraining, GateFloor ($\mathrm{SiLU}(z) + δ$, $δ\in [0.01, 0.1]$) keeps the gate positive at zero input, reducing near-zero gradients by 28 orders of magnitude in experiments up to 370M parameters, with perplexity comparable to the baseline.

title: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design
abstract: The classical model-based optimal design criteria (D-, T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality) are usually motivated via the Cramér--Rao bound as optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). This paper offers a complementary reading in which each criterion appears asymptotically as $N \to \infty$ as the leading-order term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the FIM entering through the Bernstein--von Mises limit. The Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of the posterior relative to the prior recovers D-optimality (classically known); a reverse KL of the prior relative to the posterior recovers T-optimality (here defined as maximization of the trace of the FIM, following one common convention) and its weighted-trace generalization; and a first-order approximation of the squared 2-Wasserstein distance recovers L-, C- and A-optimality. The five criteria emerge as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template, indexed by three choices: the dissimilarity, the prior parametrization, and the approximation scheme used to evaluate it (e.g.\ Taylor expansions of the matrix square root). For the weighted criteria, the Gaussian prior covariance encodes the criterion's weight matrix, so any choice of weights corresponds to a specific prior in the family. The T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality derivations appear novel to the best of my knowledge. A sixth criterion, E-optimality, is recovered not as an independent expected-dissimilarity limit but as a min-max robustification of C-optimality against uncertainty in the modeler's prior direction. The framework is extended to distinguish between a designer's prior over unknown parameters at design time and a modeler's prior used for posterior inference, recovering the classical expected information gain objective as a special case.

title: BMO preservation and quasiconformality
abstract: In dimension $n\ge2$, a homeomorphism of $R^n$ preserving BMO space therein was proved to be quasiconformal, up to an orientation reversing reflection.

title: DynOSeg: Dynamic Object Segmentation via Motion-Geometry Fusion
abstract: Moving Object Segmentation (MOS) detects and separates dynamic objects from the static background in a video, which plays a fundamental role in dynamic-scene understanding. Most MOS methods rely on pure visual motion cues alone, such as optical flow or point tracks, which is inherently ambiguous due to the compounded camera and object motions as well as motion-induced appearance changes, e.g. shadows and reflections. Naive fusion of additional information such as depth and semantics, however, cannot leverage their complementarity to the fullest extent. We therefore propose DynOSeg, a novel MOS approach that takes on a two-stage fusion structure. DynOSeg first combines a geometry-aware residual map and depth encoding into a geometric representation of motion, delineating camera motions and object dynamics. We then further incorporate semantic features to refine object understanding. We have additionally curated a diverse training corpus including CARLA-MOS, a new synthetic urban-driving dataset for MOS training. Our experiments show that DynOSeg consistently outperforms published state-of-the-art MOS methods across a diverse range of datasets. Our code and pretrained models can be found at https://github.com/ACFR-RPG/DynOSeg

title: Nuisance structure and the detection boundary for population size: how profiling can change a rate, not only a constant
abstract: A system contains an unknown number $N$ of units, each failing at an unknown common rate, each unit is removed once it fails. The failure-rate declines as units are removed, but after only a few failures the decline is too slight to distinguish from a constant rate, and the maximum-likelihood estimate of $N$ is infinite with substantial probability. This is a well-known feature of the model, but its probability has not been quantified. We show that about $N^{2/3}$ failures are needed before a finite population can be distinguished from an inexhaustible one, and that at this scale the profile log-likelihood ratio converges to that of a Gaussian shift experiment, in which an infinite estimate occurs with a calculable probability. The exponent is not a property of the model alone. Profiling annihilates the Taylor terms that the nuisance-parameters can reproduce, and detectability is governed by the first surviving term. For example, unknown drift in testing-effort reproduces the linear term, leaving a quadratic survivor and raising the requirement to $N^{4/5}$; in general the critical scale is $N^{2q/(2q+1)}$ for a survivor of order $q$. We obtain the limiting-law of the estimator, the null likelihood ratio distribution, and confidence sets that may be unbounded.

title: Trustworthiness as a Measurement Structure for Task Conformance in 6G Service Chains
abstract: A 6G service crosses a chain of stages from different vendors, and its contract binds class-conditioned guarantees at the terminal interface: in the packet relay chain studied here, a priority class is owed a timely-delivery rate and a loss ceiling. We define trustworthiness as conformance of the delivered per-class distribution of outcomes to the contract and develop the measurement structure this forces. Two results fix its form: a discrepancy that treats outcomes interchangeably cannot express contract preferences, and no single expectation-valued score that determines the contracted terminal expectations can be carried from stage to stage once two or more contracted indicators remain independent at some stage. The minimal record is one signed number per independent contracted indicator, which the downstream design data carry to the terminal exactly; classical scalar trust models are the single-indicator case. The terminal deviation splits exactly into per-stage contributions. Transition logs at a stage estimate its contribution without reconstructing its full deployed behavior, a stage at its design behavior is flagged at most at a declared rate whatever traffic it receives, and the estimates bracket each stage's share of the terminal deviation at explicit confidence. In the three-relay chain, a relay that either deprioritizes premium traffic or has degraded capacity violates the same clause with identical contracted evidence: the transition audit localizes the relay in 300 of 300 windows and brackets its share of the deviation, and a diagnostic separates the causes.

title: SourceFlow: Collaborative Source Coupling for Flow-Based Recommendation
