These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
abstract: Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^eμ^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of \[ \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg] \] for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$. The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

title: She Sees Shells by the Stellar Shore: A Kinematic View of NGC 253's Stellar Halo
abstract: The stellar halos of nearby galaxies are fossil records of ancient mergers, providing insight into the formation and growth of these systems. These halos often contain substructure in the form of streams, shells, and debris fields that make up dynamically young remnants of past accretions. These remnants can be probed with resolved-star spectroscopic observations, giving insight into the kinematics of bygone satellite companions. Such observations have been made for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda, but are much more challenging and expensive to do outside the Local Group. The Local Volume has an abundance of MW-mass galaxies with richly structured halos, such as NGC 253. Leveraging the power of Magellan's M2FS fiber-fed multiobject spectrograph, we have obtained medium-resolution spectra of 225 stars centered on NGC 253's southwestern shell. These spectra enabled us to make the first-ever measurement of the resolved-star stellar kinematics for 89 stars in NGC 253's halo. We also detect substructure in several ways and identify regions likely to be accreted and in-situ, finding among them a low-velocity region coincident with the previously reported SW shell we believe was accreted recently, and an in-situ component that traces the outer disk. After subtracting NGC 253's systemic velocity, we measure median line-of-sight velocities of $-34_{-12}^{+16}$ km/s and $167_{-14}^{+16}$ km/s for the accreted and in-situ populations, respectively. This work highlights the utility of kinematics to differentiate between accreted and in-situ stars, and acts as a pathfinder for future observations with next-generation 30 m telescopes and wide-field multiobject spectrographs.

title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $γ$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $ΔE = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

title: Krylov meets Fock: Complementary lenses on quantum dynamics
abstract: Quantum dynamics in Krylov space can be represented by a particle hopping on a chain whose sites are the Krylov basis vectors. The goal of this work is to extend this idea to the Fock basis, which in turn allows the description of a generic dynamics in terms of a more general, possibly higher-dimensional lattice. This construction has been dubbed the Fock state lattice (FSL), since its sites are identified with Fock states. To analyze the dynamics on the FSL we introduce various measures of the spread of a state, comparing them among themselves and with their Krylov counterparts. We apply our analysis to two models of light-matter interaction studied in quantum optics: the multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings and the Dicke models. We find that, whenever the FSL is not a chain, the corresponding dynamics provides insights complementary to the Krylov space analysis and, in some instances, greater analytical control. For example, we obtain analytical results for the FSL spread measures of the Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit and determine that their scaling in time detects the superradiant phase transition.

title: ReveaLLAGN 2: Exploring the Nuclear Gas and Stellar Kinematics of Nearby LLAGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU
abstract: Low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGN) represent the most common mode of black hole accretion in the local Universe, yet their nuclear structure, stellar and gas kinematics remain poorly constrained at parsec scales. We investigate the nuclear regions of eight nearby representative LLAGN, the ReveaLLAGN sample: M87, M104, M94, M81, NGC1052, NGC4258, NGC5128 and NGC4395. Using JWST/NIRSpec data, we probe the stellar, molecular hydrogen, hydrogen recombination, and high ionisation coronal lines kinematics and their spatial distribution, exploring how detectability and spatial distributions of these lines vary across different Eddington ratios. The stellar LOSV maps reveal a slowly rotating disk in the nuclei of all our targets, characterised by an anti-correlation with the h3 Gauss-Hermite moment. Across the sample, the stellar velocity dispersion rises toward the central black hole. Only in M104 and M94 does the velocity dispersion display a more intricate pattern that departs from a simple disk configuration, indicating the presence of multiple kinematic components in these galaxies. Across the sample, the gas distribution and kinematics exhibit rotation that is frequently decoupled from the stellar rotation, suggesting that the stellar gravitational potential is decoupled from the current accretion state. The gas kinematics are often visually aligned with the radio jet, presenting broader velocity dispersions along the jet direction. Line-ratio maps indicate that the dominant excitation mechanism is photoionisation by the central AGN, with mechanical heating from shocks becoming important only at higher Eddington ratios. Across the sample, we detect coronal lines in all LLAGN when using nuclear-aperture spectra, and we can obtain spatially resolved kinematics only in NGC5128 and NGC4395, the highest Eddington ratio sources.

title: Boosted Entanglement Swapping
abstract: Entanglement swapping entangles photons that never interacted directly. When implemented with linear optics, its success probability is upper bounded by $50\%$, due to the limited efficiency of linear-optical Bell-state measurements. Here, we demonstrate boosted entanglement swapping using an ancilla-assisted linear-optical Bell-state measurement, which raises the theoretical success probability to $62.5\%$ and allows all four Bell states to be identified. We measure an acceptance rate of $p_{\mathrm{a}}^{\mathrm{b}}=(69.39\pm0.39)\%$ with an average fidelity of the swapped states of $\langle F^{\mathrm{b}}\rangle=(76.6\pm1.0)\%$. We implement this protocol using photons at 1550 nm, making it well suited for quantum repeaters, where it could enable more efficient entanglement distribution. Beyond quantum communication, it could also enhance fusion-based quantum computing.

title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
abstract: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/α_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $α_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $ω\leq α_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schrödinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.

title: SMEFT Constraints on Top Electroweak Couplings and a Composite Higgs Interpretation
abstract: Recent LHC measurements of $tWZ$, $t\bar t Z$ and single top production provide complementary probes of top quark electroweak interactions. We incorporate these measurements into a global Standard Model effective field theory analysis of 46 independent dimension-six Wilson coefficients at linear order. The updated fit remains compatible with the Standard Model at $95\%$ CL, and favors negative values of $C_{Hq}^{(-)}\equiv C_{Hq}^{(1)}-C_{Hq}^{(3)}$ and $C_{Ht}$, with central values suggestive of TeV scale new physics. We also present an effective composite Higgs model based on a two-site description that realizes this pattern of Wilson coefficients through partial compositeness. The model includes custodial symmetry and protection of the $Z\bar b_L b_L$ coupling. A fermion bitriplet generates the required left-handed shift, and an additional embedding of the right-handed top allows negative contributions to $C_{Ht}$ from both fermion and spin-one exchange. Scanning four right-handed top embeddings, we find parameter regions within the $68\%$ CL contour that are compatible with electroweak precision data, Higgs coupling measurements and applicable direct searches. The $T$ parameter limits the negative fermionic contribution to $C_{Ht}$, favoring a spin-one contribution of comparable or greater magnitude. Larger $SU(2)_R$ representations extend the reach toward negative $C_{Ht}$, and also enhance four-quark interactions that increase the four-top cross section, in the direction favored by current measurements. The mechanism connects the preferred top electroweak shifts to complementary tests through single production of quarks with electric charge $-4/3$, modified Higgs couplings and four-top production.

title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
abstract: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

title: Bounded decoding complexity in transversal circuits with magic state injection
abstract: We characterize the complexity of space-time correlated decoding for fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures that implement Clifford gates transversally and realize non-Clifford gates via magic state injection. In this approach, decoding graphs for logical measurements are constructed by backpropagating measurement operators through the circuit, which causes them to grow with circuit volume. However, the decoding volume can be substantially reduced by decoding measurements sequentially, committing corrections, and excluding syndrome data that have already been processed for earlier measurements. For random circuits, we find that the resulting decoding volume associated with mid-circuit measurements approaches a stationary average that is determined by the density of magic state injections. Large decoding instances are exponentially suppressed. We further find that the decoding complexity is remarkably insensitive to different choices of measurement products to be decoded, and that the same qualitative behavior persists across different circuit connectivities and Clifford gate ensembles. These results suggest that scalable space-time correlated decoding of large-scale fault-tolerant quantum algorithms is achievable since the magic states that make transversal architectures universal also keep them decodable.

title: Neuromorphic Camera for Multi-Target Pointing Acquisition and Tracking in Free Space Optical Communication
abstract: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC) applications must achieve both low jitter and a large Field of View (FoV) to support beacon acquisition and multi-target tracking. While conventional frame-based sensors provide the necessary angular coverage, their performance is limited by latency, available frame-rate, and motion blur. This work explores and demonstrates the application of an event-based vision sensor for PAT tasks in FSOC. The system employs a neuromorphic sensor that asynchronously records brightness changes (events) with microsecond-level temporal resolution. The main contribution of this paper is a comparative analysis of event-based tracking algorithms for the simultaneous acquisition and tracking of multiple optical beacons that operate directly on this asynchronous stream. The performance of these strategies is validated on an experimental dataset representing realistic operational conditions for dynamic High-Altitude Platform (HAP) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. The analysis compares key metrics, such as tracking accuracy and processing latency, under various signal-to-background conditions.

title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The spectral shape of gravitational waves predicted in this scenario is markedly different compared to the case of domain walls remaining sub-dominant all the way till annihilation. These gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

title: The Power and Limits of Money Burning in Bilateral Trade
abstract: We study the power of money burning in bilateral trade. In this problem, a seller owns an indivisible item, a buyer would like to acquire it, and each of these two traders has a private value for the item and the values are sampled from independent distributions. We ask whether the traders can benefit from a mechanism that burns money, that is, one that charges the buyer more than it pays the seller, so that neither trader enjoys the difference (money burnt is a loss for the traders). Is it possible that the traders will ever be better off if the trade mechanism can burn money? For Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms and for deterministic dominant-strategy incentive-compatible (DSIC) mechanisms, it is known that money burning is always a waste and can only hurt the traders. Maybe surprisingly, we show that once a DSIC mechanism can use randomization, money burning can significantly benefit the traders, and the gain of each of them can be arbitrarily large. In contrast, we show that the power of DSIC randomized mechanisms that burn money is still very limited in the sense that they cannot guarantee any constant fraction of the first-best gains-from-trade.

title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage. Empirical experiments across varying numbers of objectives demonstrate the effectiveness of OGC-DPO over existing active preference learning methods under the same annotation cost. Further analysis demonstrates that informative conflicts, rather than being uniformly harmful, provide a useful policy training signal.

title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
abstract: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. The hierarchical framework comprises: (1) A unified motion-force controller tracks the reference motion while applying the commanded force to the world. (2) A high-level force planner that issues a force command online based on object state and proprioception observations. In simulation and on hardware, Ctrl-F completes loco-manipulation that demands large, sustained interaction force and adjusts its command online as the load changes, both out of reach of a force-blind tracker. On hardware, Ctrl-F demonstrates hand-based dragging, pushing, and lifting, as well as foot-based kicking, successfully manipulating boxes weighing up to 20kg in pushing and kicking tasks where the force-blind baseline fails, while adapting online to additional loads introduced mid-task.

title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.

title: From Claws to Conferences: Device-Independent Key Agreement Beyond Non-Signaling
abstract: Device-independent conference key agreement (DI-CKA) allows a group of users to establish a common secret key without trusting the internal operation of their quantum devices. Existing DI-CKA protocols derive their security from multipartite Bell tests and therefore require the device components not to communicate during each round. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first DI-CKA protocol that removes this non-signaling assumption: all interfaces and their mutual communication are treated as one untrusted device, which only has to be quantum polynomial-time while the protocol runs. Assuming that the Learning With Errors (LWE) problem is hard for quantum algorithms with quantum advice during the execution, we prove finite-size security against coherent attacks, in which the device may keep quantum memory and correlate and adapt its behavior across rounds. For two parties the protocol is a computational DI-QKD protocol with an explicit finite-size proof against coherent attacks. Technically, we lift the claw state underlying the classical-verifier test of Brakerski et al.\ (FOCS 2018) to multipartite entanglement, obtaining a \emph{GHZ-correlated claw state}. %that is prepared with one coherent claw-free function evaluation and $N-1$ CNOT gates. We then introduce the \emph{collective adaptive hardcore bit}, a multiparty generalization of the adaptive hardcore bit of Brakerski et al.\ and show that it follows from the original property by a tight reduction. Combined with Jordan's lemma, an entropic uncertainty relation, and entropy accumulation, this certifies smooth min-entropy of the key against an external quantum adversary. Our protocol achieves \emph{everlasting security}: LWE needs to hold only during the execution, because the final key is statistically secure and its secrecy persists even if LWE is broken after the protocol ends.

title: Fast and accurate false-alarm probabilities for linear detection statistics in Poisson noise
abstract: Detecting weak signals in noisy data often requires calculating the statistical significance, or false- alarm probability, of a detection statistic. When the underlying noise follows Poisson statistics, as in low-count measurements such as photon-starved astronomical images, this calculation becomes non- trivial, and existing approaches typically rely on extensive simulations to estimate detection thresholds. We derive an accurate and efficient solution for computing false-alarm probabilities for arbitrary linear detection statistics under Poisson noise. We show that the detection statistic is a compound Poisson random variable, which unlocks efficient implementations based on the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and the Panjer recursion. The method is exact up to numerical discretization, accelerates computation by several orders of magnitude compared with simulations, and enables evaluation of false-alarm probabilities computationally inaccessible through simulation. Although motivated by low-count astronomical imaging, the framework applies broadly to detection problems involving Poisson-distributed events. It transforms the computation of detection significance under Poisson noise from a simulation problem into a deterministic numerical calculation. We provide open-source Python and MATLAB implementations.

title: Improved lower bounds on the approximability of Multiway Cut using Sherali-Adams relaxations
abstract: The Multiway Cut problem is among the most well-studied problems in the area of combinatorial approximation algorithms. The currently best approximation ratio for the problem is 1.2787, obtained recently by the authors (2026). The best lower bound on the approximation ratio that can be achieved for the problem in polynomial time, under the Unique Games Conjecture (UGC), is 1.20016, obtained by Bérczi, Chandrasekaran, Király, and Madan (2020), building on and slightly improving a bound of $\frac65=1.2$, obtained by Angelidakis, Makarychev, and Manurangsi (2017) by introducing the important framework of non-opposite multiway cuts. We obtain a substantially improved lower bound of 1.22232 on the approximation ratio of the Multiway Cut problem. Manokaran, Naor, Raghavendra, and Schwartz (2008) showed that under UGC, the approximation ratio of Multiway Cut is equal to the integrality ratio of a simple LP relaxation, known as the CKR relaxation, introduced by Călinescu, Karloff, and Rabani (2000). Thus, stronger LP relaxations are not required for obtaining an optimal approximation algorithm for the problem. We show, however, that relying on the framework of Angelidakis, Makarychev, and Manurangsi (2017), stronger LP relaxations from the Sherali-Adams hierarchy for non-opposite multiway cuts can be used to obtain improved integrality ratios for the CKR relaxation, and hence improved lower bounds on the approximation ratio of the Multiway Cut problem. One of the novel features of our analysis is considering a continuous limit of discrete LPs defined on a simplex. Our proof of the new 1.22232 bound is completely analytic. We also present strong numerical evidence that suggests that our techniques can be used to improve the lower bound to at least 1.23003.

title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling stale or conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources. We introduce SlackBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on realistic research and engineering workflows that require joint reasoning over workplace communication and evolving repository state. Grounded in privacy-preserving reenactments of real academic research projects, SlackBench provides reproducible environments with realistic multi-party dialogue, evolving decisions, and corresponding code changes grounded in GitHub repositories and Google Docs. It contains 140 queries spanning heterogeneous-source agentic search, abstention on unanswerable or false-premise questions, goal-directed summarization, and circumstance inference over long conversations. These tasks are not reducible to static corpus question answering: agents must determine which conversations matter, traverse threads, inspect repository state, and synthesize evidence across communication and code artifacts. Across 33 frontier models and agent harnesses, the best system scores around 80% and most agents score below 66%, highlighting substantial headroom for improvement. SlackBench thus provides an extensible framework for evaluating agents in collaborative work environments. The SlackBench dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuanzhiMao/SlackBench .

title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.

title: Where models of minimal height are hard to find: cubic rational maps with a multiple fixed point
abstract: Given a rational point of the moduli space of cubic rational maps, we seek a map in its class with the smallest integer coefficients. A recent algorithm (Shaska, arXiv:2610.33990) combines an exact descent and minimisation of the resultant with a reduction and a local search; it is nearly exact where the minimal height is known. Beyond that range, a certified deeper search shows that the instances in which a smaller model lies beyond its reach are not random: a classifier predicts them from the six invariants of the point, and asking what it relies on leads to an exact algebraic surface, the maps with a triple fixed point. Invariant theory and the stability hypothesis of reduction theory (Hutz and Stoll, 2019) then identify the larger locus that contains it: the hypersurface $ξ_1^3=6ξ_2^2$ of maps with a multiple fixed point, on which the fixed-point quartic is not stable. It holds most of the hard instances. On it the two invariants of the fixed-point quartic are $(ξ_1,ξ_2)=(6m^2,6m^3)$ for an integer $m\ge0$; we parametrise the integer points of the surface, and show that on its generic part the sign of $ξ_5$ is the sign of the cubic coefficient at the parabolic fixed point. A covariant defined on the locus, added to the reduction, resolves only a minority of the hard instances: they appear to be mainly a matter of the search's reach. These findings lead to a certified structured search that never returns a larger model than the original algorithm and finds most of the smaller models within reach, also at heights not used to design it, at a small multiple of its running time.

title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
abstract: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret text but lack numerical precision, while Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are quantitatively accurate but cannot reason about the effects of text. Moreover, the lack of large-scale paired multimodal datasets limits progress in bridging this gap. In this work, we address this challenge by providing a scalable approach for generating realistic multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs. Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. We align the two models in stages, first fine-tuning the LLM via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward tied to covariate-induced improvement in forecasting performance, and then fine-tuning the TSFM on covariates generated by the aligned LLM. Our experiments show that models trained on our synthetic multimodal corpus generalize to real benchmarks spanning finance, economics, weather, traffic, and security. Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o. Code, checkpoints, and the evaluation datasets are publicly available.

title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
abstract: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.

title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
abstract: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. We also propose BACE (Belief-Aware Critic with Epistemic tracking), a lightweight action chooser method on top of a frozen LM backbone, and show that BACE more consistently chooses the optimal number of clarifying questions than methods such as GRPO and ArCHer.

title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
abstract: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. All methods are applied to mock surveys based on cosmological simulations that include generating individual tracer stars, convolving their phase-space coordinates with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored models of the survey selection functions. By comparing the performance on these mocks, we quantify how systematic biases from both methodology assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium impact each estimate. The mock-based systematics, which differ by method and tracer, are used to correct the individual estimates and to derive joint estimates using a rigorous formalism that accounts for per-method biases and residual correlations between methods. We obtain a joint estimate of the mass within 80 kpc to be $M(r < 80 \mathrm{\,kpc}) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} \times 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$ and a virial mass estimate of $M_\mathrm{200c} = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} \times 10^{12}$ M$_\odot$, with similar results when combining only RRL-based or BHB-based measurements. These results provide a roadmap for future DESI efforts, as well as those in other spectroscopic surveys, to reliably constrain the mass of our Galaxy.

title: Mock catalogues for the DESI DR2 Milky Way mass modeling effort
abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) survey is an ongoing campaign to obtain millions of spectra, including for stars within the Milky Way. One of DESI's Key Projects for its second data release (DR2) is to measure the mass of the Milky Way using a variety of techniques applied to six-dimensional kinematics of distant halo stars. We present mock surveys generated from the Auriga cosmological simulations (AuriDESI) that are used to validate these techniques in several companion studies. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are tailored to reflect key features of the DR2 Key Project dataset, including the selection of RR Lyrae and blue horizontal branch stars, uncertainties on line-of-sight velocities and proper motions, and variation in observational completeness within the survey footprint. We discuss how well the resulting AuriDESI tracer catalogues compare to their observed DESI counterparts, including suggesting improvements that can be generalized to similar mock survey efforts within the community. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are publicly available on Zenodo.

title: Constraining the Milky Way Mass profile with data driven distribution function using DESI DR2 halo stars
abstract: We employ a novel data-driven dynamical modeling method, the empirical distribution function (emPDF), to constrain the Milky Way mass profile using a large sample of halo stars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Milky Way Survey (DESI MWS). The method does not assume any functional form of the tracer distribution. Deviations from the steady-state assumption and the effects of observational errors are further tested and calibrated using a number of realistic mock observations (AuriDESI). Applying the calibrated method to two classes of tracers in DESI, we derive a best-constrained virial mass and concentration of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.05_{-0.12}^{+0.21}(_{-0.18}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.20_{-0.16}^{+0.11}(_{-0.24}^{+0.20})$ for BHBs. For RR Lyrae stars we derive $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.15_{-0.14}^{+0.22}(_{-0.19}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.12}^{+0.09}(_{-0.18}^{+0.16})$. The uncertainties quoted outside and within brackets are statistical and total errors including systematic errors calibrated from AuriDESI, respectively. The two tracer populations provide overall consistent measurements of the MW halo mass profile. Combining the halo star constraints with the independent constraint from satellite dynamics, we derive a robust and precise final measurement of the MW halo parameters of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.12_{-0.05}^{+0.05}(_{-0.04}^{+0.06})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.03}^{+0.05}(_{-0.07}^{+0.05})$, with correlation coefficients of $ρ=-0.90(-0.54)$.

title: A distribution-function estimate of the Milky Way mass profile from outer halo stars in DESI DR2
abstract: We present measurements of the Milky Way mass using blue horizontal-branch (BHB) and RR Lyrae (RRL) stars from the second data release of DESI (DR2), covering its first three years of operations. We employ 279 BHBs and 213 RRLs at $\sim\!50$--$80$\,kpc from the Galactic center, selected from catalogs roughly twice as large as those of DESI DR1, used in our previous mass measurement. We apply the Galactic Mass Estimator (GME), a hierarchical Bayesian framework that assumes power-law forms for the potential and the tracer density, and accounts for distance and velocity uncertainties. Validating the method on 24 AuriDESI mock catalogs (six Auriga halos at four viewing angles), we find that it overestimates the enclosed mass by $\sim\!15\%$ at 80\,kpc, and correct our results accordingly. We obtain $M(<80\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.64^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$ and $0.53^{+0.05}_{-0.05} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$ for BHBs and RRLs, respectively, while including Sagittarius stream stars lowers these masses by $\sim\!10$\%. Extrapolating to 100\,kpc, we obtain $M(<100\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.74^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$ and $0.62^{+0.06}_{-0.07} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, and anchoring an NFW halo to our GME constraints at 65\,kpc yields virial masses of $M_{200} = 1.12^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $0.89^{+0.11}_{-0.10} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$. BHBs yield systematically higher masses than RRLs across the full radial range, reflecting the impact of tracer choice even within a single method. This work is part of a wider DESI DR2 Key Project effort to measure the Milky Way mass and constrain systematics arising from different samples and methodologies.

title: From Activation to Intervention: Interpreting Sparse Visual Features through Reconstruction
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose visual representations into individual features, offering a promising basis for explaining model behavior. Interpreting these features typically relies on images or pixel regions that most strongly activate them. However, this evidence becomes ambiguous when multiple features with different semantics frequently activate in the same locations, such as texture and color in the same patterns. We propose Reconstructive SAE Intervention (RecSAEI), a framework that shifts feature explanation from passive observation to active visual reconstruction. By intervening on representations along SAE decoder directions and reconstructing the visual output, we provide direct evidence of a feature's semantic meaning. We demonstrate that our method successfully disambiguates feature meanings across multiple datasets and vision encoders. Furthermore, our framework grounds [CLS] SAE interventions in a sparse set of patch SAE decoder directions. Beyond stable target response, this attribution also exposes the compositional relationship between elementary visual patterns and high-level semantics. Our results advocate for intervention reconstruction as an essential complementary signal for explaining neural networks.

title: On Parallel Sums of Set-Valued Operators: Monotonicity, Paramonotonicity, and Decomposition Invariance
abstract: In this paper, we investigate structural properties of the parallel sum of set-valued operators in a real Hilbert space, with particular emphasis on monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, and paramonotonicity. We examine the decomposition-invariance property of the parallel sum of two paramonotone operators and provide a direct proof based on monotonicity and the equality of admissible decompositions. This approach establishes the required orthogonality relations without invoking the Attouch--Th{é}ra Duality duality framework. We also revisit the classical maximal-monotonicity property of the parallel sum and present an alternative graph-based derivation involving an auxiliary shifted operator. Furthermore, we study the parallel sum of a set-valued operator and the normal cone operator associated with a closed linear subspace. Explicit characterizations of its values, domain, and range are presented, and a decomposition-independent representation is obtained under paramonotonicity through the orthogonality of the underlying subspaces. These results provide a unified and self-contained treatment of selected properties of parallel sums and clarify the role of paramonotonicity in their structural behavior.

title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Building on the single-agent construction that embeds control barrier function (CBF) constraints into reverse-diffusion updates, we: (i) formalize joint safe sets as intersections of per-agent and pairwise barrier sets; (ii) derive centralized and decentralized (communication-aware) constrained denoising procedures with provable invariance under mild assumptions; (iii) address local-trap and deadlock phenomena via time-varying specifications and liveness CBFs; and (iv) develop a lightweight benchmarking suite including a multi-agent Maze2D domain. Empirically, MA-SafeDiffuser reduces violation counts relative to unconstrained diffusion baselines, while retaining planning quality. We provide algorithms, proofs, and reference implementations.

title: On symmetry and monotonicity of singular solutions to critical fractional Hartree equations
abstract: This paper continues the study initiated in \cite{GuJevnikarYang2026b} of fractional Hartree equations with zero capacity singular sets. We are concerned here with the critical case, i.e. \[ (-Δ)^s u=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ} \frac{u^{2_{μ,s}^*}(y)}{|x-y|^μ}\,d y\right)u^{2_{μ,s}^*-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ, \] where $N\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $μ\in(0,N)$ and $2_{μ,s}^*$ is the critical exponent associated to this class of problems. We prove symmetry and monotonicity with respect to the singular set $Γ$. The Kelvin transforms centered at regular points provide sufficient decay at infinity for both the transformed solutions and their associated Hartree coefficients, without imposing global integrability assumptions. Combined with a moving plane argument and a comparison estimate in critical Lebesgue spaces, this allows the moving plane method to cover the full interaction range.

title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.

title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order Hölder Smoothness and Uniform Convexity
abstract: In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose $p^{th}$-order derivatives are Hölder continuous with degree $ν$ and parameter $H$, and that are uniformly convex with degree $q$ and parameter $σ$. When these orders match, namely, $q = p + ν$, we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order $p$ requires $Ω\left(\left(\frac{H}σ\right)^{\frac{2}{3(p+ν)-2}}\log\frac{Δ_0}ε\right)$ oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of $Δ_0$ to $ε$. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global Hölder smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.

title: The Confidence Score: a New Measure on Kernels
abstract: Across a wide range of applications, kernel measures are used to tune hyperparameters, select among candidate kernels, and assess the suitability of kernels for specific learning tasks. For classification, kernel measures are used to predict which kernels may produce accurate kernel classifiers. Many existing kernel measures, such as alignment to the ideal kernel, are designed to reward kernels which captures all samples from the same class as similar. While effective in many settings, this requirement is unnecessarily restrictive for classification, where classes may exhibit substantial internal structure. In this work, the "Confidence Score", a new kernel measure, is proposed. Unlike alignment-to-the-ideal kernel measures, the Confidence Score measures the alignment between an encoding of the ground truth and that ground truth projected by the kernel, allowing kernels that preserve intra-class structure to achieve high scores. Through experiments, it is demonstrated that the Confidence Score exhibits a higher correlation with classification accuracy across a variety of kernels on both real-world and synthetic datasets, compared to select other kernel measures.

title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

title: Schwinger Effect with a Transversal Boundary
abstract: We study the effect of a boundary on pair production by an electric field. In particular, we are interested in the case in which the electric field has a normal component with respect to the boundary. This is essentially more complex than pure tangential fields due to the reflection of created particles against the boundary. In this article we provide the explicit solution for the case of an instantaneous electric pulse which is spatially uniform and normal to a flat surface. We show that pair production exhibits a bulk contribution that accounts for the interference of reflected modes, in addition to a purely boundary term. To conclude, we give an expression for the total particle production due to an irrotational electric pulse in a region delimited by an arbitrary boundary.

title: Hamilton cycles in bicirculants with non-coprime connection sets
abstract: A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_{m-1}\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in T\} \cup \{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in S\}.$ Some of the well known bicirculants include the generalized Petersen graphs and Cayley graphs of dihedral groups. In 1983, Brian Alspach proved that the only non-hamiltonian generalized Petersen graphs are $G(m,2)$ where $m \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. In a recent paper we conjectured that this is the only exception among regular connected bicirculants of degree at least two, and we have verified the conjecture for bicirculants with $|S|\le 3$. Results of Alspach, Chen and Dean imply that the conjecture also holds for all bicirculants with $m$ even and $\gcd(m,S)=1$. In this paper, we show that the conjecture holds for all bicirculants with $|S| \geq 4$ and $\gcd(m,S)>1$ such that $R\cup T$ contains an element that is not coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$ and, if $m$ is odd, is also not divisibile by $\gcd(m, S)$ or $R \cap T$ contains an element that is coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$.

title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
abstract: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $π$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $π$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.

title: Data-Driven Stochastic LQR Control with Probabilistic Guarantees and Uncertainty Refinement
abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for the direct, data-driven synthesis of the stochastic linear- quadratic output-feedback control for linear systems sub- ject to process and measurement noise. Using delayed input-output measurements, we derive a lifted parameter- ization together with an equivalent lifted linear quadratic cost, enabling controller synthesis without explicitly identi- fying the lifted dynamics. Two complementary closed-loop formulations, based on trajectory and covariance represen- tations, are then developed, whose uncertainties depend only on the realized but unknown lifted noise. We char- acterize the relative performance of the two formulations in finite-data regimes. High-probability uncertainty bounds are developed for realized noises, leading to a convex optimization solution to the problem, whose feasibility cer- tifies probabilistic mean-square stability (p-MSS) and per- formance guarantees. To reduce conservatism, Gaussian zonotopes are used to refine uncertainty sets by elimi- nating noise realizations inconsistent with measured data, and a novel intersection rule enables the consistent fusion of data-driven and physics-informed information. These components are integrated into an adaptive framework that unifies indirect (identification-based) and direct (control- oriented) data-driven linear-quadratic output-feedback con- trol. Unlike existing direct data-driven LQR methods that verify stability a posteriori, our by-construction approach achieves robust stability alongside reduced conservatism and superior performance. Simulation results show that the proposed controller approaches the ideal optimal solution while outperforming existing data-driven methods under noisy measurements.

title: One-third Hölder stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
abstract: We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ρ$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $μ$, $ν$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_μ-T_ν\rVert_{L^2(ρ)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(μ,ν)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincaré inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.

title: On the Detectability of Compact Multi-Planet Systems via Gravitational Microlensing
abstract: Compact multi-planet systems orbiting ultracool dwarfs, such as TRAPPIST-1, may be a major population of terrestrial worlds with poorly constrained demographics. Individual close-in planets are expected to escape microlensing detection, but whether a compact system can produce a detectable collective signal remains to be quantified. We calculate the microlensing signal from each TRAPPIST-1 planet, and of all seven combined, if the system were a lens toward the bulge. For a 0.09 $M_\odot$ lens at 4 kpc, $R_E \approx 1.21$ AU, placing the planets at $s = 0.010$--$0.051~θ_E$, 12--63 times interior to the lensing zone. We measure each signal as the residual after fitting a single-lens model, which accounts for the barycentric dipole. Because the quadrupole term cancels between the two images to first order, the residual scales as the octupole ($q s^3$), reaching $|δA / A| \sim 10^{-6}$. The seven planets combined yield $Δχ^2 \sim 10^{-3}$ even at 1~mmag precision, five orders of magnitude below the standard detection threshold. Detection requires increasing all planet masses by a factor of $\sim$300, whereas the resonant chain loses its guarantee of Hill stability at a factor of $\sim$7. Only a lens within $\sim$15 pc of the source or the Sun places the outer planets in the lensing zone. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is therefore not expected to detect a TRAPPIST-1-like system through microlensing, whereas its transit channel in the same fields can detect such planets in large numbers, marking a sharp boundary in the Galactic census between microlensing and transit sensitivity.

title: Identifying Compact Object Candidates using Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations and Jerks
abstract: Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) provides astrometric measurements for more than a billion sources, hundreds of thousands of which have non-single-star astrometric solutions that indicate deviations from linear proper motion. Although sources with orbital solutions have been extensively inspected for compact objects via the astrometric mass function, two other solution types--the 7-parameter constant-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbfμ}$, and the 9-parameter variable-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbfμ}$ and $\ddot{\mathbfμ}$--have not been as carefully explored. In this work, we develop a methodology for selecting sources within the Gaia DR3 9-parameter non-single-star astrometric solutions that are most likely to host massive compact companions. We assume that a source is the luminous star in a binary orbit around a dark object and derive analytic expressions for the sky-projected accelerations and jerks for three binary populations with different orbit approximations: inclined eccentric, face-on eccentric, and face-on circular. Using POSYDON, we develop a fourth, more realistic population of binaries, each consisting of a luminous star and a black hole. For each population, we address observational biases using gaiamock and select only the systems it fits with a 9-parameter solution. We find that binaries likely to host massive compact companions can be identified from the characteristic joint astrometric accelerations and jerks exhibited by the luminous stars, despite 9-parameter fits under-constraining full orbits. Finally, to illustrate the utility of our approach, we analyze a historical object of interest, HD 12871, and examine 9-parameter fits of Gaia BH3-like binaries.

title: Quantum theory of damping: A new approach to temporal evolution of density operator without the rotating wave approximation
abstract: The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing dissipative dynamics of the open quantum system context. Its conventional derivation, however, relies on the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), which neglects the counter rotating terms in the system-reservoir interaction. Here, we derive a generalized Lindblad master equation beyond the RWA within the density operator formalism, retaining the full systemreservoir coupling. We consider two prototypical open quantum systems, a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized field, each interacting with thermal or squeezed reservoirs described by the Wigner-Weisskopf theory. The resulting master equations are applied to the evolution of representative physical observables and compared with the conventional RWA based formulation. We show that counter-rotating terms produce significant modifications to the dissipative dynamics and therefore cannot, in general, be neglected. For a thermal reservoir, increasing the mean thermal photon number, nth, enhances the decay of hσ^yi beyond the RWA but suppresses it within the RWA. Likewise, the evolution of hσ^zi exhibits opposite damping behavior with increasing Γt and squeezing parameter r. These findings demonstrate the importance of including counter rotating terms for an accurate description of open quantum systems.

title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
abstract: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction
abstract: LLMs can repair noisy OCR transcripts of historical documents, but they also change text that was already correct. We propose EditVeto, a veto gate placed after a full-context LLM rewrite. The rewrite is character-aligned to the OCR input, its differences are split into blocks, and a 0.6B-parameter gate keeps or reverts each block. An oracle analysis motivates the design: given the true error locations, per-span generation is worse than no correction, whereas vetoing a full rewrite's edits helps. Trained on rewrites by two Qwen3 models and evaluated, frozen, on the eight HIPE-OCRepair-2026 test sets, the gate improves all five rewriters tested, two of them unseen in training: weighted cMER falls by 0.0026-0.0044 and the preference score rises by 0.15-0.25 (paired bootstrap, p ~ 0.0002 each). On published competition outputs it lowers cMER for three of four teams but raises it for the winning run (0.0050 to 0.0065). In a second, disclosed test look, a retrained gate still improves LoRA-tuned rewriters (cMER -0.0011 to -0.0021), and an ensemble of their gated edits reaches a cMER of 0.0069 and a preference score of 0.928, mostly through fine-tuning and pooling rather than gating. Built only on public models and data, it is behind the winner (0.0050) and tied with the second-ranked run (0.0071), both from the only team using domain pre-training, and ahead of all other published runs. A third, secondary look shows the unchanged gate improving zero-shot Qwen3.8-27B (cMER 0.0114 to 0.0108) but only the preference score of its LoRA-tuned version.

title: ProofStudio: Five Proof Assistants in the Browser
abstract: Recent advances in AI-assisted proof automation are extending the use of proof assistants in software verification and mathematics. However, greater proof automation does not remove users' responsibility to assess whether formal statements capture their intended requirements, making education in formal specification and reasoning essential. To lower the installation and learning barriers associated with mature proof assistants, we present ProofStudio, a browser-based environment integrating Isabelle/HOL, Lean, Rocq, HOL4, and HOL Light with corresponding worked examples, preconfigured proof search, and contextual AI assistance. With ProofStudio, users can explore formal specifications and proofs across five systems without local installation, inspecting native prover feedback and experimenting with automation through a common interface.

title: Higher-order quantum information inequalities and error-correction of non-Markovian noise
abstract: Defining entropy of a quantum channel has become a challenge with potential candidates recently reported in literature. In this Article, it is taken under consideration the entropy of a quantum channel defined as the quantum entropy of its associated Choi state. The consequences presented here of such approach is two-fold. First, the limitations on the information-processing of quantum channels are assessed, leading to the \emph{higher-order quantum information inequalities}. Those are then considered as useful witnesses of non-Markovian effects beyond a given number of quantum side-channels in a quantum process. Importantly, the presentation is given with the application of the methods for the study of examples. Second, such approach provides a characterization on the condition for the recovery of quantum channel preparations under non-Markovian noise. Such result is a straightforward extension of standard error-correction conditions which gives further meaning to the higher-order information measures defined here.

title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference
abstract: Whole-page ranking jointly optimizes advertisements and organic content to balance business outcomes and user engagement under complex layout and business constraints. Existing non-autoregressive (NAR) approaches enable efficient page generation but typically score candidate items independently of previously selected items, limiting their ability to capture order-dependent interactions. Autoregressive (AR) methods address this limitation through sequential conditioning, but incur substantial inference overhead that challenges large-scale deployment. Bridging this quality-efficiency gap remains a challenge in industrial whole-page ranking. We propose Multi-Item Scoring (MIS), a prefix-aware NAR-style framework that incorporates sequential context into efficient multi-item scoring. MIS integrates global candidate interactions, localized prefix conditioning, and position-aware scoring within a shared representation architecture. By computing reusable representations once per request and performing lightweight prefix-conditioned scoring during constrained beam search, MIS captures important sequential dependencies without repeated full-model inference. Experiments on KuaiRand-1K and RL4RS demonstrate that MIS approaches the generation quality of an autoregressive CGA baseline while achieving 4.07x and 3.54x faster CPU decoding, respectively. In a randomized evaluation on a large-scale social-video platform, MIS improves the realization metric by 0.104% and watch time by 0.058%, while reducing ranking-service CPU consumption by 9.73%. These results demonstrate that prefix-aware multi-item scoring can narrow the quality gap between NAR and AR generation while retaining the efficiency required for industrial scalability.

title: Generalized Hyperrectangular Prediction Sets in Multivariate Conformal Prediction
abstract: In multivariate conformal prediction, many nonconformity scores yield prediction sets with complex geometry (e.g., ellipsoids or density level sets) that are difficult to interpret and visualize. Hyperrectangles offer a practical alternative by providing one interval per output. We extend this notion to Cartesian products of arbitrary one-dimensional sets, which we call generalized hyperrectangles. We introduce a rectangularization framework that turns any continuous multivariate nonconformity score, or conditional density, into one yielding generalized hyperrectangular prediction sets with finite-sample coverage. We establish key geometric properties of our rectangularization framework and provide useful intuitions on generalized hyperrectangles. We further establish a representation theorem showing that a broad class of hyperrectangular conformal methods based on max-aggregated coordinate-wise scores can be interpreted as rectangularizations of implicit conditional densities. Through synthetic and real-world experiments, we quantify the efficiency cost of rectangularization, while highlighting its benefits, especially for practical applications of uncertainty quantification.

title: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures
abstract: In this paper, three operations on Gibbs probability measures are studied: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting. The resulting measures are shown to be Gibbs probability measures with explicit expressions for their objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors. These measures are further characterized as unique solutions to optimization problems involving linear combinations of the original objective functions, subject to either relative entropy regularization or relative entropy constraints. When the reference measures are probability measures, geometric interpretations of these three operations are established involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics.A central result is the equivalence between nesting and normalized log-linear combinations of Gibbs probability measures. These results are then applied to supervised machine learning with Gibbs algorithms, which are represented by Gibbs probability measures. In this context, either through nesting or log-linear combinations, Gibbs algorithms trained on local datasets are used to form new Gibbs algorithms trained upon the aggregation of all local training datasets. Interestingly, the parameters of such operations, determine the weights of each training data point on the aggregated dataset. %Operations on local Gibbs probability measures are shown to control the contributions of training data. This observation is leveraged for achieving: (a) exact machine unlearning in centralized, decentralized, and federated learning systems; and (b) centralized-equivalent performance, in the sense of producing algorithms trained on the aggregation of all local datasets in decentralized and federated learning .

title: Mueller Matrix Decomposition for a General Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer
abstract: This work develops a Mueller matrix decomposition that factors a nondepolarizing Mueller matrix $M$ into three components $M = T_1 D T_2$, where the elements $D$, which correspond to a diagonal Jones matrix, are separated from rotations and circular diattenuation $T_1, T_2$. This decomposition is employed to calibrate a prototype reflective rotating-compensator ellipsometer designed to operate using extreme ultraviolet (EUV) radiation. This decomposition allows for the measurement of the full Mueller matrix of a sample without full knowledge of the compensators or the source polarization, while allowing for significant diattenuation and retardance for the optics. A generalization of the decomposition is developed for depolarizing Mueller matrices, and the technique is tested on reflection data collected on an Au mirror at $266$ nm.

title: FedSharp: Byzantine Robust Decentralized Federated Learning Under Noisy Channel
abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server but remains vulnerable to data heterogeneity, Byzantine attacks, and channel noise. We show that noise accumulates as models propagate across nodes, becoming increasingly significant as the learning rate decays. Moreover, accumulated noise enables Byzantine attackers to exploit loss-based model selection by mimicking honest model averages.
