To make this contract practical, SEER uses a CAS-based dual-layer event queue: local event queues preserve per-entity causal order, while a parallel executive list exposes ready work to global worker threads. SEER further uses STPA, a preflight-guided thread-pool selection mechanism that combines short runtime traces with static workload and hardware features. We evaluate SEER on two parameterized MARL workloads: compute-intensive UAV swarm control (Aircraft) and communication-intensive wireless management (PCS). On Aircraft, SEER reduces inference latency by 16.2\% over the baseline. On PCS, SEER reduces environment-execution latency by 46.9\%, 19.5\%, and 64.9\% over ROSS-T, NBSE, and ROOT-Sim, respectively.

title: Atomic Parity Violation: Standard Model Tests
abstract: Atomic parity violation (APV) offers a sensitive high-precision, low-energy test of the Standard Model and a powerful probe of new physics. It played a significant role in confirming the nature of the neutral weak currents, and gives unique information about fundamental weak parameters and possible new physics, reaching energies well into the TeV scale and beyond. In this chapter, we provide a pedagogical introduction to the fascinating field of APV. The underlying mechanisms are introduced, an overview of past and ongoing experiments is presented, including prospects for measuring parity violation in molecules, and the critical role of electronic structure theory in interpreting the experiments is described. The importance of the nuclear anapole moment and other nuclear-spin-dependent parity-violating contributions for understanding nuclear structure and weak nuclear forces is highlighted. We discuss the current challenges and identify the most important and pressing goals in this field, which promises exciting discoveries in the coming years.

title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
abstract: It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles. Fragment-based representations have therefore emerged as an effective strategy for incorporating chemically meaningful inductive biases, as exemplified by molecular fingerprints and fragment-based attention mechanisms. However, many existing fragmentation-based machine learning methods rely on predefined chemical rules, which may yield suboptimal fragmentation for previously unseen or chemically unfamiliar structures and often overlook the importance of multiscale molecular representations. To address these limitations, we formulate molecular fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization problem inspired by the k-center formulation, where the number of clusters is not fixed a priori but emerges from the specified radius, and propose a geometry-based fragmentation method that partitions arbitrary molecular or material structures using largely geometric information, without relying on predefined chemical fragmentation rules. The method provides flexible control over fragment size, enabling the construction of multiscale fragment representations for scale-adaptive modeling. Building on this framework, we develop a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism that integrates multiscale structural information and incorporate it into a multimodal machine learning model combining p-SMILES representations with three-dimensional (3D) conformational information. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that incorporating 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties over models based exclusively on p-SMILES representations. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses further provide insights into the physical relevance of the learned representations.

title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
abstract: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields. Tracing over the unmeasured idler continuum yields an exact spatial Lindblad master equation along the propagation axis, proving that spatial dephasing is driven by an information divergence flux determined by the SPACS overlap fidelity $F = |α|^2/(1+|α|^2)$. Uniting this relative-entropy flow with quotient measurement theory (detailed in Section~S3 of the Supplemental Material), we rigorously resolve nonlocal wavefunction collapse into local coset projections---explaining macroscopic state reduction without superluminal signaling. This exact open-system framework simultaneously saturates the wave-particle-entanglement triality [T.~H.~Yoon and M.~Cho, Sci.~Adv.~\textbf{7}, eabi9268 (2021)] and anchors hardware-native time--frequency Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill stabilizers to the comb symplectic structure.

title: LithoSAGE: Spatially Adaptive and Geometrically Equivariant Neural Operators for Computational Lithography
abstract: Operator learning offers an efficient surrogate for lithography simulation, replacing costly numerical solutions with direct model inference. However, existing learning architectures are not designed to simultaneously provide geometric equivariance and adaptability to layout windows with different physical extents, and thus their generalization capability is limited. To address this problem, we propose LithoSAGE, a spatially adaptive and geometrically equivariant neural operator method trained on lithography data. Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.

title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

title: When GeoFMs Meet VHR: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery
abstract: Geospatial foundation models are a widely adopted starting point for remote sensing tasks. Most are pretrained on Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat imagery at a ground sampling distance (GSD) of 10m or coarser. Many applications instead rely on very high resolution (VHR) imagery, where individual buildings, roads, and amenities are resolved. We study which pretraining regimes transfer well to this scale. We introduce VHR-Bench, a benchmark suite of ten datasets at 1.5m GSD or finer spanning five task families, eight application domains, and both satellite and aerial platforms. We evaluate twelve encoders in three pretraining tiers with frozen backbones at two training-data fractions. We find that both pretraining on large natural-image collections and VHR-specific pretraining transfer effectively to VHR tasks, with complementary strengths. SkySense leads when labels are scarce; at the full label fraction the web-pretrained DINOv3 ViT-L edges ahead, with the two close together there. Encoders pretrained only on Sentinel-scale imagery transfer least well under RGB input. Guided by these complementary results, we continue the self-supervised pretraining of DINOv3 ViT-L on 1.02 million held-out VHR tiles and evaluate the resulting encoder without changing the downstream protocol. The continued model gives a clear improvement over the released backbone when labels are scarce and a modest one at the full fraction, at no increase in inference parameters or compute. These findings support a generalize-then-specialize strategy: already strong, broad natural-image pretraining can be further improved by a short VHR continuation stage while preserving its general visual features.

title: Extensions to the Dubins Airplane Method - Flight Performance Constraints in Uniform Wind
abstract: This paper extends the Dubins Airplane Method to generate trajectories for fixed-wing aircraft that remain within flight performance limits in the presence of uniform wind. Within the field of runtime-efficient trajectory generation for fixed-wing aircraft, the Dubins Airplane Method represents a well-received and widely adopted compromise between algorithmic complexity, runtime efficiency, and solution quality. However, its simplistic kinematic model restricts its ability to generate safe and feasible trajectories, especially in the presence of wind. As a mathematical foundation to overcome these limitations, a set of closed-form equations are derived that relate flight performance constraints to kinematic constraints. Building upon existing methods that use trochoids for planning of 2D trajectories in uniform wind, this paper presents a set of iterative algorithms for planning versatile 3D trajectories composed of trochoidal or circular turns and straight flight segments, with constant vertical speed, constant thrust or smooth longitudinal transitions. The presented methods comprise a flexible and modular framework for runtime-efficient generation of performance-aware trajectories based on parametric curves without the need for numerical trajectory representations.

title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement
abstract: Current language-guided 3D object placement typically predicts a rigid 6-DoF pose, ignoring the physical reality that indoor placements are dictated by contact. Consequently, predicted poses often float, interpenetrate supports, or fail to deform soft surfaces. We propose Deformable Contact-Aware Placement (DCAP), a framework that reframes placement as a drop-to-equilibrium process. Rather than predicting a static pose, DCAP constructs a semantic release state that specifies the drop location, object scale, and deformable components, allowing a coupled rigid-deformable simulator to settle the object under gravity and friction. This explicitly separates semantic intent from physical realization. Evaluated on a benchmark of 2,063 prompt-asset-scene cases, DCAP significantly outperforms static baselines. On standard placements, it improves VLM Physics & Naturalness by 21.2 points and human preference by 26.5 points over the strongest raw rigid baseline, while reducing mean penetration depth by 72.3%. Compared to simulated rollout baselines, DCAP reduces residual speed by 72.1%. Ultimately, our results prove that physically accurate 3D placement requires modeling semantic intent and physical realization as strictly separate processes.

title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech
abstract: The exponential growth of textual and audiovisual information has made the task of automatic keyphrase extraction (KE) increasingly significant. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of contemporary theoretical approaches and practical solutions for KE across both text and speech modalities. The primary contribution of this work is its systematic synthesis of these often-disparate research strands into a unified analytical framework, highlighting the evolution of the field from statistical methods towards large language models (LLMs) and end-to-end speech processing. We examine the stages of KE, the characteristics of keyphrases in written and spoken language, and terminological nuances. Various methods for automatic KE are discussed and analyzed in detail: statistical, hybrid, machine learning-based, and structural. The review dedicates substantial attention to emerging paradigms, including keyphrase generation using LLMs, and provides a detailed overview of methodologies and challenges in automatic corpus annotation. Furthermore, we specifically analyze current directions and inherent difficulties in KE for spoken language, comparing transcript based and end-to-end acoustic approaches. This synthesis leads us to conclude that the field is moving towards a more integrated, context-aware paradigm. Future progress will depend on addressing key challenges such as data scarcity for low-resource languages, effective multimodal fusion, and the nuanced evaluation of generative KE systems.

title: Geometry-Aware Channel Aging in MIMO Systems: When Is Kronecker Separability Enough?
abstract: This letter investigates when Kronecker-separable spatial correlation approximates the covariance of multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels. We propose a geometry-aware channel model in which the same propagation environment determines both the Weischelberger spatial coupling matrix and the temporal correlation coefficient. The propagation environment follows a 3GPP-inspired clustered channel model. We consider a MIMO system affected by symbol-level channel aging caused by the user equipment's mobility. We schedule both uplink and downlink pilots, thereby deriving the respective spectral efficiencies (SEs) in the presence of imperfect channel state information. Numerical results show that channel aging's magnitude is strongly geometry-dependent, with diffuse propagation inducing greater temporal decorrelation and SE degradation than concentrated scattering. The results also identify regimes where Kronecker separability can be applied and regimes where geometry-aware Weischelberger coupling is needed.

title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
abstract: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$. The Bayesian evidence favours DBI in every compilation, moderately for Pantheon$+$ ($Δ\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq3.4$) and inconclusively for DES-SN5YR and Union3 ($Δ\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq0.6$-$0.7$). The field thaws naturally. Dark energy perturbations stay several orders of magnitude below matter perturbations, yet the noncanonical sound speed still alters the Hubble friction term, raising $S_8$ by only $\approx0.5σ$ relative to $Λ$CDM. Four independent diagnostics, namely the CPL parametrization, $Om(z)$, the statefinder hierarchy, and the growth index, all point to genuinely evolving dark energy rather than a cosmological constant. The thermal history is left intact, with negligible early dark energy. However, one limitation remains. Because $w_ϕ=\dotϕ^2-1\geq-1$, the phantom regime is out of reach, which is in line with the no-go theorem for a single minimally coupled scalar field, so the model cannot follow the DESI DR2 preference for an effective equation of state crossing $w=-1$.

title: A Unified Fractal Impedance Control Framework
abstract: Physical human--robot interaction requires controllers capable of maintaining intrinsically bounded interactions with the environment. The Fractal Impedance Controller (FIC) has been proven to guarantee these safety characteristics by design. This paper introduces the robotic implementation and experimental validation of its most advanced architecture: the Harmonic-Passive Motion Paradigm (H-PMP), an evolution of the Passive Motion Paradigm designed to mimic human-like interaction. Furthermore, we present a unified framework for FIC deployment, supported by an open-source software suite featuring ROS2, MuJoCo, and physical hardware integrations. Through three experiments conducted on a Kinova Gen3 arm (trajectory tracking, a wall press with sudden loss of contact, and learning-by-demonstration) we compare the H-PMP against earlier FIC architectures. The results demonstrate that the H-PMP achieves a seamless trade-off between admittance and impedance behaviours. This makes it ideal for deployment in unstructured environments, enabling the robot to transition between interaction modes with no computational overhead.

title: Quantum transport of vortex electrons in bending magnets and circular accelerators
abstract: Controlling the sizes and phase structure of single-particle wave packets in accelerators remains an experimental challenge and requires understanding how bending magnets transform these states. An important example is transporting relativistic vortex electrons through the magnets to a collision point while keeping a narrow orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distribution. We derive an effective Hamiltonian that accounts for the packet acceleration, employ it to obtain a generalized BMT-like equation, match the electron state at both magnet boundaries, and calculate the mean OAM and its variance. A half turn can reverse the mean OAM relative to the momentum while broadening its distribution, so recovering the mean does not ensure state recovery. We identify windows in packet sizes and bend angles for a small OAM spread and show that weak bends can produce narrow distributions with the mean OAM tilted relative to the momentum, making these states candidates for spatiotemporal vortices. For a few MeV electrons, we propose to use half-turn magnets that leave the mean OAM nearly antiparallel to the momentum while keeping its distribution narrow. For a circular orbit in a uniform field, the OAM variance after the exit grows as $N^2$ over $N$ turns, favoring linear accelerators, such as LINAC at JINR, for first experiments in MeV range.

title: Route-DMD: Distribution Matching Distillation with Task-Routed Mechanism for Speech Foundation Models
abstract: Speech foundation models built on flow matching handle generation, editing, and processing in one system, but every request costs 20-50 iterative steps, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) doubles each of them. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) trains a student that approaches the teacher's quality in a few steps, yet existing speech distillation work applies it to generation alone. We show that a distribution-matching objective does not serve every task: in separation, the noised states of erroneous student outputs deviate far from the teacher's training distribution, where its prediction is unreliable. Route-DMD therefore makes the objective task-dependent, routing the affected tasks to a regression loss and keeping decoupled distribution matching elsewhere. The student is initialized by consistency distillation, and teacher rollouts use adaptive projected guidance (APG) instead of CFG. Without CFG, the 4-step student matches the 32-step teacher on generation, editing, and processing tasks at a 4.5$\times$ end-to-end speedup.

title: Symmetry-Aware Surrogate-Assisted Testing of UAVs
abstract: We investigate a symmetry-aware surrogate-assisted testing approach for UAV autopilots. The proposed approach exploits geometric symmetries between flight missions by trans- forming obstacle configurations into a shared canonical coordi- nate frame. This enables a neural-network surrogate trained on a single reference mission to be reused across arbitrary missions, reducing the amount of high-fidelity simulation data required for training. The surrogate model is trained to predict the minimum clearance distance between a UAV and surrounding obstacles and is used to guide test generation towards safety-critical scenarios. We evaluate this approach using the Aerialist UAV test bench and benchmark its performance against techniques from the 2024 to 2026 UAV Testing Competitions. Results show that the approach achieves an average critical-test-case hit rate of 42% across the evaluated missions, compared with approximately 10% for the constrained-random baseline used to generate the training data. This approach also achieves high input diversity and competitive benchmark performance. However, our findings reveal limitations in transferring surrogate predictions across missions with differing flight-path characteristics, highlighting the boundaries of geometric canonicalization. To support reproducibility and future research, we provide the trained surrogate model and a dataset comprising more than 2,500 high-fidelity simulations.

title: Development of Anthropomorphic Arm for collaborative and Home Service Robot CHARMIE
abstract: Service Robots are becoming a reality and are progressing by leaps and bounds. Alongside this avenue of robotics is also the field of prosthetics, which is evolving rapidly. These topics are hot cakes in the industry and are widely developed. Some have one quality, and some have others, but are making a shoreline towards success. The development of arm and hand as individual or as a package is becoming common as more and more advanced collaborative robots come to the surface and join their human counterparts in the real world. This dissertation presents an open-source 3D-printed arm which was assembled and programmed on two fronts. The first is the control of the hand by utilising teleoperation with a camera and ML-based hand pose estimation. Secondly, it is the control via kinematics utilising the Denavit-Hartenberg method to define the motion and to find the position of the end effector in 3D space.

title: Probabilistic Relevance Decisions for Semantic Retrieval
abstract: Dense similarity supplies reusable corpus representations, while probabilistic relevance decisions offer query-dependent document scoring. We compare dense-only BGE-M3 with TypeSafe Jev Noul and OpenAI Decisions Predicate scores on the official BEIR SciFact test benchmark. The study evaluates 300 official test queries using identical positive-enriched 100-document pools and full-corpus dense retrieval followed by reranking at candidate depths of 50 and 100. Unlike the controlled pools, neither dense prefix receives positive injection. Jev has the highest observed Recall@5 and nDCG@10 under the evaluated conditions. At depth 50, full-corpus nDCG@10 is 0.6413 for BGE-M3, 0.7545 with OpenAI and 0.7805 with Jev. Extending depth from 50 to 100 increases known-positive candidate recall but produces small, uncertain final-effectiveness changes. All four paired-bootstrap depth intervals include zero. Unique-condition API scoring cost approximately doubles, while compatible cached decisions reduce incremental expenditure. OpenAI returns many exact-zero scores, and secondary exact-tie randomization reveals ranking sensitivity without replacing deterministic primary results. Top-100 latency mixes cached and new execution. Historical hybrid latency is a saved-component sum under different execution environments and timer boundaries. These exploratory, unadjusted analyses support relevance decisions as a complement to dense retrieval within this protocol, without establishing general superiority, probability calibration or equivalence between depths.

title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for language-model post-training, combining dense teacher supervision with training on student-generated trajectories. This creates a feedback loop where each update changes the student and thereby the training distribution that generates subsequent updates. Yet, how this feedback shapes learning and generalization remains poorly understood. We conduct a mechanistic analysis of OPD's learning dynamics, distinguishing the two feedback loop stages: conversion of the distillation signal into parameter updates, and broadcast through which these updates change predictions across prefixes and reshape the rollout distribution. This framework helps us understand both limited student responsiveness despite substantial teacher-student disagreement, and degeneration when updates that improve local teacher agreement also increase the probability of unsuccessful continuations, exposing the student to unreliable supervision in subsequent rollouts. Finally, we show that offline distillation can prepare a student for OPD without significantly improving immediate held-out accuracy. While OPD alone may degrade generation, it can yield substantial accuracy gains after sufficient offline preparation. Together, our results connect teacher supervision, student geometry, and the evolving rollout distribution in determining the learning dynamics of OPD and its effects on downstream performance.

title: Closed analytical formulas for the Ashley-Ritchie-Brandt and Jackson-McCarthy polarization functions
abstract: The $Z_{1}^{3}$ correction in the Bethe-Bloch formula that quantifies the electronic stopping power of matter for heavy charged particles is revisited. This correction accounts for the Barkas-Andersen effect. Ashley, Ritchie and Brandt (ARB) wrote it in terms of a non-relativistic polarization function, and Jackson and McCarthy (JM) obtained the relativistic counterpart. Both expressions involve intricate triple integrals. The present manuscript describes how the polarization functions of JM and ARB can be reduced to compact analytical formulas. The corresponding asymptotic behaviours are also found. The accuracy of two currently-used empirical fits to the ARB and JM polarization functions is assessed.

title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
abstract: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(EΦ^2+P(Φ))}dΦ$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $dΦ$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(Φ)=\fracλ{4}Φ^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.

title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
abstract: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.

title: Sigmoid Tensor Decomposition for Compact Representations of Binary Data
abstract: Nonlinear low-rank decompositions are receiving growing attention as a way to represent structured data with fewer parameters than conventional linear methods. Existing nonlinear approaches have focused mainly on matrices, which limits their ability to capture multidimensional structure. We propose a nonlinear tensor decomposition based on sigmoid nonlinearization in the Tucker and tensor-train formats. A binary tensor is represented by a low-rank real-valued score tensor, whose parameters are estimated by minimizing the binary cross-entropy loss. The resulting optimization problem is jointly nonconvex, but becomes convex with respect to one factor or score block when the remaining factors are fixed, as in the corresponding matrix case. We evaluate the method on several structured binary tensors and compare it with conventional Tucker and tensor-train decompositions across a range of common ranks. These results indicate that sigmoid nonlinearization is particularly effective in the low-rank regime, where it can provide more accurate binary reconstructions than conventional linear tensor decompositions at comparable model sizes.

title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image
abstract: In healthcare, protecting patient privacy is crucial due to the sensitivity of medical data and its extensive accessibility. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving training paradigm, making it an ideal solution for healthcare applications. A critical challenge in healthcare is that real-world medical data often exhibits long-tailed distributions in local and global views. Existing methods addressing long-tailed FL problem typically assume that the model will be evaluated on uniform test data distribution. However, practical test data in healthcare systems is often agnostic and unpredictable, leading to potential model failures in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a novel task termed Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning and propose GTAFL, a comprehensive framework to address this challenge. During the training stage, GTAFL employs adaptive re-sampling, expert classifier retraining, and self-supervised learning to correct biased classifiers and distorted feature spaces caused by long-tailed training distributions. During the inference stage, an ensemble mechanism combines retrained expert classifiers to handle test data with unknown distributions. Extensive experiments on CIFAR10 and two medical datasets manifest that our framework outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/cgy-lavine/GTAFL

title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
abstract: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\leγ(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $γ=γ_t=γ_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number. Independent dominating sets correspond to maximal intersecting families of subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$; we obtain a closed formula for the independent domination number of every finite non-local ring, which can be exponentially larger than the domination number. The proofs rest on the class sizes of the blow-up description of $\mathcal{G}(R)$ due to Moconja and Petrović, which we determine for every ring with finitely many maximal ideals, finite or infinite; with them, domination problems on $\mathcal{G}(R)$ become weighted extremal problems on subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$, and the formula for the independent domination number follows from the multiplicative form of these sizes. We also treat rings with infinitely many maximal ideals, graph polynomials, and lattices whose maximal ideals are prime.

title: Precision - Preserving Subtensor Inference for a 22B Joint Audio - Video Generator under a Fixed GPU Working Set
abstract: Complete-block offloading reduces model residency but requires each transferred block to fit the GPU budget. We present Precision-Preserving Subtensor Inference (PSI), a fixed-arena runtime that combines sub-block weight streaming with separately managed intermediate state for the BF16 LTX-2.5 22B joint audio-video transformer. The contribution is a construction whose managed GPU footprint is determined by reusable pages, live state, and bounded workspace, together with controls that separate resource use, transport correctness, and numerical fidelity. Its partitioned operators preserve the dense real-arithmetic construction under stated assumptions. Across nine matched full-prompt cases on RTX A6000, modified PSI reduces sampled transformer-process peak memory from 8,578 to 360 MiB relative to official MATH, while mean time for the eleven transformer invocations rises from 247.11 to 349.00 s. Its managed arena is 80 MiB. Complete native generation and a complete-block FLASH path both succeed under a fixed 3 GiB available-memory cap. The matched A6000 comparison and separate DGX Spark service suite both achieve 100% success in complete audiovisual decoding. FFN reuse lowers mean block time by 4.0% with unchanged BF16 outputs; a fixed-arithmetic one-token transport control preserves all saved states bitwise. Targeted bias and attention changes improve local and one-token numerical comparisons, while mean endpoint error increases across nine full-prompt cases. The construction enables BF16 audiovisual inference with an explicit transformer-memory budget and makes numerical fidelity a separate, testable property of the implementation.

title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
abstract: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

title: From maximum work to maximum power in an optimally controlled quantum Ising Otto engine
abstract: In finite-time quantum Otto engines, maximizing power requires balancing the duration of the unitary strokes against the losses from nonadiabatic excitations. We address this trade-off in an Otto engine with a free-fermion working medium, using quantum optimal control. Having determined the single-particle energy scales that maximize ideal work at fixed reservoir temperatures, we realize them as the two endpoint Hamiltonians of a transverse-field Ising chain, connected by a path that crosses the quantum critical point. Optimal control of the unitary strokes yields near-ideal work on a time scale growing linearly with system size, instead of quadratically as for linear driving. We derive a time-rescaling relation that maps protocols with different energy scales onto a single reference problem and, for complete thermalization strokes of fixed duration, use it to build an analytical model of the cycle power. The model predicts two competing maximum-power regimes: a slow branch that approaches the ideal work, and a fast, size-independent branch that trades work for a shorter cycle and dominates above a crossover size, in quantitative agreement with numerical optimal-control results. It also identifies power-optimal energy scales that differ from the work-optimal ones and further increase the power. Our results provide a predictive approach to jointly optimizing the operating conditions and finite-time dynamics of quantum heat engines.

title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
abstract: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $η$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ by determining the exact set of values that $η$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $η$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $η$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $η$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $η$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|η|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11ξ/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32ξ/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.

title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
abstract: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

title: The infrared unmodulated pyramid wavefront sensor: simulations, lab and on sky
abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets requires strong suppression of stellar light at small angular separations, achievable with extreme adaptive optics (XAO). The pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) is widely used for its sensitivity but suffers from nonlinearities and limited dynamic range. Modulation extends the range but reduces sensitivity and limits loop speed. We investigate an unmodulated infrared PWFS (IR-umPWFS), where the dynamic range scales with wavelength, removing the need for modulation and enabling faster operation. We adopt a 3-sided PWFS, which eliminates the roof defect of the classical 4-sided design. We assess its feasibility and performance through end-to-end simulations, lab tests, and on-sky observations on the PAPYRUS bench at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP), and compare it with a visible modulated PWFS (VIS-mPWFS). Simulations show reliable operation, reaching Strehl ratios up to ~60% at 1400 nm for seeing up to 4''. Infrared operation improves linearity, reduces optical-gain variations and modal cross-talk. Laboratory results validate the simulations and confirm the pyramid quality. On sky, stable closed-loop operation was achieved over three nights. Compared with the VIS-mPWFS at 500 Hz, the IR-umPWFS at 1000 Hz showed gains of ~1.63 in Strehl ratio and ~1.26 in encircled energy, and a ~2.03-fold reduction in residual wavefront error. The IR-umPWFS remained robust to tip-tilt offsets up to 3 lambda/D at 1400 nm. It is a strong candidate for future XAO systems: operating in the infrared extends the linear range sufficiently to remove the need for modulation, enabling higher loop speeds no longer limited by the modulation mirror, which contributed to the improved on-sky performance. The OHP turbulence (D/r0 ~ 17 at 1400 nm) is comparable to typical VLT conditions (D/r0 ~ 20), supporting the relevance of these results for VLT/RISTRETTO.

title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
abstract: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

title: Recovering the Length of a Path from its Signature
abstract: We prove the length conjecture of J. Chang, T. Lyons and H. Ni for paths of bounded variation for arbitrary real Banach spaces and any reasonable tensor (algebra) norms. More precisely, we establish the missing lower bound and in this way show that the length of a tree-reduced path is recovered from the asymptotic behaviour of its normalised signature. The main technical argument uses the norm duality and shuffle algebra to express natural powers of polygonal length approximations as combinations of linear functionals acting on restricted signatures, which are then glued by suitable integrations into a linear functional of controlled growth acting on the full signature. In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.

title: Economies of scale and the equity-efficiency trade-off: Evidence from a piped water network in rural Bangladesh
abstract: Policymakers who set prices for public infrastructure often anticipate an equity-efficiency trade-off: while higher prices could increase revenues from fee-paying users, helping to offset costs, they may reduce take-up among the poor. But this trade-off is fundamentally altered in the presence of economies of scale, which are common in infrastructure networks. We elicit willingness to pay for a household-level piped drinking water connection in rural Bangladesh, where truthful revelation of preferences is incentivized by the opportunity to connect to a new pipeline network that we construct, and we use project cost data to measure economies of scale. Combining the two, we show that the cost-effectiveness-maximizing price---that which minimizes the cost per connected household---is zero. Economies of scale strongly dominate revenues raised by user fees. More generally, the two conditions needed for a zero price to maximize cost-effectiveness are important economies of scale and high sensitivity of demand to prices near zero, which is well documented across developing countries. Since a zero price naturally maximizes equity, we conclude that economies of scale can eliminate the equity-efficiency trade-off.

title: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the $\ell^p$ Coefficient Norms
abstract: This paper advances the theory of reproducing kernel Banach spaces (RKBSs) by investigating the general $\ell^p$ regularization framework, with a particular focus on the non-convex regime $0<p<1$. While our preceding work established the foundation for RKBSs with the $\ell^1$ norm, the pursuit of stronger sparsity---closer to the $\ell^0$ pseudo-norm---naturally motivates this exploration into $\ell^p$ quasi-norms. For $0<p<1$, we construct reproducing kernel quasi-Banach spaces (RKQBSs) with $\ell^p$ quasi-norms and establish existence and sparsity results for interpolation and regularized learning under appropriate assumptions. We characterize the linear and relaxed representer theorems in terms of a generalized Lebesgue constant and derive bounds under kernel decay, sample spacing, and stability assumptions. For $p>1$, we construct RKBSs using a fixed countable dictionary, establish minimizer existence, and identify the optimal relaxed representer factor through an off-sample coefficient operator. These results reveal fundamental differences between the regimes $0<p<1$, $p=1$, and $p>1$. Numerical experiments compare the accuracy and sparsity of solutions for these three cases.

title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

title: Approaching quantum limits in sub-Rayleigh resolution using phase modulation optimization
abstract: Spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) has made significant progress in incoherent optical imaging and has been implemented through various experimental approaches. Holography-based SPADE is widely used in proof-of-principle experiments because of its low cost, stable optical arrangement, and ease of implementation. However, its low photon utilization severely limits its practical applications. Alternating Fourier transforms and phase modulations can implement unitary optical transformations. Building on this idea, we use backpropagation to optimize the phase profiles of spatial light modulators (SLMs) and thereby design quantum measurements that are efficient in both information and energy. We study centroid--separation estimation for two incoherent point sources, using Fisher information or the estimation errors of an auxiliary neural network estimator as optimization objectives. As the number of SLMs increases, the optimized measurements approach the quantum limits characterized by the quantum Cramér-Rao bound and the information-regret tradeoff relation. With a few SLMs, our method can outperform direct imaging, showing its potential for superresolution imaging.

title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
abstract: Modern classifiers remain sensitive to small input perturbations, while strong model-agnostic robustness certificates such as randomized smoothing are often too expensive for deployment, requiring an extensive number (e.g. 2000) of model forward passes per input. We propose a framework that delegates certification to a cheap proxy function while statistically controlling its deviation from the original sound certificate. Given an exchangeable unlabeled calibration set, we tune the proxy via robust conformal risk control to guarantee a bounded marginal (rather than pointwise) false-approval rate: the probability, over future inputs, that the proxy accepts an input whose prediction is flipped due to perturbation. The resulting proxy certificate can be used either as a standalone marginal certificate or as a fallback mechanism that invokes the expensive certificate only when the proxy rejects. We provide both single-sample and sample-heavy calibration recipes. Empirically, as a standalone certificate our method reduces the test-time certification cost to a single model forward while retaining much of the certified performance of randomized smoothing at small radii, and as a fallback it recovers the certified ratio of randomized smoothing at a more modest speedup. This enables cheap yet effective robustness guarantees for larger architectures such as vision transformers and language models.

title: Fast prediction of electron-beam parameters using transfer maps and machine learning in a digital model of a MeV $γγ$ collider
abstract: Tuning the electron beam of a MeV-scale $γγ$ collider, first in the design and later in a digital twin of the machine, requires the beam parameters at the interaction point (IP) for many injector states. Start-to-end particle tracking is too slow for this and needs the full particle distribution, which an operating machine cannot measure. We address this problem for the 200-MeV transport line of the collider with two fast predictors. For design, second-order transfer maps from the transport entrance to the IP are applied to every particle. For a digital twin, an extremely-randomized-trees (ExtraTrees) model predicts the IP parameters from the means and rms widths of the beam at the transport entrance. On 89 held-out start-to-end simulations, the map predictor reproduces Elegant tracking for the mean energy, momentum spread, bunch length, transverse rms sizes and normalized emittances with coefficients of determination ($R^2$) of 0.97--1.00 and is ten times faster. The ExtraTrees model reaches an average $R^2$ of 0.88, compared with 0.58 when the injector settings are used as input, and performs similarly with eleven inputs that can be measured or reconstructed. Under a 2% input perturbation, the average $R^2$ of the six parameters other than the mean energy decreases only from 0.917 to 0.895, whereas the mean energy requires an accurate momentum calibration. The two predictors provide the IP-beam evaluation for the collider design and the prediction layer of a future digital twin.

title: Microscopic Origin and Josephson Signatures of $d$-Wave Superconductivity in Monolayer FeSe
abstract: Monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$ exhibits high-temperature superconductivity with an electron-only Fermi surface, raising fundamental questions about its unconventional pairing mechanism. Motivated by recent Josephson scanning tunneling microscopy evidence for nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity, we investigate the microscopic role of the Fe $d_{xy}$ orbital using an experimentally constrained multiorbital theory. A tight-binding model fitted to quasiparticle interference and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals substantial $d_{xy}$ character near the Fermi level and dominant nearest-neighbor hopping, in contrast to the conventional kinetic-frustration picture of iron-based superconductors. Both itinerant spin-fluctuation calculations and strong-coupling exchange approaches favor a robust $d$-wave pairing state, whose interband pairing components allow a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum. We further establish a symmetry-based selection rule for spatial Josephson tunneling, revealing characteristic bond-centered maxima and mirror-enforced interference zeros that distinguish $d$-wave pairing from competing $s$-wave states. These symmetry-enforced nodal lines survive near Fe-site impurities, while a pronounced contrast between the $d$- and $s$-wave Josephson patterns persists around vortices despite the loss of mirror protection. Our results connect the unconventional $d_{xy}$ electronic structure to nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity and demonstrate the power of spatial Josephson interference for resolving pairing symmetry in multiorbital superconductors.

title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
abstract: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $Φ^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.

title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
abstract: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. We present HITCH (Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids), a harness in which perception returns the 3D position of any point the VLM selects in its image, and execution turns commands for the pelvis, torso, hands, walking, and gaze into whole-body motion with a learned tracker. We find that both measuring the scene and executing commands accurately raise task success. We then fine-tune a VLM on trajectories in which teacher policies solve five base tasks through HITCH, so that it learns how to operate the humanoid. Without task-specific trajectories, the fine-tuned model completes 51% of SIMPLE episodes and 42.5% of HumanoidArena episodes, and adding five trajectories per SIMPLE task raises its SIMPLE success to 95%. On a real G1, it carries a box and walks to a goal without real training data.

title: Effective Thermodynamics of a Volume-Dependent Qubit
abstract: We develop an effective thermodynamics for a qubit whose energy gap depends inversely on a volume-like control parameter, $Δ(V)=Δ_0/V$, where $V$ is a spectral-control coordinate rather than a literal mechanical volume. Starting from the canonical Gibbs state, we derive a complete thermodynamic structure from the Helmholtz potential and its Legendre and stability properties, including the fundamental relation $S(U,V)$, a generalized pressure conjugate to $V$, the equation of state $U=PV$, the first law, and the associated Maxwell relations. Reversible adiabats preserve the Gibbs populations and satisfy $TV=\mathrm{const.}$ and $PV^2=\mathrm{const.}$, corresponding to an effective exponent $γ=2$. The resulting effective Carnot cycle attains the Carnot efficiency, $η_{\mathrm{Carnot}}=1-T_C/T_H$, whereas the Otto cycle yields $η_{\mathrm{Otto}}=1-V_{\min}/V_{\max}$ and remains strictly sub-Carnot at finite work output. We identify the source of Otto irreversibility exactly: entropy is produced entirely during the isochoric thermalizations, and the cycle entropy production quantifies the informational mismatch between the adiabatically transported states and the reservoir-selected Gibbs states through the sum of the corresponding quantum relative entropies. Finally, we show that unitary-generated nonpassivity can act as a nonequilibrium battery, producing an apparent efficiency above Carnot when its preparation cost is omitted. At the same time, complete work accounting restores the thermodynamic bound.

title: Results from a Stellar Occultation by (623) Chimaera
abstract: We present results from a stellar occultation by the asteroid (623) Chimaera on October 21st, 2025, when it passed in front of V magnitude 13.86 star UCAC4 626-004193. Chimaera is the largest asteroid in the Chimaerid asteroid family and will be subject to a spacecraft flyby in the 2030s. Eighteen telescopes were deployed, spanning the United States from Arizona to North Carolina, incrementally spaced by $\sim4.4$\,km with respect to the cross-track of the shadow. In total, sixteen telescopes collected useful data. This multi-chord observation, when compiled into a single sky-plane plot, suggests a profile which is well-described by an elongated elliptical fit, with a semi-major axis $a=26.2\pm0.8$ km and a semi-minor axis $b=16.0\pm1.0$ km. The projected area from ellipse fitting is 1316 km$^2$, and a limb fit is calculated to enclose 1312 km$^2$. Photometry collected in the Gaia G band over a seven-month period coinciding with the occultation corresponds to a geometric albedo $p_G=0.059\pm0.005$; comparing with archival occultation observations and direct observations gives $p_G=0.051\pm0.004$ and $p_V=0.051\pm0.004$. We compare occultation sky-plane projections with 3-D modeling from inversion techniques and demonstrate that the models can accurately predict the orientation of Chimaera at the time of each occultation.

title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties
abstract: Model raising revisits Turing's developmental view of machine intelligence. Formal Raising (FR) has recently been proposed to complement this view with explicit behavioral properties. This paper extends that proposal to the security of the raising environment. Secure Formal Raising (SFR) models policy integrity, authorization, and confidential data flow using four-valued evidence that preserves unknown and inconsistent assessments. We prove six security invariants and show that they force admission to accept only confirmed evidence. A plain-C reference implementation satisfies the invariants in a bounded exhaustive exploration, which also exposes a confused-deputy gap for tool calls that a provenance requirement closes.

title: Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium
abstract: This memorial tribute to Mannque Rho focuses on the role of scale symmetry in baryonic matter, especially on its profound influence on the possible resolution of the ``quenched $g_A$" problem in the Gamow-Teller transition of nuclei, the pseudoconformal structure of dense nuclear matter and the origin of the peak of sound velocity of nuclear matter. The discussion is based on the genuine dilaton scenario, anchored on the Crewther-Tunstall infrared fixed point, which provides a unified framework where scale symmetry---broken explicitly by the QCD trace anomaly---can be spontaneously broken, yielding the scalar $f_0(500)$ as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson. In nuclear medium, this scenario serves as a natural foundation of the Brown-Rho scaling---a relation that has been central to nuclear physics for over three decades. The sound velocity of nuclear matter exhibits a characteristic peak at intermediate densities arising from the kink behavior of the dilaton field, a unique signature of scale symmetry realization that distinguishes the dilaton-compensated effective theory from conventional Walecka-type models. At higher densities, the approach to the dilaton-limit fixed point produces pseudo-conformal behavior with sound velocity $v_s^2 = 1/3$ saturating from below at $n \gtrsim 3n_0$, while the trace of the energy-momentum tensor remains nonzero. The framework also provides a natural resolution of the long-standing ``quenched $g_A$" problem, demonstrating that nuclear correlations, not fundamental quenching, account for the effective axial coupling approaching unity. The continuity from the unitary limit at low density to the dilaton limit at high density suggests a pervasive role for scale symmetry in nuclear dynamics across all density regimes.

title: Few-Weight Linear Sets and Divisibility of Rank-Metric Codes
abstract: We study $\mathbb F_q$-linear sets whose positive point weights belong to a prescribed finite set $A$. The integer $e=\gcd(A)$ always divides the rank of the defining subspace, but the divisibility does not by itself imply linearity over $\mathbb F_{q^e}$. We show that it does in a broad parameter range. Let $L_U$ be an $\mathbb F_q$-linear set of rank $N$ spanning $PG(h-1,q^m)$, $h\ge2$, without being equal to it, and assume that $q\ge m$ and that the minimum weight of its points is $a\ge2$. Combining the theorem of Csajbók, Marino and Pepe on the maximum field of linearity with the lower bound of Adriaensen and Santonastaso for the size of a linear set containing a point of weight one, we prove that $L_U$ is also defined by an $\mathbb F_{q^t}$-subspace, for some divisor $t$ of $m$, whose $\mathbb F_q$-dimension is exactly $N+t-a$. Under a natural gap condition excluding divisors of $m$ in the interval $(e,N-e]$, this forces $a=e$ and the defining subspace to be $\mathbb F_{q^e}$-linear. Through geometric duality, the point weights of the dual of a system are the deficiencies $m-w$ of the rank weights $w$ of the associated code. For rank-metric codes in which the subcode generated by the codewords of nonmaximum rank contains codewords of maximum rank, we show that deleting suitable coordinates yields the $\mathbb F_q$-expansion of a code over $\mathbb F_{q^t}$. We show that the codes in which the codewords of nonmaximum rank generate a subcode without codewords of maximum rank are exactly the direct sums of a simplex code and a code of length smaller than $m$. We derive field-reduction results for two-weight and three-weight rank-metric codes, and show that no gap condition is needed when $m$ divides the length or when the code has only two nonzero weights. Finally, we study two-dimensional codes of length at most $m$ and provide families of three-weight examples.

title: Types of Bursting with a Two-Block Spiking Primitive
abstract: Excitable spikers are attractive systems for sparse, event-driven computation. A spiking primitive composed of a linear frequency selector closed in positive feedback around a high-gain saturating nonlinearity has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable system. This paper asks which bursting classes that primitive can produce with two elementary selectors: a first-order high-pass filter, and a second-order resonant band-pass filter. The nonlinearity decides whether the system fires, and where the rheobase sits. The selector decides whether rest and repetitive firing can coexist, and therefore which bursting class is available. We show that the high-pass never makes rest and firing coexist, whatever the nonlinearity, and that no linear slow feedback branch can then produce bursting. With a piecewise linear nonlinearity, it gives type I excitability, and a second copy of the primitive gives parabolic bursting. The resonant band-pass gives a Hopf, type II excitability, and a subcritical onset above a computable gain, hence a window where rest and firing coexist. A single additional slow linear feedback then gives elliptic bursting. We also show that the resting point is unique for both selectors, which makes square-wave bursting structurally unavailable. Closed-form thresholds, firing rates, and criticality conditions are given and validated numerically.

title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels
abstract: Nowadays, large language models produce text at scale, and much of it is redistributed across platforms. A moderator who finds a suspicious comment, post or article may want to know which platform generated it and for which account. In this paper we study attribution over the channel through which such text actually travels, copy-paste, which discards document metadata but keeps Unicode code points. We present KeHoSu, which turns the confusable characters of homoglyph attacks into a keyed attribution channel: the variant chosen for each carrier letter encodes one bit of an identifier made of a platform field, a user field and a truncated authentication tag. Moreover, given that reshared text is often quoted in fragments, and the placement therefore keeps no positional state, we show that KeHoSu is invariant to sentence reordering up to a constant boundary layer and depends on a partial quotation only through the retained length. We characterize the code-point channel by its capacity, removability and detectability, and provide an achievable region that relates the three. We evaluate KeHoSu over a wide range of use cases and show that the mark survived copy-paste across 18 common platforms, attributing the majority of all excerpts to the correct account at 178 letters (about two sentences) on LLM-generated stories and 167 letters (about one sentence) on standard English prose.

title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
abstract: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.

title: Performance metrics in machine learning: a scenario-based guide from the confusion matrix to calibration, regression and uncertainty
abstract: Performance metrics can yield different conclusions from the same predictions. This methodological tutorial explains the effects of class prevalence, decision thresholds, aggregation rules and software conventions through controlled scenarios. Twenty-two confusion-matrix metrics are organized in a prevalence-coded map. Fifteen scenarios cover binary and multi-class classification, score discrimination, probability calibration, regression, uncertainty and consistency checks. Inputs are fixed in released files, and one factor is varied in each scenario. All 205 verification checks passed; 202 were independent and 3 were internal. An always-negative rule achieved an accuracy of 0.990 at a prevalence of 0.010, with balanced accuracy of 0.500. At fixed sensitivity and specificity, precision fell from 0.889 to 0.008 as prevalence fell from 0.5 to 0.001. Three probability variants shared a ROC-AUC of 0.825 but had calibration slopes of 2.08, 1.04 and 0.52. With 10 participants, participant-majority accuracy of 0.700 had a 95% interval of 0.348-0.933. Fold-averaged scores were falsely flagged as inconsistent under an inappropriate pooled-test-set model. A goal-based metric table and a reporting checklist are provided. The scenarios illustrate mechanisms and do not estimate their frequency in published studies. A literature audit and a real-data demonstration are specified as future protocols and were not executed.

title: When Molecular Dimerization Induces Magnetic Bi-Stability at the Metal-Organic Interface
abstract: We present a method to create metal-organic dimer complexes by on-surface assembly on a metal substrate using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS). We demonstrate that a dimer of Mn-Phthalocyanine (MnPc)2 on a Ag(111) surface can be switched between two stable configurations upon a small conformational change controlled by STM manipulation. By means of density-functional theory calculations, it is found that the two conformations correspond to an antiferromagnetic (AFM) and a ferromagnetic (FM) state respectively. Directly coordinated Mn atoms of the dimer lead to an AFM-coupling whereas indirectly coordinated (shifted) Mn atoms lead to a FM-coupling. Rarely seen in a molecular- dimers with transition-metal atoms, the FM-AFM-FM transition is thus readily on-surface accessible. Furthermore, the two configurations of the switch are easily identified by their Kondo states, opening interesting routes in terms of both, writing (FM versus AFM states) and reading. These results pave the experimental route toward dimer-based materials with complex magnetic structures of potential interest for application in spintronics, logics and computing.

title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
abstract: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180° rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.

title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
abstract: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.

title: The Moving Frontier: How the National Justice Project Is Using Digital Technology to Expand Access to Justice
abstract: Over the past three decades, technological advances have assisted individuals to gain access to legal information, enhance the efficiency of legal services, and streamline dispute resolution. More recently, the proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has reinforced this emphasis on firm-level productivity, with commercial legal practice increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence tools to automate document creation and optimise case management. While commercial technology focuses on productivity, community organisations are exploring how artificial intelligence can level the playing field for marginalised communities. Far less attention has been given to free, direct-to-consumer legal technologies, as these models are often unprofitable. Consequently, justice technology scholarship has overlooked a distinct class of technology: digital reporting platforms that enable people to record their experiences of harm, while simultaneously aggregating those accounts into a body of evidence capable of supporting advocacy, institutional accountability, and law reform. Crucially, experiences of discrimination and administrative abuse are often dismissed by oversight bodies as individual grievances. To understand the transformative potential of these platforms, this article asks two questions. First, how can digital reporting close the knowledge and power gap for marginalised communities interacting with the legal system? Second, how can these tools collect evidence to hold institutions accountable, drive change and contribute to a more just society?

title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
abstract: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation. Agents observe an article's reliability and their predecessors' actions, which indicate whether they liked or disliked the article. They may also pay to fact-check it. We examine how welfare, defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when a free, error-prone automated tool supplements costly but perfectly accurate manual fact-checking. Two opposing effects arise. Broader use of fact-checking helps agents escape wrong cascades. At the same time, errors from the automated tool can mislead agents who would otherwise have verified the article perfectly, reducing the likelihood of correct cascades. We prove that adding the tool strictly lowers welfare for articles of intermediate reliability when truthful articles are not too informative and manual checking is sufficiently costly. Simulations show that the tool can help on either side of the intermediate range, and that it improves on manual-only checking on average only above a threshold accuracy.

title: NutriVisRAG: Multimodal Exemplar Grounding for Nutrient Estimation with Vision-Language Models
abstract: Diet is a major determinant of health, yet accurate dietary assessment from free-living meal images remains challenging. Existing retrieval-based Vision-Language Model (VLM) approaches to nutrient estimation typically rely on textual food representations, while, to our knowledge, direct grounding on visually similar annotated meals has not been investigated.
