As a nontrivial consistency check, we show that the two Seiberg--Witten curves agree with each other when expressed in the Weierstrass normal form.

title: Scaling Graph Similarity Learning with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph similarity computation is an important task in graph mining with many real-world applications, such as chemical compound analysis, program dependence comparison, and social network analysis. The problem is computationally challenging: Graph Edit Distance (GED) and Maximum Common Subgraph (MCS), which quantify the distance between graphs and identify their largest shared subgraph, respectively, are NP-hard to compute exactly. To address these computational challenges, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been applied to this problem. However, existing GNN-based approaches have primarily focused on small-scale graph datasets, while scalability to larger scales remains underexplored. In this work, we propose FiLSim, a scalable GNN-based framework, and investigate whether a simplified GNN pipeline can maintain competitive performance on standard benchmarks while scaling to large graphs. We additionally propose a sequential graph-editing strategy to construct large-scale graph datasets with reliable GED labels to evaluate scalability. The proposed framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets and four newly created large-scale datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and scalability. FiLSim remains accurate on graphs with more than 150{,}000 nodes, where the baseline methods run out of memory or fail to learn, and scores all test pairs within seconds on a single GPU.

title: An Efficient Synchronization Scheme for Distributed Bandits
abstract: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. Finally, applying these results to distributed multi-armed bandits, we show an upper bound on the regret of our synchronization scheme.

title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: A conversational agent that remembers has to decide what to keep. Retrieval-augmented generation keeps the transcript and searches it; the alternative is to compact each turn into atomic facts and search those. We compare the two on LoCoMo, with both arms answering all 1,985 questions in one window, against the same stores, with the same generator and judge, and both predictions on one row, which licenses McNemar's exact test on the 512 questions where they disagree. On the four categories comparable work reports, compaction scores 71.4 per cent against 64.6, a lead of 6.8 points (p = 5.5e-08) at 34 per cent fewer prompt tokens. On all five, including the adversarial set comparable work drops, the lead falls to 2.0 and stops being significant, because the baseline leads adversarial by 14.6. That loss has a structure. Our lead falls as the reference answer demands more source wording, 9.6 points ahead at one or two reference words and 3.1 behind past eight, with token overlap moving the same way, so the judge is not the cause. Compaction keeps what a fact asserts and discards how it was said, so it wins where the answer is a value and loses where it is a phrasing. We also report four negative results with their power calculations.

title: Agents on the Patch Path: Mining AI-Associated Security Remediation in GitHub Security Advisories
abstract: Autonomous coding agents are increasingly involved in software development, but their participation in real-world security remediation remains poorly understood. We investigate observable evidence of coding-agent involvement in commits referenced by reviewed GitHub Security Advisories (GHSAs), characterize the associated vulnerabilities, and examine review timing in relation to advisory disclosure routes. We develop a local-Git mining pipeline that identifies agent evidence through known agent accounts, explicit commit-message attribution, repository instruction files, and agent configuration artifacts. Linking these findings to GHSA-referenced commits yields 469 valid candidate advisories across 189 repositories, including 448 with direct attribution and 21 supported only by repository-level evidence. Claude is the most frequently observed tool family, followed by Copilot and Cursor. We further compare review timing against other advisories and historical baselines using an exact route--timing decomposition. Relative to advisories published in the same months, candidate advisories exhibit a modestly longer mean review lag, primarily associated with within-route timing rather than disclosure-route composition. Compared with a historical baseline, they exhibit substantially shorter mean review lags, with both route composition and within-route timing contributing to the difference. These findings demonstrate that coding-agent involvement is already observable across hundreds of security advisories and repositories, including high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities. By distinguishing direct attribution from repository-level adoption evidence and separating route-composition effects from within-route timing differences, we provide an empirical characterization of agent-associated remediation in the GHSA review pipeline.

title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
abstract: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+Ω(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

title: Reversible Interchain Associations Dominate Plateau Elasticity in Conjugated Polymers
abstract: The modulus plateau is widely regarded as a hallmark of topological entanglement in homopolymer melts and has been used to identify entanglement in semiflexible conjugated polymers. Using regiorandom poly(3-alkylthiophenes) as a model system, we show that their plateau elasticity relaxes through an Arrhenius process decoupled from segmental and terminal dynamics, reorganizes persistently under mechanical perturbation, and varies systematically with side-chain length. These behaviors are hard to reconcile with a purely topological-entanglement picture and instead support a transient network dominated by reversible interchain associations, consistent with π-π interactions between conjugated backbone segments. The results thus demonstrate that plateau elasticity alone does not uniquely identify topological entanglement in conjugated polymers. More broadly, they identify the strength and lifetime of interchain association as molecular design parameters linking backbone packing to stress relaxation, viscoelastic properties, and processability in conjugated polymers, complementing their established role in electronic structure and charge transport.

title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
abstract: In this paper, we provide a new set of tools for establishing the number rigidity of point processes which are particularly well suited for the spectral processes of stochastic operators. These tools allow one to prove the number rigidity of a wide class of stochastic operators that had been previously inaccessible to the standard methods in the area, such as the variance of linear statistics, which require being able to precisely analyze correlations between individual points. We propose an alternative mechanism which uses a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of the unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise which allows one to convert the probabilistic problem into a more tractable perturbation theory problem. This new approach allows us to prove the rigidity of previously inaccessible operators including those with heavy tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. As a demonstration, we use these tools to prove the number rigidity of new classes of stochastic Schrödinger and Sturm-Liouville Operators which are resistant to analysis using the standard rigidity toolkit.

title: The Double Copy of the Doubly Spinning Black Ring
abstract: We establish an exact curved-background Weyl double copy for the doubly spinning Pomeransky--Sen'kov black ring. Its full Weyl tensor is a quadratic form in two source-free Maxwell fields: one generated by the stationary Killing vector, the other a flux-carrying magnetic field obtained by linearizing the dipole-ring gauge potential about its vacuum limit. The mixed Maxwell bilinear is essential: no spacetime-independent real or complex change of field basis removes it. We identify the inverse $S_{IJ}$ of the Weyl coefficient matrix as a matrix zeroth copy. The same matrix arises independently from a weighted limit of the inner products of two Killing vectors in a six-dimensional Ricci-flat parent and satisfies $\Box_g S_{IJ}=-\tfrac12 F_{I\,ab}F_J{}^{ab}$. The singly spinning limit recovers the diagonal two-field Weyl double copy of the Emparan--Reall ring.

title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
abstract: We develop a conforming virtual element framework for differential forms on general polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. Recursive local Hodge-Laplace boundary value problems define a trimmed virtual de Rham complex, from which moment constraints yield a complete subcomplex. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial spaces of differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom and computable polynomial projections. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and both complexes have cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual families, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and mesh-uniform norm equivalences in all form degrees. We further derive canonical interpolation error bounds and discrete Poincar'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge-Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity. Moreover, the two conforming complexes are cochain isomorphic to their fully discrete counterparts (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2025, doi:10.4171/JEMS/1602), and the norm equivalences provide a key analytical bridge between the conforming and fully discrete formulations.

title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
abstract: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
abstract: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. Calibrating by forecast wind regime turns marginal coverage into regime-level coverage, cutting day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40% relative to pooled calibration while narrowing bands overall.

title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
abstract: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records. Many questions must be answered in a query-specified perspective rather than the observed camera viewpoint, and prompting with a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded visual cues. To address these gaps, we introduce BEV3SR, a training-free and backbone-agnostic framework for RGB-D videos with camera parameters. BEV3SR turns video observations into queryable metric bird's-eye-view (BEV) scene memory and formalizes each query into an evidence-aware spatial task. The Spatial Task Formalizer specifies the query's reference frame, spatial constraints, objective, and evidence requirement. The evidence requirement determines the appropriate reasoning pathway. A query treated as requiring geometric evidence is handled by the Geometric Reasoner, which deterministically computes the answer using the metric BEV records in the query-specified reference frame. Otherwise, a query treated as requiring visual evidence is passed to the Visual Evidence Aligner, which uses BEV-indexed object records and their associated supporting views to retrieve object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding. Within a standard 16-frame budget, BEV3SR consistently improves different VLM backbones across multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, delivering large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA. These results demonstrate that BEV3SR offers an effective, efficient, and interpretable framework for explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the study of lattice gauge theory. This chapter is a contribution to the online book ``Lattice QCD at 50 years,'' (LQCD@50), edited by Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Maarten Golterman, Rajan Gupta, Laurent Lellouch, and Steve Sharpe.

title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
abstract: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein representations and as a prior for editing them. Generation quality scales smoothly with depth and compute. As a lens, single GLP "meta-neurons" are the strongest probes of discrete Swiss-Prot concepts at both hosts, beating InterPLM's released SAE features, and lead on continuous properties at 8M though not at 650M; falsification tests show this is mostly concentration, not new information. As an editing prior, the on-manifold correction makes DiffMean steering of three biochemical properties effective and restores on-manifoldness, but only in isolation: re-embedding the sequences actually produced after several rounds of decoding, the structural plausibility is compromised. This is mainly reproduced in additional SAE-based clamping structural steering experiments, where only Helix motif succeeds. The naturalness failure is traced to the rewriting coverage and the decoder rather than the prior, highlighting what the method must clear before it can serve for both discovery-by-editing and discovery-by-exploration. Trained GLPs are released on huggingface.co/collections/HPAI-BSC/glprot.

title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. Applying this model to $1s$ acoustic polarons in an MoSe$_2$ monolayer, we reveal a distinct kink in the polaron dispersion, accompanied by a pronounced broadening of its spectral function. These spectral signatures mark a critical transition from a regime of well-defined bound exciton polarons, characterized by a renormalized energy, reduced group velocity, and enhanced effective mass, to a regime dominated by exciton-phonon scattering. Furthermore, by incorporating intervalley exciton-phonon interaction, we demonstrate that the energetic position of momentum-dark excitons strongly modifies the exciton-polaron lifetime. Overall, our work provides a microscopic framework for determining renormalized properties of exciton polarons and establishes experimentally accessible polaron signatures in 2D semiconductors.

title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
abstract: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.

title: Mellin Transform formulas for special values of Goss $L$-functions
abstract: In the present paper, we provide formulas for the special values of dual Goss $L$-functions of Drinfeld modules at any non-negative integer in terms of the determinant of the values of a motivic map, extensively studied by both authors in 2026, for a large class of Anderson modules. Our result may be seen as a function field analogue of conjectural formulas for special values of motivic $L$-functions in terms of algebraic Mellin integrals.

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which Gemini 4 agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 2.55x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

title: Regular multi-types and the Bloom conjecture II
abstract: Let $M\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ $(n\geq2)$ be a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface. We prove that, for every $1\leq s\leq n-1$, the regular $s$-contact type, the $s$-commutator type, and the $s$-Levi type coincide at every point of $M$, thereby resolving Bloom's conjecture in any dimension. The solution in dimension three was obtained in 2021 by the second and the third authors. Moreover, for any smooth rank $s$ subbundle $B\subset T^{1,0}M$, we establish the equality of the commutator type and the Levi type associated with $B$, giving an affirmative answer to the generalized D'Angelo conjecture.

title: Neutral Ricci spectra of homogeneous Riemannian four-manifolds
abstract: It is shown that every quadruple of real numbers with two positive and two negative entries is the Ricci spectrum of some left-invariant Riemannian metric on a Lie group of dimension four. Consequently, for eight out of the fifteen possible Ricci signatures of four-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, one can determine precisely which spectra in each given signature actually occur. We also describe the Ricci spectra realized by left-invariant metrics on a certain class of 2-step solvable Lie groups of all dimensions $n>2$.

title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
abstract: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at https://github.com/OpenBitSys/BitDecoding-FP4.

title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
abstract: We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -Δ_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_ϕY,\qquad g_ϕ=dr^2\oplusϕ(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions. We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $ϕ(r)=e^{ar}$ and $ϕ(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=ϕ^{-σ}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $σk>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $σk>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.

title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
abstract: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. Beyond the initial X-ray burst, electrons released by radioactive fission products can become trapped in Earth's magnetic field, repeatedly exposing satellites as an artificial radiation belt. Here we couple prompt radiation, electron trapping and belt evolution to satellite failures, collisions and atmospheric drag. For a 1-Mt detonation at 500km over the South Atlantic, repeated belt exposure disables approximately 98% of modeled satellites within one week in our central case. Tripling the assumed radiation tolerance delays widespread failure by only days: approximately 97% are still disabled within two weeks. The loss of maneuverability sharply increases collision risk, with approximately 20 collisions expected within two years. Drag removes many disabled spacecraft from lower altitudes, but replacement satellites could remain exposed to radiation and debris for years. These findings show how a single detonation could devastate orbital infrastructure and support efforts to prevent the deployment and use of nuclear weapons in space.

title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. To study how best to use monitors to mitigate reward hacking, we introduce and open source three realistic environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks: a coding environment hackable via test overwriting, a medical chat environment hackable via sycophancy, and a biography generation environment hackable via hallucination. We first focus on the coding environment, where we find that: (1) models can learn to evade highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic flaws in probes and LLM judges; (2) monitors that leak more learning signal during RL suppress reward hacking but are more often evaded; and (3) including easier problems in training can decrease reward hacking. We apply our findings to build better reward hacking monitors for the medical chat and biography generation environments that improve upon naive baselines to reduce reward hacking rates across seeds to before-training levels in some interventions. Our results demonstrate that our takeaways translate to new settings and that better monitor intervention designs are possible.

title: Odd Loops: What Structures Can Produce a Parity-Violating Inflationary Trispectrum?
abstract: Non-Gaussian perturbations generated during inflation can often be described perturbatively via integrals of kernels acting on Gaussian fields. In this work, we investigate, in a model-independent manner, whether these kernels can produce parity-violating (PV) contributions to the trispectrum, and which Wick's theorem contraction configurations of the Gaussian fields lead to them. In detail, we evaluate all possible contraction configurations arising from the third- and second-order density perturbations. We find that, for the third-order perturbations, only one configuration can support PV contributions, as it retains three independent wave-vectors. In contrast, none of the four second-order perturbation contraction configurations can produce a PV contribution under statistical isotropy. These results offer a first step toward deriving kernels from inflationary models capable of generating a PV trispectrum. Such kernels could then be used to perform PV searches with current and upcoming galaxy redshift surveys such as DESI, Roman, SPHEREx, and Euclid, and photometric efforts such as LSST. Our results also offer a guide for exploration of PV with CMB data-sets such as Planck.

title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
abstract: Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of deterministic quantum search to NP problems while retaining the quadratic query advantage over classical exhaustive search.

title: Quantifying the importance of equation of state and transport property compatibility in supercritical fluids
abstract: High-fidelity simulation of supercritical flows requires accurate values of thermodynamic properties including the density (rho), specific heat cp, enthalpy h, and entropy s as well as transport properties such as the viscosity (eta) and thermal conductivity (lambda) as functions of the temperature T and pressure P. In simulations of mixtures, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) with contaminants, a generalized equation of state (EoS) is often used, leading to errors in rho(T,P) when compared to results from correlations developed specifically for individual species. Similarly, generalized correlations for eta and lambda are often used, with a corresponding decrease in accuracy. However, a second source of error is introduced in calculations of transport properties. These correlations are created and computed as functions of T and rho instead of as functions of T and P. Because of this, when eta(T,rho )and lambda(T,rho) are calculated, errors in rho(T,P) propagate through the calculation. This work creates a procedure for tracking both errors caused by using a generalized correlation for eta(T,rho) and lambda(T,rho), and for tracking the errors caused by using a generalized correlation for rho(T,P) in these calculations. The viscosity and thermal conductivity of supercritical CO2, N2, andCH4 are used as examples to demonstrate how to separate the errors due to the generalized property correlations and the errors due to the generalized EoS. Both sources of error are largest near the critical temperature Tc. These errors are large enough to impact both the numeric stability and the accuracy of simulations.

title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
abstract: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.

title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
abstract: Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions. We implement this formalism using the open-source Dedalus spectral framework. This accommodates heterogeneous edge lengths, material properties and spectral resolutions. Initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems share a parallel solution method that eliminates internal unknowns independently on subgraphs and couples their solutions through shared boundary vertex interfaces. We verify numerical convergence and demonstrate strong and weak scaling on networks with millions of edges. We present applications to localized optical resonances in photonic networks, preferential channel formation during mineral replacement in evolving pore networks, and nonlinear dispersive waves for KdV on a periodic network.

title: The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs
abstract: Investors turn signals into holdings through decision rules: buy the top decile, hold stocks with high momentum and low volatility, exclude stocks that fail a screen. Many such rules are Boolean functions of threshold statements about signal ranks, and writing them this way shows both what a rule holds and how often it trades. A Walsh decomposition splits the return of any rule into exposures to individual signals and to interactions among signals; an intersection and a union of the same two screens, for example, have opposite interaction exposures. The same coefficients, together with the persistence of the underlying statements, determine turnover. Interactions are less persistent than their components, so rules that load on higher-order interactions trade more, and thresholds discard information, so at equal risk threshold implementations of interactions trade more than smooth ones. In U.S. stocks from 1973 to 2024, these predictions hold closely: predicted and realized persistence have correlations of at least 0.999, predicted turnover matches realized turnover with a slope of 1.02, and the same interactions are more persistent as products of ranks than as threshold rules. Trading costs rise with order, and because premia fall with order, 58% of single-signal portfolios have absolute premia above their quoted-spread costs over 1995-2024, against 24% of two-signal and 6% of three-signal interaction portfolios. Out of sample, interaction portfolios raise the Sharpe ratio of single-signal tangency portfolios, and over 1995-2024 they reject a six-factor model that conventional sorts on the same signals do not reject.

title: Ensemble Individual Mode Frequency Modeling of Kepler Giants - Extending the IACgrid towards the red-giant branch
abstract: Precise stellar parameters, in particular ages, are vital for understanding the formation and history of the Milky Way. Usually, this is achieved by fitting stellar evolution models to observational constraints such as spectroscopic and astrometric parameters. Adding global asteroseismic properties to the classical parameters (global seismic modeling) breaks some degeneracies and improves the results. However, this approach has its limitations, with red-giant random age uncertainties usually $\sim$ 20-50%, and often lacking proper quantification of the systematics. We aim to extend seismic modeling to include individual mode frequencies for red-giant branch stars, increasing the number of evolved solar-like oscillators with precise stellar parameters (ages, masses, and radii), and allowing us to quantify the systematics in global seismic modeling. We developed a grid of stellar evolutionary models and computed the individual oscillation frequencies, including a figure of merit to find the best-fitting model. We validate our methodology on a sample of red giants with individual frequency modeling from the literature, finding our masses, radii, and ages in close agreement. We then apply our method to around 100 Kepler red-giant branch stars of near-solar mass and metallicity, which previously have only been modeled with global seismic parameters. We obtain random average uncertainties of 3.4%, 1.3%, and 13.2%, for stellar masses, radii, and ages, respectively. We find that ages from individual mode frequency modeling are significantly, 14% on average, larger than those from global seismic mass-constrained modeling. The modeled luminosities agree within 1.0% with those derived from Gaia parallaxes. We conclude that modeling individual mode frequencies improves age precision by a factor of two for red-giant branch stars, providing stronger constraints for galactic archaeology.

title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
abstract: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. We describe a radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular tools to produce a structured report, and use it to measure what such a system can do with the tools from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices. Report generation is simulated on a large multi-modality report corpus, with the orchestrator given either a catalog of finding classes consolidated from the cleared devices, each available on the modalities it is cleared for, or an unlimited catalog in which any class can be requested, and planning either from the clinical indication or from the target report. Tool outputs are simulated from the reference report, so the comparison isolates tool availability and orchestration from tool error. With the cleared catalog and the indication alone, the orchestrator recovers under a third of the clinically actionable findings; recovery improves substantially with the unlimited catalog, and further when the plan is written from the target report. Attributing every missed finding to a cause shows that most are classes no cleared device offers for the study's modality, and that a third are classes or tools that were offered and not called. Adding the most frequently missing tools closes most of the gap to the unlimited catalog on held-out reports, whereas a smaller orchestrator with the unlimited catalog gives up the whole gain. Tool availability and effective orchestration are thus complementary constraints on comprehensive AI-assisted radiology reporting.

title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
abstract: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}ψ\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap. Additionally, the state accurately reproduces both the exponent and coefficient of the asymptotic radial probability density predicted by the three-graviton amplitude.

title: Instantaneous control for stabilization of interacting particle systems: convergence rates and dominant frequencies
abstract: We study a class of Cucker-Smale-type systems with a binary interaction potential subject to an external control input. We apply an instantaneous rolling horizon control (IRHC) feedback to address two different control problems: full set-point stabilization of a spatial configuration with zero velocity and stabilization of the center of mass at a desired position with zero mean velocity using a single external agent. The IRHC feedback has been shown to preserve the port-Hamiltonian structure of the corresponding open-loop systems. We analyze how the control parameters and the time discretization affect convergence rates and oscillation frequencies and compare the IRHC feedback with the corresponding IDA-PBC feedback obtained by omitting an additional correction term. For the reduced center of mass dynamics, we derive explicit predictions for continuous- and discrete-time spectral decay rates and oscillation frequencies and verify these predictions numerically. For the full nonlinear particle system, the controller comparison is done by numerical experiments.

title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Rényi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

title: GroundWork: Bridging Human and LLM Reasoning Through a Structured Argumentation Model
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into workflows that require reasoning over text documents, yet interaction remains largely conversational. This leaves argumentative structure implicit or embedded in text, making it difficult to maintain, compare, and revise arguments as analyses evolve. We present GroundWork, a mixed-initiative system that makes argument structure a shared, editable state for humans and LLMs. GroundWork operationalizes the Toulmin model of argumentation as a typed graph with explicit operations for human and LLM edits. It exposes this structure through coordinated corpus views and an editable workbench for constructing, comparing, testing, and tracing source-grounded arguments. We evaluate GroundWork through an expert study with four participants spanning consulting, product development, law, and immunology, and three use-case scenarios in intelligence, law, and medicine. Our findings show that GroundWork makes source-grounded arguments inspectable, comparable, and revisable as shared human-LLM state.

title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
abstract: Data deduplication has become increasingly important in large-scale storage systems, driven by the rapid growth of digital data. By identifying and removing repeats in the data stream, deduplication saves storage space more efficiently than traditional compression methods. In this paper, we study the performance of variable-length deduplication and multi-chunk deduplication algorithms from an information-theoretic perspective, focusing on data streams where repeats are approximate rather than exact. We consider two probabilistic source models in which source strings consist of repeated blocks that are modified by either a constant number of substitution edits or burst-insertion edits per block, the latter capturing the localized edit patterns commonly observed in real-world data. For both models, we show that variable-length deduplication achieves asymptotically arbitrarily large compression ratios, and that multi-chunk deduplication achieves compression within a constant factor of the source entropy under mild conditions.

title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
abstract: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". The dataset PigAirwayPressure is not an outlier. Although the archive is the standard benchmark, whether its tasks resemble the problems TSC is meant to solve has rarely been examined. We find that several datasets are repurposed from their original task, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits. We further question how representative the archive's ordered non-temporal sequences (e.g. spectra, shape outlines) are of real TSC, and the potential downsides from the decomposition of multivariate problems. Our findings call for more careful interpretation of archive-wide scores and greater attention to deployment-relevant evaluation. The audit is at https://github.com/automl/ucr-provenance-audit.

title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$. The resulting score has mean $(3/2)^d$ for every partition, while its distribution reflects the geometry of the tiling. Comparing two such scores, with the shifts chosen independently, defines a game in which the larger score wins. In dimension $d=4$, we construct a geometric realization of the Steinhaus--Trybuła paradox: three periodic partitions form a cycle in which each beats the next with probability strictly greater than $1/2$. We describe local configurations by finite cube tiling codes and prove that every resulting list of counts is majorized by that of the simple code $C_d=\{0,2\}^d$. Nevertheless, every non-simple code differing from $C_d$ in only two coordinate directions beats it, with a sharp lower bound on the winning margin. We also show that the ratio of wins to losses of $C_d$ has limit superior at most $1$ as the dimension tends to infinity, uniformly over opposing codes. For $4\mathbb{Z}^d$-periodic tilings, changing the window size can repeatedly reverse the winner, but the winning margin eventually stabilizes separately for side lengths $4m+1$ and $4m+3$.

title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
abstract: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. We propose AdaptivePnP, a PnP framework that jointly estimates $σ$ and $γ$ at every iteration from the data-fitting residual. To do so, we apply the PnP virtual model to the data-fitting proximal map and show that the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by $γ$ and $σ$. However, when one parameter is much larger than the other, the residual carries little information about the smaller one and using the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator can degrade the PnP iterations. We therefore introduce the identifiable maximum likelihood (IML) estimator, which restricts the ML estimator to an identifiable window in which the normalized Cramér--Rao bound of every parameter is bounded by a user-specified tolerance. For the virtual model, this window is an interval of ratios $ρ= γ/σ$, so computing the IML estimate reduces to a one-dimensional search over $ρ$. We apply AdaptivePnP to two standard PnP methods, yielding algorithms that require neither a tuned $γ$ nor a known $σ$. On image deblurring and super-resolution, AdaptivePnP matches or outperforms PnP baselines tuned with the true $σ$. Code is available at https://github.com/hdubasullivan/AdaptivePnP.

title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
abstract: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. We operationalise this intuition with (i) controlled summary generation from diverse models; (ii) a LLM evaluator that compares pairs of summaries and emits structured judgments; and (iii) a calibrated aggregation rule that combines supportive evidence while penalising only corroborated contradictions.

title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
abstract: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. These results suggest that the skills CUAs learn on software, such as visual grounding, precise clicking, and exploration, already carry over to embodied tasks, giving CUAs a far broader scope in embodied AI than previously realized. We therefore advocate that computer-use agents can be embodied generalists. Further, we advocate that, by following the training strategy that made computer-use agents general, embodied AI can converge on a single general model as well, ushering in a new era of general embodied AI. Website: https://pranjal2041.github.io/cua-embodied

title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
abstract: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1. The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. The hash-only sender delivered 857 of 1,000 messages on the first attempt and cost 192.8 bits per message, 18.4 bits more than PPM order 1 (95% bootstrap interval 10.9 to 26.3); by the pre-registered rule it spends more and is not equivalent within one byte. As secondary results we map measured sender memory against bits. The hash-only sender (8,190 B on a host build, keyed BLAKE2b tag included, as in every method) was the cheapest point in bits from 8,190 B up to, but excluding, PPM order 1 at 24,844 B, 45 to 46 bits below smaz2 and Unishox2; from PPM order 1 upwards, in-domain senders spend fewer bits, except order 2 pruned to 16 KiB. In airtime it loses to PPM order 1 on all five links priced, to Unishox2 on four, and to raw text with a tag on two, because each failure costs an acknowledgement frame and a fallback frame. A wider receiver search recovers half of the failures and makes the cost 7.7 bits lower than PPM order 1, at about three minutes of receiver time per failure, and still loses in airtime on four of five links. We report the measurement as a delimitation, with every deviation of the run.

title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.

title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
abstract: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. Demographic-class balancing produced relatively small changes in performance, while evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters showed modest attenuation. Under training with diagnosis-based grouping, demographic-associated signals remained detectable across multiple organs, including sex in gastric tissue (AUROC 0.865), age group in breast (0.816), and self-reported race in skin (0.728). Literature-guided analysis of these settings generated candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for further investigation. Together, these findings provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, informing investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning, and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.

title: The AIDA-TNG project: Galactic bar pattern speeds in self-interacting dark matter
abstract: Cosmological simulations within the standard cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm systematically predict higher values of the dimensionless bar-speed parameter, $\boldsymbol{R} \equiv R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ (where $R_{\mathrm{cr}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ denote the corotation radius and the bar radius, respectively), than those inferred from observations of local galaxies, a discrepancy known as the fast-bar tension. Since bar slowdown is primarily driven by dynamical friction with the dark matter halo, bar dynamics is inherently sensitive to the properties of dark matter particles. We aim to determine whether dark matter self-interactions alleviate or exacerbate the fast-bar tension, and to identify the physical mechanism behind the differences in bar dynamics between CDM and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models. We use the $51.7\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ box of the AIDA-TNG cosmological simulations, run with three different dark matter models: standard CDM, and two SIMD models one with a constant cross-section model (SIDM1), and the other with a velocity-dependent model (vSIDM). We identify barred disk galaxies with stellar mass $M_* > 10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshifts $z=0.2,\,1.0,\,1.5,$ and $2.0$, and measure the bar fraction, bar strength, bar length, pattern speed $Ω_{\mathrm{p}}$, and the ratio $\boldsymbol{R}=R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$. The pattern speeds in the SIDM1 and vSIDM models are generally lower than in CDM at nearly all redshifts probed in this study. The subsequent slowdown proceeds with nearly 10\% more effective in the SIDM models likely due to velocity-anisotropy. Consequently, at low redshift the mean value of $\boldsymbol{R}$ is significantly higher in the SIDM models, indicating that the fas-bar tension is further exacerbated in these scenarios.

title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
abstract: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.

title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
abstract: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM and used it for the matching. Our question is whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Improving its accuracy required fusion with a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single shift per ground track, then per observation. For most tracks, the shifts nearly matched those from the airborne LiDAR DTM, likely because DTM errors canceled out across many observations. Per-observation corrections, however, did not match. At a single observation, the error does not cancel out and is too large for the correction. This error likely originates mainly from the input DTM. Therefore, even without a 1 m-resolution DTM, a roughly 10 m-resolution DTM, fused with a global DTM and super-resolved to 1 m, should yield track-wise corrections nearly matching those from a 1 m-resolution DTM.

title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
abstract: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.

title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
abstract: Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. We show that double-plane lenses are sensitive to a specific combination of the mass-sheet components of the two lens planes. Using literature values of the cosmological scaling factor from the double-plane lenses J0946 and AGEL0353, a measurement from the point-source images of J1721 (the ``Einstein zig-zag'' lens), and a reference value of $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, we show the constraints that can be placed on the mass-sheet component of each of these systems. We show that the additional information brought by images of a second source can improve measurements of $H_0$ from individual time-delay lenses by up to $\sim50\%$, depending on certain key assumptions. Using forecasted Euclid and LSST double-plane lens samples, we show that these samples will enable strong constraints on the population of mass sheets in lens galaxies. Such population constraints will have implications for a range of strong-lensing science applications, in particular in constraining $H_0$, dark energy, and the dark matter profiles of galaxies.

title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
abstract: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\fracα{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-ΔS^m = u_0/Γ(1-α)$. Moreover, we show that $t^αu^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $α=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole
abstract: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordström black hole.

title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
abstract: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

title: Finitely Presented Covers of Topological Full Groups
abstract: Commutator subgroups of infinite minimal subshifts provide the first examples of infinite, finitely generated, simple amenable groups. We prove that if $G$ is a finitely presented group which maps onto the commutator subgroup of the topological full group of an infinite minimal subshift, then $G$ contains a non-abelian free subgroup. This in particular implies that these groups are not finitely presented. We also show that the topological full group of an irreducible subshift of finite type contains non-abelian free subgroups.

title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
abstract: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis. In this setting, successful alignment should preserve both the global structure of the target distribution and the instance-level correspondence observed in paired source--target training data. Existing objectives typically address only part of this goal: contrastive losses encourage relative similarity, distribution-matching losses improve marginal agreement, and pointwise regression fits each source sample to its paired target without explicitly modeling target-space path geometry. We propose FlowAlign, a flow-guided target-space alignment method that repurposes conditional flow matching as a training-time alignment signal rather than an inference-time transport model. FlowAlign uses the learned flow field to guide the alignment of source-side representations with the fixed target space, encouraging them to preserve paired correspondence while remaining compatible with the global target-space structure. We further provide theoretical analysis showing how FlowAlign helps improve paired correspondence by controlling endpoint accuracy and capturing local target-space geometry. Experiments on synthetic data, paired single-cell multiome benchmarks, and image--text alignment demonstrate that FlowAlign improves instance level correspondence while preserving target-space structure across different modality settings.

title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
abstract: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations and distill the learned critic into a lightweight grasp utility network that ranks candidate grasps using only the candidate grasp configuration and goal information. At inference time, we select the grasp with the highest predicted downstream utility for the downstream policy to complete the task, before even making a contact. Experiments demonstrate that Grasp-TAGS improves rearrangement success over both fixed single-grasp policies and random grasp selection, achieving an average success rate of 89.84% compared with 79.87% for the best-performing single-grasp policies, an improvement of 9.97 percentage points. Grasp-TAGS also reduces final orientation errors across all evaluated objects. For more qualitative results, refer to the supplementary webpage: https://rpm-lab-umn.github.io/Grasp-TAGS-web-page/

title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
abstract: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory.
