Its inverse is a finite sum acting directly on the possibly rank-jumping body complex. Global acyclicity of the differentiation kernels gives invertible counits that are the identity on the body. Infinitely flat and nongeneric rank-jumping examples illustrate the nonregular theorem. Separately, regular two-term coefficients admit a residue classification and an exact ordinary-quotient descent criterion. Nonzero residue obstructs pullback through any strict map to an ordinary groupoid nerve with represented objects in the stated raw coefficient theory. For regular vertical families over $S\times\mathbb R^2$, we also prove a finite-projective bundle-valued theorem natural under smooth parameter pullback; its two-term invariants are bundle arrows, rather than pointwise rank profiles.

title: Observational signatures of Bardeen black holes under nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: We investigate the shadow and optical appearance of the Bardeen black hole (BH) within nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED). Since photon propagation in nonlinear electromagnetic field can be equivalently described as null-geodesic motion in the effective metric induced by NLED, we derive the corresponding effective optical geometry of the NLED-Bardeen BH. Furthermore, by examining the horizon-photon sphere-shadow inequality, we demonstrate that the NLED-Bardeen BH does not satisfy the complete inequality chain. In addition, we investigate photon dynamics and the corresponding optical images generated by both thin disk and spherical accretion models. Increasing $g/M$ reduces the photon sphere radius and critical impact parameter, resulting in a more compact shadow and an inward shift of the emission peak. For the thin disk accretion model, photon trajectories are classified into direct emission, lensing ring, and photon ring components according to the corresponding impact parameter. We find that Model 1 exhibits three distinct intensity peaks, whereas Models 2 and 3 display two and one peaks. The systematic dependence of these features on the magnetic charge indicates that the NLED-Bardeen BH may exhibit observational signatures distinguishable from those of the Bardeen BH. In static spherical accretion, the intensity peaks near the critical impact parameter because of the enhanced optical path length, while infalling spherical accretion introduces an additional Doppler redshift that suppresses the observed intensity. These results indicate that the shadow size, ring structure, and intensity distribution can serve as potential observational signatures of NLED effects in the strong-field regime.

title: Preconditioned Implicit Midpoint Langevin Sampling for Non-Smooth Bayesian Imaging
abstract: We introduce P-IMLA, a preconditioned implicit-midpoint Langevin sampler for high-dimensional log-concave targets with non-smooth regularization. The obstruction is that the large steps enabled by matrix preconditioning are precisely where preconditioned Euler-Maruyama inflates stationary variance. Implicit midpoint removes this surplus via a Cayley-transform identity, making P-IMLA Gaussian-exact at any step size. Beyond Gaussians, whitening transfers the sharp IMLA contraction rate to $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and backward-error analysis gives drift-only rather than Euler-type diffusion bias under explicit smoothness assumptions. An $M$-norm Moreau envelope yields a proximal non-smooth variant with a three-term error budget. Controlled Gaussian and TV-regularized imaging experiments confirm the predicted separation: the unpreconditioned midpoint scheme retains long transients as $κ_f$ grows, whereas P-IMLA remains $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$-governed and near variance-exact.

title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $μ^3_3$, where $μ_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

title: QCVS: Question-Contrastive Visual Steering for Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: Inference-time steering in vision-language models often entangles query-relevant reasoning dynamics with low-level perceptual noise, causing collateral degradation on correct predictions. We propose Question-Contrastive Visual Steering (QCVS) to isolate task-specific intervention directions via double-differential activation probing. By contrasting spatial layout perturbations under the target query against a generic description reference, QCVS cancels task-agnostic visual artifacts without ground-truth supervision. A dual-threshold gating mechanism then evaluates relative interaction strength and signal amplitude, selectively applying a single bounded hidden-state update only when necessary. Empirical evaluations across multiple scales of Qwen3.5 (2B to 9B) and DeepSeek-VL2 on DynaMath and We-Math demonstrate that QCVS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy gains under sparse coverage (approximately 22%-30%). Crucially, QCVS yields repair rates up to 13.98% while suppressing collateral damage down to 0.41%, proving high intervention precision and computational efficiency.

title: Stable Configurations of Dark Energy Stars in f(R,L_m,T) Gravity
abstract: In the context of $f(R,L_m,T)$ gravity, two analytical solutions are proposed in this study, representing the structure of compact spherical objects whose behavior is dominated by dark energy fluid parameters. The extended field equations are derived using a static interior spacetime under the considered model which characterize a geometric structure including both dark energy and ordinary matter. The field equations are solved using the connections between dark energy with conventional matter, which are governed by different equations of state. This analysis further employs the Kohler-Chao-Tikekar and Durgapal-Fluoria spacetimes as two distinct ansatzes to close the system of field equations, resulting in two independent solutions. For both solutions, the constants are fixed by matching the interior and exterior spacetimes at the boundary using junction conditions. This study also assesses the proposed models using data from SAX J1808.4-3658, and explore the implications of varying the parametric values within the standard modified framework. The analysis concludes that both models fulfil the necessary physical conditions to ensure their candidacy for realistic stellar structures.

title: Zeroth law of black hole mechanics in general Horndeski theories
abstract: We investigate the validity of the zeroth law in the general class of scalar-tensor theories with second-order field equations, namely Horndeski theories or generalized Galileon theories in four-dimensional spacetime. Assuming that the non-minimally coupled scalar field inherits the spacetime symmetries, we show that the horizon mixed projection of the field equations implies constant surface gravity on a stationary Killing horizon. Our analysis incorporates the most generic non-minimal scalar couplings permitted within the Horndeski framework, which we consider as a perturbative expansion about general relativity. Our results therefore classify the possible cases within this framework of proof for different classes of scalar-tensor theories, including shift-symmetric scalar fields. These results extend the applicability of black hole mechanics beyond Einstein gravity and provide further evidence for the thermodynamic consistency of general Horndeski theories.

title: Rigidity of spacelike graphs in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes via the infinity-Laplacian
abstract: In the search for new characterizations of spacelike slices in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes, we introduce a new approach. The main tool for addressing this question is the infty-Laplacian with respect to the Riemannian metric induced on the spacelike hypersurface, together with a Liouville-type property for the infinity-Laplacian on any complete Riemannian manifold by Araujo, Mari and Pessoa in 2021. Starting from the infinity-Laplacian of the height function of a spacelike hypersurface, we derive several differential equations involving the infinity-Laplacian of suitable compositions of the height function, namely, the warping function f(h), its primitive P=\int f, and the logarithmic composition log(f(h)). Under some natural assumptions, including timelike and null energy conditions, global rigidity results are established in the parametric setting. Some of these results specialize naturally to complete spacelike hypersurfaces in the Steady State spacetime and in Einstein-de Sitter spacetime. Finally, we consider a second-order PDE involving the infty-Laplacian and study the uniqueness of its entire solutions on the fiber of the generalized Robertson-Walker spacetime. This leads to new Calabi-Bernstein-type uniqueness results in the non-parametric setting.

title: One-Particle Equivalence of Lorentz-Violating and Lorentz-Deformed Theories
abstract: Planck-scale departures from special relativity are commonly described by theories that break Lorentz symmetry and theories in which such symmetry is deformed. We prove that, under a global shell-linearizability condition, these two descriptions are physically equivalent for a single particle, corresponding to unitarily equivalent realizations of the same Wigner orbit expressed in different momentum coordinates. This equivalence breaks down for multiparticle systems, except when the momentum-composition law can be reduced to the ordinary addition of momenta. Our results imply that the distinction between Lorentz violating and Lorentz-deformed kinematics can only be tested by genuine multiparticle observables. We discuss Compton edge measurements as a prototype example of such a multiparticle probe.

title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) perform strongly in face recognition (FR), yet their fixed-depth inference limits deployment in resource-constrained settings. We propose SD-ViT, a training framework that gives a usable exit at every block depth by making every depth produce discriminative embeddings, for budget-selected fixed-depth exits. Standard ViTs supervise intermediate layers only through backpropagation, so their intermediate representations are not directly optimized to form usable identity embeddings. SD-ViT adds a stochastic auxiliary signal: at each iteration a randomly selected intermediate block is passed through the same embedding head as the final layer and trained with a weighted margin-penalty softmax loss. The objective is thus stochastically sampled deep supervision through a shared classifier. Because both loss terms share that head and classifier, intermediate tokens are trained to map into the same embedding space as final-layer tokens. This matters for FR, where matching is by similarity: a probe processed at an early exit can be compared directly against full-depth gallery embeddings, with no gallery recomputation or adaptation layers. On established benchmarks, SD-ViT stays within 0.4 IJB-C points of the same backbone trained conventionally at full depth, while its early-exit probes recover over 96% of their own full-depth performance at 50% of the computational cost without modifying the reference gallery. A single verification threshold calibrated at full depth remains usable from quarter depth onward.

title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
abstract: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.

title: Prestatability in the Macroscopic Limit
abstract: We examine whether the variables required for a future macroscopic description of a given physical system can themselves be stated in advance. Representing macroscopic descriptions as coarse-grainings of a fixed microscopic phase space, we distinguish formal prestatability, concerning the existence of an effective complete vocabulary of admissible macroscopic distinctions, from dynamical prestatability, concerning whether the future relevance of those distinctions is decidable. Both obstructions disappear for finite microscopic state spaces. In the infinite limit, exhaustive formal prestatability can fail, while a restricted predictive architecture may remain formally pre-statable. We construct such an architecture and show that, under universal dynamics, the future relevance of a candidate variable is equivalent to the halting problem. Thus a fixed microscopic phase space can support macroscopic descriptions whose future variables are not fully pre-statable.

title: Peer Memory Changes Who LLM Agents Consult Without a Detected Gain in Answer Accuracy
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems often reuse the same agents across tasks, creating an opportunity to draw on past interactions when deciding whom to consult. We study this form of memory with PeerMem, which saves MACE's LinUCB state and reuses it when the same agents return. Using six agents, a fixed set of 80 HotpotQA questions, and 12 paired lineages per model, we compare cold, warm, and shuffled initialization in an answer-exchange protocol with reference-answer feedback. Under stable evidence access, warm memory lowers pooled hindsight regret and increases consultation of other evidence holders on Qwen3-32B and Gemma-4-31B-it, while final token F1 differences remain uncertain. Qwen interaction traces further show that warm agents more often encounter peer answers that score above their own prior answers. We extend the evaluation to Qwen3.5-9B using freshly learned memory to compare warm and cold initialization under reassigned and paired stable roles. The primary changed-minus-stable final-F1 interaction is -1.38 points, with a 95% interval of [-3.50,+0.73]. Together, these experiments trace the effects of peer memory through consultation, answer revision, and final task performance.

title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
abstract: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, $N$, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with $N$, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in $N$ for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches $95\%$ of that of the same number of independent pores. $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$ scales linearly with pore diameter $d$, and grows with $N$ as $\sim\log N$ for linear arrays and $\sim\sqrt{N}$ for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

title: Federated Lightweight Transformer for Network-Layer Cyberattack Detection in O-RAN
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) improves radio access network flexibility through disaggregation, open interfaces, and programmable RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). However, the same openness and distribution increase the attack surface and make centralized intrusion detection difficult to scale across heterogeneous RAN sites. This paper presents a federated lightweight Transformer framework for privacy-preserving network-layer cyberattack detection in O-RAN. Each participating site trains a compact Transformer locally on temporally ordered network-flow records, while only model parameters are shared with a federated coordinator. To model realistic site heterogeneity, the client datasets are partitioned according to a Dirichlet distribution, resulting in non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) local data. The local detector uses feature projection, positional encoding, multi-head self-attention, feed-forward layers, and temporal pooling to classify five network-layer attack categories: ICMP, Slowloris, SYN, TCP-ACK, and UDP. Experiments on the NetsLab 5G O-RAN intrusion-detection dataset show an overall accuracy of 94.89 % and a macro-F1 score of 81.09 %.

title: Retrieval-Grounded Multi-View Reasoning for Clinically Reliable Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Chest radiograph report generation is hampered by retrieved reports that resemble the current image but are clinically inconsistent with it, and by diagnostic-label imbalance. We present RG-MVR, a retrieval-grounded framework comprising Retrieval-Augmented Evidence Grounding, which combines dense memory summaries with visually gated sparse retrieved evidence; Adaptive Multi-view Evidential Reasoning, which weights image, memory, and retrieved evidence per case; and a Clinical Prompt Learner, which models finding mention separately from positive, negative, or uncertain status. On MIMIC-CXR, RG-MVR achieved a clinical-label F1 of 0.483 and a BLEU-4 of 0.118 (IU X-ray: 0.202 and 0.110). In an exploratory external cohort of 22 examinations, clinical-label agreement declined markedly (F1, 0.071) and unsupported statements remained common, although physicians found fewer unsupported temporal comparisons (9 vs. 20 cases) and device-related statements (7 vs. 15) than with the baseline. Evidence-aware retrieval and structured diagnostic prompting may reduce specific reporting errors, but broader external validation is required.

title: A Systematic Comparison of In-Context Learning Strategies for Peptide Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
abstract: Peptide sequence-property relationships are often highly non-linear, but can be learned with machine learning models and exploited for the design of new materials and bioactive compounds. Various methods based on transformer architectures have become available for molecular property predictions. These foundation models promise straightforward inference and prediction of properties of new materials through in-context learning. Benchmarks of individual model architectures exist, but a systematic comparison of various foundation models against classical baselines on similar datasets is lacking. Here, we provide a systematic evaluation of the predictive performance of various in-context learning strategies. We compare several large language models, tabular foundation models, and typed decision models against an XGBoost baseline. We evaluate predictive performance on binary and multiclass classification tasks on pH-dependent surface activ-ity, IR spectral signatures, self-assembly, and anti-cancer activities. Our results show that ICL is competitive, yet does not significantly outperform classical baselines, and performance varies between models and tasks. Our findings further suggest that language models use both in context examples and knowledge acquired during pretraining to infer properties of unseen samples. This finding indicates that pretrained models can leverage the existing literature for predictions, but may also bias their predictions towards established sequence-property relationships.

title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
abstract: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.

title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions in Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.

title: SurvAD: How Anomalies Survive Diffusion Reconstruction
abstract: Diffusion-based anomaly detectors reconstruct a test image towards normality, yet how much of an anomaly survives, its leak, remains uncharacterized. We show that a first-order deterministic sampler obeys an exact recursion along the anomaly, whose continuous limit is a survival law. The anomaly decays exponentially as the noise falls, at a rate set by the retention $r$, the share the model keeps on the states it visits. Because $r$ depends on the noise level and not on the step count, one measured path predicts the leak of other step counts, samplers and schedules from a nearby start to within a few hundredths, on four diffusion models and real defects. The law also shows that the leak's growth over steps is exposure bias and that normal details obey the same law, so changing the path or the training trades leak for detail error. We introduce SurvAD, which fine-tunes the reconstructor on inference-like starts and fits a comparator that adds evidence to the residual map without suppressing its ranking elsewhere. For under $2\%$ more inference time, SurvAD raises the multi-class pixel average precision (P-AP) of DeCo-Diff from $76.8$ to $80.7$ on MVTec AD and from $57.5$ to $60.0$ on VisA. It matches CostFilter-AD on the same reconstructor with $9\times$ fewer trainable parameters and, under Dinomaly's protocol, exceeds its reported P-AP on Dinomaly on both benchmarks.

title: Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network for Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation
abstract: The segmentation of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential step for computer-aided neuro-oncology, treatment planning and follow-up. While effective encoder-decoder representations are achieved by U-Net and Attention U-Net, the skip sections of the network can generate weak-contrast or noisy responses in the case of heterogeneous boundaries of the tumor. In this paper, we introduce a Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network (QGDL-Net) that can be used for binary tumor segmentation from FLAIR MRI slices. The proposed model is able to predict the slice quality based on contrast and SNR statistics and to fine-tune the encoder features prior to decoding by learnable quality gates. We used the 80:20 train-validation split for experiments with BraTS 2021. QGDL-Net achieved a Dice of 0.9747, IoU of 0.9506, precision of 0.9755, recall of 0.9739, F1 of 0.9747 and accuracy of 0.9982, outperforming U-Net and Attention U-Net. The EigenCAM maps and segmentation overlays provide better tumor localization and interpretable activation around the lesion regions.

title: Standoff chemical identification of harmful aerosols
abstract: Aerosols - solid or liquid particles suspended in air - are an effective means of dispersing chemical warfare agents and toxic pharmaceuticals, posing acute risks to public safety and security. Exposure to aerosol particulate matter in the environment and in industrial settings has also been linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease. In both cases, rapid chemical identification is key to generating early warnings and attributing sources. Established methods chemically identify aerosols only after extracting a sample, while standoff techniques such as lidar classify aerosols only into broad categories. Chemical identification at a distance is hindered by aerosol extinction signatures that are weak, spectrally broad, and obscured by far stronger absorption from ambient gases. Here, we demonstrate time-resolved, standoff chemical differentiation of aerosols with dual-comb spectroscopy and machine learning identification algorithms. The high spectral resolution of dual-comb spectroscopy allows ambient gas absorption to be removed, and the algorithms identify chemicals without knowledge of aerosol size and morphology. We demonstrate identification of aerosolized benzyl fentanyl (a fentanyl simulant) in mixtures with other aerosols in a standoff measurement through ambient H2O, CO2, and CH4. Despite the aerosol producing only subtle, <1% changes in the extinction spectrum across hundreds of wavenumbers, we find the limit of identification to be an order of magnitude below lethal concentrations for a 1 m aerosol cloud. This technique provides a new paradigm for performing rapid chemical speciation of aerosols using their infrared absorption signatures without extractive sampling. Together with advances in chip-based mid-infrared dual-comb spectrometry, we anticipate this technique will enable real-time networks for standoff detection of aerosol emissions and aerosolized chemical threats.
